lessons.title: Separate discovery, identity replay and proof scope

lessons.title: Keep shallow enumeration, deep centres and adaptive coverage distinct

Do not count a known public rank28 point as a fresh candidate gain, time a retrospectively selected winning chart alone, call an in-span finite signature rational dependence, or retry previously completed equivalent boxes as new coverage. Count actual new boxes and independently exposed curves, not merely roster rows. A duplicate-only row is not a fresh failed search. Do not turn the three completed no-gain banks or finite-column admission misses into rank upper bounds, or discard other map lanes globally from this one fixed-bank result.

The completed next-direction benchmark selected factor-free125k: four controls recovered in151.019 CPU seconds versus239.016 for standard dual-map V3, then an alternative-subgroup validation in83.570 versus168.420 seconds. The frozen policy made2164 completed calls on three rank27 follow-ups without a certified gain. Curve90 contributed zero new exposure after all376 maps matched prior coverage. The result is cheaper control recovery, not improved production rank or a general minimization-dominance theorem.

lessons.title: Keep class-relation construction parked unless a new finite experiment clears its gates

Distinguish local/order data, factor-base image, class-group generation and exact 2-rank; measure novel relation rank before widening collection. Define the cubic algebra and specialization before comparing fibres. A fixed word needs a full-word valuation and collision-prime certificate; an adaptive constructor may select a fresh word. A square norm does not preserve a dependency, and a fixed-word obstruction does not constrain an adaptive constructor.

The fixed column-6 word has a genus-at-least-5 valuation obstruction and finitely many rational Selmer specializations, but neither limits alternate words, the soluble 3/17 class, or parameter-dependent constructors. The frozen transfer adapter failed cold positive calibration before strict extraction, so no fresh fibre ran. Missing data remain UNKNOWN.

lessons.title: Keep the root presentation separate from the intrinsic normalization
lessons.when: Reusing the Keller incidence or finite-étale fibre compiler.
lessons.use: For a fixed universal atomic map, retain the normalized compiler and its exact finite inverse algebra. For a presentation-free canonical marked assignment, use UACANFIB1 instead: evaluate the cubic in A, take Tr((3X^2-X)/2), and apply the fixed rank-N selector. Its whole marked fibre is Spec(A), with effective gluing on A^3 plus O^3. UAFILTER1 gives the general invariant finite-fibre selector. UACANVOL1 adds a canonical volume line. Separate this constructed non-atomic receiver from the obstructed old degree-N stable class and the still open atomic canonical problem. UAPARALLEL1 closes arbitrary polynomial profiles in all retained first outputs: every block subset has a polynomial factor even with cycles. UAWEILATOM1 gives exact ground-field stable length from the field-component count of A after the chosen base extension. The one-direction joint theorem remains complete. UAMULTIKER1 extends the exact common kernel C[Z] to every return rank. UABASICTIME1 factors selectors proved to lie in C[Z,t], even for nonlinear time Keller maps and cyclic nilpotent matrices. UAMARKEDDEF1 preserves the complete marked restrictions by vanishing ideals in a retained first output, giving atomic auxiliary maps of every generic degree d>=3 and preserving any prescribed finite-order thickening and canonical receiver deformations which still factor. UARETURNESC1 gives actual non-descended rank-two and full-rank escapes from the old cubic factor; full canonical atomicity still needs a separate proof. UAROOTDAG1 closes arbitrary polynomial corrections in all retained signals and source roots X_i=x_i*q_i: Keller forces the exact self equation and an effective DAG. UAROOTFACT1 gives polynomial order-ideal models and absolute stable atomic block stages even for some genuinely non-descended rank-two selectors. UAROOTSYM1 groups these into equivariant orbit factors; a transitive action on all blocks has complete fixed-target fibre T0^N and cannot give the natural N-label cover. UASELFCTRL1 closes one affine coefficient line with arbitrary own-source polynomial controls, and even rational controls if the WHOLE output map extends polynomially: only retained-signal effective profiles survive. UASELFLAUR1 supplies the exact nonlinear response and reciprocal-Riccati/pole proof. UASELFFORMAL1 provides all-order formal marked deformations and a genuine source denominator as the concrete next integration gate. UANATIVE2GEN1 replaces every finite native list by two unique effective source controls without changing the map. UAAFFINER1 closes all one-block affine-r controls and gives a fixed-size determinant equation for the nonlinear remainder. UASIGFIELD1 identifies stable signal-field normalizers as weighted compiler scalings plus vertical Keller maps. UAETALEGAUGE1 says the marked finite/formal examples are unique source coordinate changes, with necessarily unbounded source degrees in the explicit scalar family. UAQFSAT1 supplies polynomial descent for any dominant quasi-finite affine-space self-map. UANATIVEORBIT1 classifies the full native profile-coordinate orbit: affine Cout, generic affine-pair reducibility and signal-field-respecting stable profile equivalence all give the unique shear ideal (a^5*c^3). Its finite polynomial-r degree reduction closes the whole quadratic sector. UACUBICDESC1 tests an actual old cubic factor by reducing each output to its three fixed field-basis coefficients; no target-degree ansatz is needed. UAPROFFACT1 upgrades the native profile orbit to complete rational factor rigidity: recovery through ANY retained profile forces its unique target shear, by the already imported published HC4MYGL0 line theorem. UARPLANE1 converts the nonnegative-r generic leaf sector to an actual plane completion with Jacobian 1-SY. UAPLANEATOM1 makes every such completion plane-indecomposable and excludes signal-retaining whole factors whose intermediate coordinates also extend across its hyperbola. UARELPLANE1 cancels a plane Keller target whenever the final curve is a closed embedding, with no boundary-extension hypothesis. UASIGFACT1 closes EVERY native signal-retaining whole factorization, including negative Laurent-r sectors. UAINTERSURF1 replaces the former pole gate by the exact generic intermediate surface under arbitrary stabilization mixing: noninvertible target stages require a NON-PLANE fibre with the stated smooth complete-intersection, tangent, curve, unit, divisor and saturation constraints. UAPRIMUNIT1 closes the cofinite etale surface class with primitive source unit. UAUNITFACT1 uses published whole polynomial root closure to make every nonconstant geometric unit primitive and invert the source stage. A proper arbitrary stabilized native intermediate is therefore GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE and non-plane, has arithmetic UFD ring and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre whole signal component. At every chain cut the unit lattice is either full Z or zero, dropping once at the first noninvertible prefix. UALOGVOL1 closes all nonnegative-logarithmic intermediates after a noninvertible source stage, by the actual r^2 whole-volume multiplier and log pullback on boundary resolutions. UAGEOPIC1 then forces NONZERO geometric Picard group for proper native factors, while its retained-field Galois invariant subgroup is ZERO by rational-point-normalized descent. UADANVOL1 excludes every ordinary smooth Danielewski exponent-one surface by a volume period; higher exponents have an explicit regular primitive. UAPLANECHART1 tests the ENTIRE carried line against EVERY open A2 chart: containment in any one inverts the whole target. Formal etaleness still makes all its finite/formal neighborhoods standard. UADANCHART1 exposes exact simultaneous Keller gluing on the classical Danielewski atlas, a JC(2)-level burden, nondividing ruling degrees and multi-root contact constraints. Its sharp beta-integral contact family fails geometric injectivity in every exponent. UAARITHRULING1 turns ANY actually descended affine-line ruling into a finite geometric plane atlas: arithmetic fibres are integral and geometric fibres reduced. A proper native factor would give JC(2) counterexamples and its whole curve must hit two components of one split fibre. UAPRODUCTTOPO1 uses source Euler characteristic1 and pi1=Z^N on actual product leaves to exclude finite proper stages and force a finite-index abelian intermediate subgroup with index dividing source degree. UAORBFIB1 excludes all multiple-fibre patterns over A1 except one fibre or two doubles, with even source degree in the latter case. UAMLFACTOR1 identifies the trivial-geometric-ML branch exactly with target invertibility in the native class. UAAFFDESC1 PROVES uniqueness and descent of every geometric AFFINE-type ruling: center at the rational point, take a nonzero weighted Galois trace in its stable coordinate line, and contract the actual volume to obtain a retained-field additive action.
lessons.avoid: Seeking a primitive generator line naturally, treating a basis choice as canonical descent, using generic monodromy to identify a smaller boundary fibre, or describing the explicitly decomposable filter as atomic. Coordinates and identity stabilization do not erase its actual factors. Do not search larger polynomial degrees in these closed rank-one cubic-return or retained-output coupling classes, or confuse a cyclic dependence graph with the removal of an intermediate field. Do not replace a non-descended Schur matrix by an ordinary time Jacobian without proving descent, or confuse generic covering degree with total coordinate degree. Do not deepen root-only polynomial profile degrees while retaining every first signal, equate ordinary nilpotence with vanishing of all principal minors, or read apparent coefficient-list cycles before effective cancellation. Do not freeze the scalar response at coefficient zero, infer polynomial integration from every finite Keller jet or a full formal series, or treat a rational source-open formula as an entire affine map. Do not add more native indices as independent control channels, infer map-degree bounds from the normal-form indices, treat finite/formal source-coordinate existence as a polynomial family, or confuse sigma composed F with a retained first output. Do not treat nonlinear-r B output or arbitrarily high marked contact as a new stable class: explicit whole polynomial target shears already have both. Do not infer atomicity from a nonzero cubic descent remainder, or replace native polynomial-module membership by the source jets alone. Do not reopen the conditional native degree-greater-than-one after-profile branch: it is now empty. Do not deepen searches for polynomial plane decompositions of the completed native map, apply the Keller line theorem directly to its nonconstant Jacobian, or infer stable full-map atomicity from plane indecomposability. Do not reopen the former intermediate boundary-pole route: it is now closed in the entire signal-retaining class. Do not identify a generic intermediate fibre with A2 without proof, assume abstractly isomorphic source surfaces imply trivial factor degrees, or treat a generic etale formula as a whole polynomial factor. Do not reopen the nonconstant-unit intermediate branch or allow a proper finite-index unit lattice in a whole Keller factor. Do not substitute a generic J_d surface cover for whole power descent, remove the retained node, infer geometric factoriality from arithmetic localization, or claim that a unit-free surface has been excluded. Do not reopen nonnegative-log surfaces, geometrically factorial proper native factors or invariant geometric divisor classes. Do not import the finite torus-domination classification into our nonfinite maps, use the obsolete two-surface log-zero list, or turn an exact primitive into an etale plane pair. Higher-power primitive formulas and lattice models do not construct either arrow. Do not identify the raw singular retained-base spread with an actual whole Keller intermediate. Do not turn standard formal curve neighborhoods into a global plane chart, glue plane automorphisms into a non-plane etale target, or call the classical chart-to-JC(2) reduction new. Do not substitute local contacts for the whole closed embedded curve, or search increasing degrees inside the excluded beta-integral family or low/divisibly reducible ruling sector. Do not replace geometric ruling existence after finite extension by descent to K0, transfer arithmetic UFD across that extension, or accept multiple geometric components with multiplicity>1 in a descended ruling. Do not fill a nonfinite surface completion with finitely many points, infer positive Euler integral from nonnegative sheet loss, or apply product-leaf topology to a changed-signal receiver without proving its actual generic fibre. Do not reopen excluded orbifold patterns or the odd-degree two-double sector. Do not treat a unique or Galois-invariant ruling as an unresolved non-descent escape. Do not leave affine-type Galois permutation as an open escape. Do not infer uniqueness from two arbitrary COMPLETE-type rulings, or average different ruling coordinates without checking the generic fibre: the exact trace control is Gm.
lessons.boundary: The old Tschirnhaus/inertia obstructions retain their architecture and full-degree hypotheses. Non-atomic canonical polynomial-bundle existence is now constructed over all permitted schemes; a naturally trivial bundle, one fixed all-scheme map, atomicity, optimal dimensions and lower generic degree are distinct requirements. Modular low-rank and finite-base restrictions retain their stated scopes. These classifications use characteristic-zero polynomial retained-signal profiles and the named compiler. Any number of controls with rank-one cubic return is closed; non-descended higher-rank return and other compilers are separate. For another auxiliary block rank-one output recovery is equivalent to geometric generic-line connectedness; no general closedness conjecture is silently assumed. Arithmetic atomicity of connected input algebras is not absolute atomicity. Common kernels are proved for all constant ranks; the full selector classification is only one-directional. Higher-rank membership in C[Z,t] is an explicit hypothesis, not a determinant consequence. The full C is not assumed finitely generated or polynomial. Marked divisor identities hold universally; effective degree and absolute atomicity use the stated characteristic-zero field hypotheses. Fixed-signal rank-two source leaves need not be affine planes. A slice does not imply local nilpotence, and stable polynomiality is not an atomicity converse. The root-feedback theorem requires characteristic-zero fields, unchanged first signals and corrections in k[u,sigma,X]. Independent r_i diagonal variables force every principal minor to vanish. Frobenius dependencies and nilpotent coefficient cycles show why positive characteristic and nonreduced bases are excluded. Transitive product-fibre conclusions require transitivity on ALL nonidentity blocks; the trace filter has an extra auxiliary orbit and changes its first signal. Scalar self-feedback rigidity is a one-block affine coefficient-line theorem with a nonzero effective direction in characteristic zero. It permits all own-source channels and rational controls with whole polynomial landing, but says only that EFFECTIVE profiles are retained-signal polynomials; common direction factors may cancel a rational signal control. Curved coefficient families and mutually changing blocks remain outside. Finite-order parameter bases are nonreduced; the formal ring k[P][[lambda]] permits unbounded source degrees and differs from k[[lambda]][P]. The two-control module identity is universal over bases with2 invertible and preserves arbitrary source dependence. Affine-r rigidity and the stable signal-field normalizer use characteristic-zero fields. Affine-r rigidity is a one-block theorem with actual identity parameters and native source jets, not a theorem about mutually changing blocks. Formal-etale source gauges are classical and work over arbitrary nilpotent base ideals; their compatible formal limit can have unbounded source degree. The source-field normalizer leaves a vertical JC(m) problem and does not classify merely retained-output maps or arbitrary coordinate changes moving that field. Formal marked source equivalence permits actual polynomial families with arbitrary generic-degree jumps; it is not a global degree or stable-class invariant. Native orbit rigidity requires characteristic zero, one retained block, polynomial module membership and coordinate operations fixing identity parameters. Its stable equivalence is restricted to source maps normalizing k(u,sigma); unrestricted source changes are outside. A polynomial-r reduction survivor has non-dividing degrees >=2; negative Laurent sectors and genuine cross-block interaction remain open. The fixed dimension-three descent certificate excludes only the old cubic factor when its remainder is nonzero. Quasi-finite saturation is a classical elementary divisor consequence, not a novelty claim. The profile-factor theorem is one block with retained identities and a literal profile first factor; arbitrary source changes remain outside. Plane completion is generic in the signal and covers only nonnegative r powers. Plane indecomposability requires an irreducible Jacobian and an embedded line; its extension to all fields requires GEOMETRIC irreducibility. It does not imply stable whole-map atomicity. A nontrivial signal-retaining factor must have a genuine intermediate boundary pole. Whole-source special-signal landing and signal-moving factors remain open. The saturation overlap has explicit prior public attribution to Trushin Proposition3.1.1. The relative cancellation theorem leaves exactly TWO generic coordinates and requires a whole embedded A1 image; three-dimensional Keller counterexamples show that one curve alone does not invert a higher-dimensional target. It uses only the curve restriction, allowing poles elsewhere. Arbitrary identity stabilization and intermediate mixing are covered by the NON-PLANE generic intermediate-fibre obstruction. This is still a necessary all-factor condition, not full absolute stable atomicity. Intermediate surfaces satisfy BOTH saturation identities, geometrically have unit rank at most1 and their etale arrows miss at most finitely many points. Their abstract shape, smoothness and tangent triviality do not construct a proper factor. Primitive-unit surface rigidity requires characteristic zero, an AFFINE smooth target, cofinite etale image and the actual node. Its whole-factor unit theorem covers arbitrary last outputs with the fixed retained signal, without native jets or Laurent-degree bounds. Proper intermediates have CONSTANT geometric units; the earlier unit-rank-at-most-one route is now CLOSED on the nonconstant side. Whole constant-level irreducibility is not a statement about all further fibres after fixing E_u. Arithmetic UFD over k(u,a) does not prove geometric factoriality. The native NON-PLANE conclusion still requires the UARELPLANE1 embedded-curve witness. The one-way unit drop bounds no later unit-free chain length. CURRENT: a PROPER native intermediate is GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE, has log kappa=-infinity, and has NONZERO geometric Picard group with ZERO retained-field Galois invariants, despite arithmetic UFD. The Picard factor criterion uses the native curve witness and explicitly imported Miyanishi negative-log affine-plane criterion. The log dichotomy and invariant-class vanishing cover every actual whole retained-signal Keller map. Higher-power Danielewski surfaces m>=2 pass exact volume; u has no Keller mate for all m>=1. Required arrows, free tangent frame, global polynomial lift and canonical marks/gluing remain unconstructed. The raw spread a=z^d-u^m*v is excluded globally by its critical zero fibre; only another smooth whole model could realize the same generic surface. CURRENT CHART GATE: the WHOLE carried A1 crosses the boundary of EVERY plane chart in a proper native factor, despite all finite/formal neighborhoods being standard. Any non-plane etale target containing an open A2 yields JC(2) counterexamples on all charts; this remains CONDITIONAL and has Dubouloz2009 precedent. Higher-power Danielewski targets need compatible nonautomorphic pairs surviving at nondividing ruling degrees>=2 and a carried closed embedding meeting two root components with deg Z>=m*N-r+1. Sharp beta-integral contact maps fail geometric injectivity for EVERY m>=2; other multi-root embedded curves remain open. These deductions retain the actual native/witness two-dimensional fibre and entire-curve hypotheses. CURRENT RULING/TOPOLOGY GATE: a retained-field ruling has base A1, integral arithmetic fibres and reduced geometric fibres, hence a finite geometric A2 atlas and a JC(2) burden for proper native targets. Geometric ruling existence does NOT prove descent. The whole carried curve hits two components of some split fibre. On an ACTUAL U^N times A^h leaf both proper arrows are NONFINITE and intermediate pi1 has an abelian subgroup with index DIVIDING source degree. This is virtually cyclic for one block. Multiple fibres of any surjective connected-generic geometric map to A1 are limited to one or two doubles; the two-double case requires EVEN source degree. No silent product hypothesis for the trace receiver or Euler-integral positivity is permitted. Published Galois-invariant/unique-ruling descent already closes that special descent uncertainty: a proper native factor with such a ruling would disprove JC(2). Conditional on JC(2), every geometric ruling must have a NONTRIVIAL Galois orbit of inequivalent rulings. CURRENT DESCENT RESULT: every geometric affine-type ruling of a proper native intermediate is unique and actually descends; its additive action descends too. Conditional on JC(2), only ADDITIVELY RIGID intermediates with COMPLETE-type Galois-permuted P1 rulings remain. Their descent is OPEN. A zero Picard orbit norm does not identify the individual fibrations.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual atomic canonical receiver has compatible complete fibres and effective gluing, or a sharper obstruction rules out its specified architecture; alternatively a smaller degree/dimension construction is proved. An actual candidate leaves the rank-one cubic architecture, for example through non-descended higher-rank return geometry, another compiler or a non-locally-nilpotent auxiliary with constants outside the stable-polynomial criterion, satisfies its whole-source determinant identity, retains the exact complete fibre and gluing, and proves absolute atomicity. In one constant direction, an auxiliary-only canonical escape must be all-inactive and demonstrate a full constant ring outside the stable-polynomial criterion, retaining exact marked fibre and descent. For root feedback, an atomic candidate must leave the all-signal-retaining polynomial root subring class, for example using additional source channels or a changed first output, and still prove the complete marked fibre and atomicity. A proved broader curved/multi-direction or genuine cross-block construction removes the explicit formal scalar denominator on the WHOLE source, retains complete marks and gluing, and proves full-map absolute atomicity. Scalar-line degree sweeps are closed. A two-effective-control native family leaves the scalar-line and affine-r sectors through nonlinear Laurent-r dependence, or another first-output/compiler/cross-block architecture, and proves whole-source polynomial landing, exact canonical marks, gluing and full-map atomicity. A native candidate has Cout genuinely nonlinear, escapes generic profile-coordinate reduction at a non-dividing polynomial-r degree pair or in a negative Laurent sector, and proves the full marked scheme, effective gluing and absence of ALL actual polynomial factors; another compiler or changed first-output architecture remains permitted. A whole-source native construction has genuinely nonlinear Cout and exact canonical marks/gluing; any claimed factor must escape literal profile recovery and, in the polynomial-r sector, polynomial intermediate extension. A genuinely non-plane generic intermediate surface with the exact saturated field model and whole-source realization, a new curve-witness failure or another compiler must be analyzed without assuming JC(2). A proper factor realizes a NON-PLANE geometric generic retained fibre, both field degrees exceed one, and all curve, unit, saturation, divisor and whole-polynomial requirements are certified; or an actual native integration preserves complete canonical marks/gluing and excludes every such factor. A proper generic surface is geometrically unit-free with the exact arithmetic factorial ring, saturated embedded field, whole carried curve and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre intermediate signal; both whole degrees exceed one and the entire map/global marked gluing is certified. Nonconstant-unit and finite-index unit candidates are closed. Produce an actual negative-log unit-free geometrically nonfactorial intermediate with nonzero Picard group and no invariant class, the exact canonical volume and both etale arrows. The u^m*v=z^d-a families with m>=2 are explicit necessary-condition models, not permission for a bounded coefficient sweep or proof of a whole factor. Supply an actual compatible nonautomorphic Keller atlas and a WHOLE multi-root embedded line satisfying all contacts, both cofinite arrows and a different smooth whole spread, or move to a proved intermediate geometry without such a plane chart. Finite/formal neighborhoods and exact primitives alone are insufficient; JC(2) and canonical atomicity are not declared solved. Prove a compatible JC(2)-counterexample atlas in the descended-ruling class, or prove an actual failure of ruling descent retaining all field, curve, volume and whole-source constraints. Respect the nonfinite source-divisor and sheet-loss budget, the dividing-index group constraint and the orbifold multiplicity/parity gates. Full canonical marks, gluing and absolute stable atomicity remain necessary. Prove descent or exclude actual realization of the remaining COMPLETE-type Galois orbit. The affine-type descent subproblem is closed; extend by a new identification argument, not more necessary conditions.

lessons.title: Prove polynomiality and the determinant balance together
lessons.when: Constructing a boundary-cancelled or weighted suspension.
lessons.use: Use an explicit source–core–target valuation ledger, record divisibility at each boundary and verify the complete determinant product.
lessons.avoid: Treating formal pole cancellation or a rational coordinate identity as proof of a polynomial Keller map.
lessons.boundary: The chosen reconstruction open and divisor multiplicities are part of the construction. A relative or marked invariant is not automatically an unrestricted stable invariant.
lessons.reopen_when: A different ansatz supplies its own polynomiality and boundary-exhaustion certificates.

lessons.title: Exploit branch-value interpolation before nonlinear elimination
lessons.when: An RR pencil has rational double-branch values on known fibres.
lessons.use: Interpolate the branch line, divide by the product of the branch parameters and inspect forced denominator squares and recurrence structure.
lessons.avoid: Starting a generic Groebner or full coefficient solve before checking whether the marked data determine a linear interpolation problem.
lessons.boundary: The interpolated candidate still needs literal equation, marking, denominator and section checks; interpolation alone does not certify the endpoint.
lessons.reopen_when: The rational branch-value assumptions hold on the selected physical chart.

lessons.title: Record the degree of every quartic point map
lessons.when: Transporting sections through a binary-quartic Jacobian or covariant map.
lessons.use: Annotate the map degree and compare exact group-law images and heights before claiming a new section or saturation index.
lessons.avoid: Missing that a covariant transported 2P rather than P, thereby multiplying heights by four and creating a false rank/glue interpretation.
lessons.boundary: A rational point map and an isomorphism of pointed elliptic models are different certificate types.
lessons.reopen_when: The map degree, chosen origin and exact section identity are all established.

lessons.title: Optimize the measured dominant phase
lessons.when: Proposing a runtime improvement or comparing two research runners.
lessons.use: Separate worker startup, map construction, landscape/CVP, admission, point search and replay. Use retained ordered receipts and compare like inputs and verification work.
lessons.avoid: Reporting a component speedup as a whole-run improvement, or calling inherited landscape verification equivalent work to rebuilding it.
lessons.boundary: In the seven recorded future-V3 searches, point work accounts for roughly84–88% of wall time; eliminating all other work only yields the stated roughly1.14–1.18x ceiling with point time fixed. Curve52's bounded100-invocation pass took110.055 seconds while its independent full-landscape replay took117.552 seconds, so a shorter search is not necessarily cheaper to verify. These observations are not forecasts for other runs.
lessons.reopen_when: A new profile identifies a different bottleneck or a controlled comparison measures a changed component.

lessons.title: Separate coordinate cost from point-yield selection
lessons.when: Using a coordinate change, model size, or measured chart cost to choose a bounded fibre population.
lessons.use: Freeze deduplicated candidate populations, selection rules and cost measurements before point outcomes. Measure preparation, chart construction and worker cost separately from certified directions, and preserve the exact maps and isomorphism checks for every selected fibre.
lessons.avoid: Treating smaller coefficients as a rank or point-yield predictor, comparing only one component of runtime, or treating all-zero matched arms as equivalence or grounds to enlarge the same population.
lessons.boundary: The fibre-height experiment completed 468 charts on 31 distinct curves. Its smaller models had lower recorded cost but both arms found zero new directions. That is a bounded null result for these selection rules, not a theorem about other coordinates, families, or rank.
lessons.reopen_when: A separately frozen panel supplies compatible positive controls, a changed cost boundary, or a predeclared point-yield endpoint.

lessons.title: Keep beam truncation separate from certified CRT pruning
lessons.when: Using height-ranked CRT prefixes to retain candidate branches.
lessons.use: Record every omitted branch and use exact branch-specific lower bounds only where proved. Preserve the four-prime ordering counterexample as a regression.
lessons.avoid: Treating survival in a finite beam as an exhaustive sieve or assuming the ordering of branches cannot change.
lessons.boundary: A width-one beam ends at height1409 after discarding a branch completing at53. Minimum height is nondecreasing on a fixed branch; that does not preserve the ordering between branches.
lessons.reopen_when: The omitted branches have an independent exact obstruction or the task explicitly accepts a bounded beam.

lessons.title: Reduce fixed constructed covers and compare blind lifting against generic-only V3
lessons.when: Explicit extra Kummer/Selmer classes have fixed genus-one covers but their known rational lifts used a point oracle.
lessons.use: Freeze the classes, give a fresh-context worker only equations, retain all rational transformations, apply established degree4 minimisation/reduction, and exploit a ternary conic to pass to a reduced degree2 model. Independently check the complete coefficient and point transport and finite independence. Compare ordinary V3 from the same generic subgroup, with upstream construction, maps, search and replay costs stated separately.
lessons.avoid: Treating huge expanded coefficients or a degree4 height-box miss as a final search model or obstruction; treating a known-fibre blind recovery as a parameter-selection mechanism; calling the cover-only runtime the end-to-end class-route cost.
lessons.boundary: On MW16-05 at3/17, fixed columns6/7 reduce from2464/1766 to39/44 coefficient bits. Degree4 bounds1000/100000 miss, but conic-to-quartic reduction yields points at1/2 and3/10 at bound1000, independently certifying generic16 plus2. Fresh V3 reaches22 in6 charts and also supplies both exact fixed-class lifts. These are fixed-control results, not a general speed or parameter criterion.
lessons.reopen_when: An equation-derived parameter condition forces the arithmetic block, or a preregistered multi-fibre experiment accounts for class construction and recovery on common backend resources.

lessons.title: Measure point visibility with a blinded known-direction control
lessons.when: Testing whether a bounded chart policy can expose rational directions without claiming a new rank result.
lessons.use: Freeze the curve panel, generic basis, reduced metric, centre list, budgets and worker inputs. Withhold one known generic direction before selection and search; keep its coordinates in a separate oracle. Open that oracle only after every attempt and geometry replay finishes. Count recovery only from an exact rational group relation having a nonzero withheld coefficient.
lessons.avoid: Letting a withheld point, rank label, exceptional-point outcome or a later relation alter selection; calling a literal representative miss a missing direction; or reporting recovered known directions as new rank.
lessons.boundary: The retained ordinary-fibre control recovered all 31 withheld known directions in 372 completed charts, while the unmasked endpoint had zero new quotient gains. This establishes bounded sensitivity under that frozen geometry and exposure only; it does not measure exceptional-point incidence, establish exact rank or validate a selector on an all-new population.
lessons.reopen_when: A new, preregistered curve panel or a changed independent subgroup has a separate blind/oracle binding, exact relation audit and declared endpoint.

lessons.title: Certify a point-supplied generic section from the actual base curve
lessons.when: Using a fixed multi-cover base change to supply an additional generic section.
lessons.use: Write the actual connected base curve, not merely a quotient, and exhibit its rational point. Use good-reduction orders to obtain a torsion annihilator and verify a nonzero annihilator multiple. Then verify the lifted sections and their exact height Gram matrix; a positive Schur complement certifies the added generic direction.
lessons.avoid: Treating a point on a quotient as a point on the full base curve, treating a large Selmer space as a rational lift, or claiming a base generator, saturation, specialized independence or a rank upper bound without the corresponding certificate.
lessons.boundary: The retained V4 diagnostic has a degree-four genus-one base with a non-torsion point and a rank-19 displayed generic subgroup after base change. Its sampled fibres verify supplied points only; it is neither a specialized rank certificate nor a record-search advantage claim.
lessons.reopen_when: The cover equations, base point, inherited subgroup or exact height pairing changes.

lessons.title: Turn a target-conditioned height lattice into an explicit K3 parent
lessons.when: A certified point configuration suggests a generic core but its explicit parent surface is missing.
lessons.use: Recognize the candidate height form, choose a low-degree polarization and solve the line-incidence kernel. Verify both incidences and nonincidences, compile the residual cubic pencil with a rational origin, then measure section rank before proving heights, saturation and the Picard upper bound.
lessons.avoid: Counting displayed sections as independent; treating a matching lattice or equal j-invariant as a literal specialization; repeating the completed Curve302 reconstruction.
lessons.boundary: For Curve302, removing the unique norm-six outlier leaves 400 words for the determinant1092 form. The degree-four O+P+Q polarization supplies fifteen lines; the first seventeen displayed sections have rank fifteen, and two further conics complete rank seventeen. This is inverse construction conditioned on known exceptional points, not a prospective parameter selector.
lessons.reopen_when: A different target has a certified candidate generic core, a realizable low-degree polarization and an unmet geometric construction gate.

lessons.title: Reuse weight modules and prove quotient closure
lessons.when: Exact image membership for the two-slice derivation D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y.
lessons.use: Group expressions by target weight, compute one standard basis of the primitive module per group, then lift each query and verify D(primitive)=expression. Reuse those primitives across ideals. Build the quotient image of ker(D) by closure under u, v and w; require the frontier to become empty.
lessons.avoid: Rebuilding the same module for each seed or treating a finite iteration cap or arbitrary y-degree truncation as kernel-image closure.
lessons.boundary: A membership answer is exact only after the primitive and kernel correction tests succeed. Pure/mixed exponent windows remain bounded experiments. The 128-step guard fails if closure does not stabilize; it is not a completeness bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The derivation, coefficient ring, ideal or target-weight module changes; otherwise reuse the existing compiler and declared inputs.

lessons.title: Apply the principal and plinth-power theorems before searching
lessons.when: Choosing an ideal for the rank-two model LND or reusing its old conductor search queue.
lessons.use: First test whether the ideal contains a power of (u,v), or is nonzero principal. The plinth-power theorem LND-NPF and complete principal theorem LND-CPM give all-order safety. The five historical nonprincipal charts all contain (u,v)^3.
lessons.avoid: Expanding old NPL/PDP/PCD power windows or treating the rational-root ladder as the current end of the principal classification.
lessons.boundary: These theorems concern the stated rank-two derivation and ideal classes. Genuinely nonprincipal ideals outside plinth-power saturation, and different derivations, retain their own obligations.
lessons.reopen_when: An explicitly specified ideal lies outside both completed classes, with an all-order theorem or counterexample target.

lessons.title: Use the lowest valuation face in conductor arguments
lessons.when: Clearing Laurent denominators in the invariant-affine principal LND families.
lessons.use: Pass to the associated graded ring for the relevant prime valuation. The lowest negative face carries the required power of the carrier. Apply pure vanishing at growing moment orders to force positive valuation, which eventually clears every fixed multiplier denominator.
lessons.avoid: Claiming carrier divisibility for every negative Laurent coefficient: u^2*y^3 contains the coefficient w^3/u in the rational-root chart, which is not divisible by q1-w.
lessons.boundary: Theorems 6.8–6.16 use lowest faces and explicitly controlled denominator losses in the model LND. The stronger coefficientwise statement is false and cannot be used as a shortcut.
lessons.reopen_when: A new carrier has a proved associated-graded divisibility statement and a compatible denominator bound.

lessons.title: Keep pointwise equations after cohomological compression
lessons.when: Reducing the cubic or higher Danielewski contraction equations.
lessons.use: Compile the small de Rham flux ledger and leading pencil first, then retain the lowest nonzero coefficients of J-1 for each degree and boundary-pole profile. Use the explicit normalized cubic family in CL25 as a regression against any claim that flux plus leading face is sufficient.
lessons.avoid: Launching the unstructured 90-variable cubic ideal, replacing J=1 by its cohomology class, using opposite signs for P'(i) and P'(-i), or quotienting by automorphisms that do not preserve the chosen degree filtration.
lessons.boundary: The 11 nonconstant flux equations are necessary. The exhibited family satisfies them all but fails J=1; both boundary derivatives equal -2. A degree-bounded quotient needs filtration-preserving transformations.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete chart classification adds the missing pointwise conditions or proves a degree-preserving normal form.

lessons.title: Reuse the finite Rees atlas and finish the surface ledger
lessons.when: Continuing the quartic weighted graph normalization or Hilbert-polynomial calculation.
lessons.use: Start from the three completed side point bases, eight-cone corner atlas and exact side-to-corner packet matches. The next finite calculation records divisor classes, Rees multiplicities, polarization restrictions and normal-bundle degrees of the center curves; apply centerwise Riemann–Roch and the existing endpoint conductor corrections before one global pushout.
lessons.avoid: Repeating ambient normalI runs that produced no certificate, redoing the completed local principalizations, or equating matching conductor colengths with equality of quotient sheaves.
lessons.boundary: The modular graph multidegree and two unknown coefficients alpha/beta remain a calibration. Local normalization and a finite-model Euler-characteristic formula do not prove global normalization, flatness or equinormalization.
lessons.reopen_when: The actual missing surface-intersection or gluing data are supplied, or a changed model invalidates the existing atlas.

lessons.title: Restrict later local rows to the existing kernel
lessons.when: A large RR ambient has a smooth block with a small exact modular kernel.
lessons.use: Match ambient labels and hashes, then restrict actual sparse component rows to the small kernel. Check every rational denominator at the chosen prime and bind the independent smooth-block rank/kernel certificate. Full stacked column rank mod p then certifies the same bounded rank over QQ.
lessons.avoid: Rebuilding a dense stacked matrix, computing node layers after the kernel is already zero, or using a smooth-kernel record from a different pole bound.
lessons.boundary: A surviving modular direction is not a rational pencil. A full-rank minor rejects only the supplied ambient; it gives no exhaustive pole bound. The good-reduction consumer trusts the independently recorded smooth rank/kernel and does not reconstruct that matrix.
lessons.reopen_when: A different, mathematically justified ambient has a compatible smooth-kernel certificate.

lessons.title: Keep product divisibility distinct from a rectangular jet
lessons.when: A resolved normal-crossing chart reduces a global pole condition to Z^a*Y^b divisibility.
lessons.use: Identify the actual principal ideal before forming a quotient. Impose compatible componentwise divisibility and overlap gluing before extracting any finite residual corner. In the recorded node t^17=Z^51*Y^68 times a unit.
lessons.avoid: Replacing the one-dimensional quotient R/(Z^51*Y^68) with the finite length-3468 quotient R/(Z^51,Y^68), or expanding a raw ten-generator ninth-power ideal before clearing chart units.
lessons.boundary: A rectangle and a product impose different conditions. Pareto-leading rows are necessary conditions; equal-leading terms and unit expansions can still interact.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact component/gluing argument identifies a finite residual quotient without changing the ideal.

lessons.title: Bind replay schemas to the exact marked section
lessons.when: An old module or physical-target script is reused after a section-normalization correction.
lessons.use: Use the primitive height-24, degree-ten q8 section and the full R*h*Dy=Ny*Dx normalization. The corrected marking wrapper dispatches the 2cover implementation. The corrected QQ checker reconstructs the section from q6 points and consumes the frozen tracked component-nef target.
lessons.avoid: Renaming the new marking JSON to the old filename, accepting its new status in old consumers, or applying the historical degree-192 branch result to a different chord input.
lessons.boundary: The old consumers require the withdrawn NS-decomposition schema; the finite-module script asserts collision degree 46. Missing q6 Jacobian/zero/E7-section inputs are a recovery gap, not permission to rebuild a campaign or evidence that q8 remains unsolved.
lessons.reopen_when: The original inputs are recovered with matching hashes, or a separately verified schema/marking transport is supplied.

lessons.title: Use factor supports to avoid all pair products
lessons.when: A complete finite set of rational quadratic covers is tested for q_i*q_j=q_k.
lessons.use: First test rational quadratics by primitive integer coefficients and nonsquare discriminant. Distinct irreducible polynomial atoms rule out every nonempty product of distinct listed characters, regardless of rational scalar factors; the compact independent packet verifies all 39,147 alternate11952 and 39,120 hidden103b2 rows. For repeated or two-linear-factor supports, use endpoint/triangle support XORs and retain the full scalar: a rational ratio or product is a square exactly when its sign is positive and its reduced numerator and denominator are integer squares. This needs no integer factorization.
lessons.avoid: Forming hundreds of millions of polynomial pair products, treating repeated polynomial support as an equal extension without a scalar-square test, silently dropping a nonconstant branch denominator, or treating a formal variable rename as transport between two bases.
lessons.boundary: The compact replay verifies branch polynomials and attachment to retained priority words. Completeness of the lattice enumeration, section-lift identities and source-curve base degrees are separate proof components. The old rank-28 and q_103b2 curves have degrees 8 and 9 over alternate11952, so they are not quadratic characters there. The ten-chart smooth layer and rational-normalization genus-one row were also closed later; use their canonical boundaries before another search.
lessons.reopen_when: A new source has actual repeated/two-factor supports or certified new degree-two characters on the same base.

lessons.title: Stream the short shell and retain the quotient
lessons.when: The short-vector list is too large although the finite quotient and one representative per orbit are small.
lessons.use: Use a unimodular LLL basis with an explicit row-coordinate transport, stream Fincke-Pohst leaves, and retain parity masks, multiplicities and canonical representatives. Evaluate every accepted norm exactly and require equality with an independent exact PARI count before asserting completeness. Export representatives in the pinned frame.
lessons.avoid: Materializing nearly three million signed vectors just to recover 39,147 M/2M classes, or confusing LLL column transforms with row-vector coordinates.
lessons.boundary: Floating pruning and a generous guard are not themselves a completeness proof; exact leaf membership, uniqueness of coordinate visits and the matching exact count are essential. Lattice coverage still does not construct branch equations.
lessons.reopen_when: The lattice, norm bound or equivalence relation actually changes; the existing complete frame tables should be reused otherwise.

lessons.title: Use the disjoint graph only for equation cost
lessons.when: Selecting two bisections for a rank-19 biquadratic construction.
lessons.use: Use XOR with norm-four masks to identify all disjoint representatives when that lowers equation cost. Test Galois-character independence by the exact quadratic squareclasses and then use the appropriate lifted height theorem.
lessons.avoid: Using membership in the 8,895,801-pair disjoint graph as a hard filter for independent characters, or restarting its common-cover scan after complete bisection injectivity.
lessons.boundary: All common-cover pairs in the published smooth-bisection frame are excluded. Distinct-character biquadratic rank 19 is a separate construction; both the published pair and the recorded low-complexity pair lie outside the disjoint graph.
lessons.reopen_when: A different geometric objective specifically requires disjoint representatives, or genuinely new quadratic characters are supplied.

lessons.title: Close a failed incidence bank before enlarging a speculative carrier hypothesis
lessons.when: Trying to propagate a frozen exceptional Kummer block into an infinite rank-gain subfamily.
lessons.use: Keep the integral frame, physical zero and I2 component; enumerate signed norm 10/14 vectors with exact LDL arithmetic and label a stopped prefix incomplete. Realize actual curves through the marked trace Riemann--Roch identity and A1 vanishing. Require nonzero rational control splitting, exact cubic-field labels, a normalized fixed-line fibre product, and certified rational infinitude. Count extensions over the fixed t-line with constant squareclasses retained. Translation identifies normalized covers and pairing cannot supply a missing lift. Close a stopped bank before returning to the successful dependency.
lessons.avoid: Do not substitute the rank-16 height matrix for the rank-17 frame; call a lattice vector a curve; identify constant twists or arbitrary base changes; equate a genus-one point with infinitude; or choose generic corrections independently. Soluble strict classes and formula counts do not give rational bisections or independent arithmetic directions. A failure before label matching says nothing about the marked block.
lessons.boundary: The stopped MW16-05 prefix has 182 exact genus-zero bisections with 182 distinct extensions, all nonsplit at 3/17. Their control values are 182 rational squareclasses, without an independence claim. There is no common obstruction at the real place or primes through 1009; 21 fail by sign. Both shells remain incomplete, with 73 split residuals and candidate 171 separate. Translation and pairing cannot repair these incidence misses. No marked rank-18 family or strict/ideal transfer is constructed; the conditional theorem remains valid.
lessons.reopen_when: Only a new theoretical connection from the actual arithmetic dependency to a different carrier hypothesis would justify a separately scoped proposal. This bank is closed; no shell completion, enlargement or interrupted-candidate repair is scheduled.

lessons.title: Cancel the Jacobian of the actual source chart
lessons.when: A primitive-polynomial derivative is used to design a mask suspension.
lessons.use: Compute the chart Jacobian first. In the A4 root algebra, interpolate H^3/(4K^3L) in the four conjugate roots and factor its denominator B^2*rho*sigma. Carry the selected field generator and exact residual divisor through every change of chart.
lessons.avoid: Substituting 1/P'(T) for the required chart reciprocal: the derivative split preserves the four-sheet field but leaves H^6/(2*Theta*K^6*L^3) in the ordinary chart. Do not confuse coefficient gcd in a nonnormal presentation with divisorial cancellation on its normalization.
lessons.boundary: The localized fourfold determinant-one map still has genuine poles. Its existence does not supply a polynomial affine source; the original masks and Hhat continuation are already closed. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. Wright boundary A4 states are not identified with full geometric generic monodromy.
lessons.reopen_when: For local geometry under a separately stated objective: A different chart or coupled source/target construction has a new exact divisor ledger and a field-recovery argument. The affine-space Keller objective requires a substantive failure of KMFI66 or changed hypotheses; a new chart, mask or divisor ledger within its hypotheses cannot reopen it.

lessons.title: Normalize and reject the boundary before reconstructing coordinates
lessons.when: A coarse deletion passes unit, class-group and ampleness screens.
lessons.use: Count actual simple/triple primes on the normalized incidence, then use its seven-curve lattice. Test forced-column content before enumerating completions. The strict B column has content two, excluding every boundary basis containing it. For a surviving split, test indispensable horizontal genera before presenting a coordinate ring.

The lattice rejection is stable under polynomial extension; the separate surface-boundary genus proof is not automatically a universal stable-cancellation theorem. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. lessons.title: Check the conductor before trying a multiple of a boundary prime

At the other quadratic pair the conic is divisorial on one normalization branch and only codimension two on the other; conductor matching forces an extra height-one zero for every positive multiplicity.
lessons.avoid: Treating the A3 local index two as a reason to try doubling, or treating one rational norm factor as a selector whose entire horizontal boundary is rational.
lessons.boundary: KIG25 excludes all positive principal divisors supported only on this conic. It does not exclude other rational-horizontal selectors or a genuinely coupled ideal-contraction construction. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. lessons.title: Compile branch jets and a norm floor before factoring selectors
lessons.when: Searching polynomial masks with prescribed normalized exceptional orders.
lessons.use: Reduce forbidden coefficients of all seven truncated branch jets modulo c^2+27 and solve exact rational linear algebra. Reuse V2,1=0, V2,2=<T^2>, the six-dimensional V3,1 and its root-quadratic extension. The pole-degree leading form gives the sharp norm floor 16 and rules out root-quadratic directions below degree 24.
lessons.avoid: Brute-force coefficient searches below a proved degree floor, or scoring the near-selector J as almost viable because only one branch jet fails. Its first exact correction is linked to Hhat by syzygies and has an absolute genus-31 strict curve.
lessons.boundary: The floor covers total degree at most three and root degree at most two. The higher correction module and other root charts remain open; satisfying all valuation jets does not imply rational boundary. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. Wright boundary A4 states are not identified with full geometric generic monodromy.

The affine-space Keller objective requires a substantive failure of KMFI66 or changed hypotheses; a new chart, mask or divisor ledger within its hypotheses cannot reopen it.

lessons.title: Remove fixed components and use the value-gradient kernel map

Replace the three moving-singularity equations by the value-gradient determinant -54*M^2*D23 and its generic kernel map of degrees 19,18,18. Audit exceptional rank drops of M separately.

Generic integrality and bounded boxes do not settle every degeneration. lessons.title: Search the smaller selector space and retain reduction exceptions
lessons.when: Looking for nonlinear factors of a small linear system over a finite field.
lessons.use: Factor all 3906 points of P5(F5) in the six-dimensional A4 selector space rather than enumerating every projective cubic coefficient vector. Reuse the classified factor list and tangent kernels. For conics, all 3875 degree-two forms have been screened; the exceptional monic-U^2/s0 lift tree dies modulo 625.

Nonlinear rational factors remain possible in the specified structural/degree-drop neighborhoods. The eight H-slice lift levels are bounded evidence. KMFI66, via KIG28, separately closes every A4-preserving affine-space Keller construction; any unresolved selector or chart classification here is local geometry only. The affine-space Keller objective requires a substantive failure of KMFI66 or changed hypotheses; a new chart, mask or divisor ledger within its hypotheses cannot reopen it.

lessons.title: Use independent affine-source rejection gates
lessons.when: An affine modification passes smoothness, factoriality or flexibility tests.
lessons.use: Keep units, class group, ML, Derksen, Hodge/topology and explicit coordinate recognition separate. SL2 passes the early algebraic tests but has class L^3-L and S^3 topology. The smooth rho=h model has class L^3 yet class group Z/2. Exact invariant failures can reject a candidate before a large mixed-incidence solve.
lessons.avoid: Calling matching invariants an affine-space isomorphism, treating a rational/logarithmic determinant-one lift as an ordinary polynomial Keller map, or requiring two modified p,q,r outputs when the retained-block argument only proves at least one.

lessons.title: Reject CAS interpreter errors even after a success marker
lessons.when: A Singular subprocess is used to certify identities, factor lists or a finite census.
lessons.use: Use singular_runner.py for the audited A4, F2 optional bridge and tagged-lift callers: reject interpreter diagnostics and nonempty stderr, require a unique terminal marker, and check expected result markers as complete lines. The many-channel RESULT adapter keeps historical program hashes and timeout records, but discards stdout on interpreter failure so downstream parsers cannot retain an apparent unit or rank.
lessons.avoid: Trusting returncode==0, subprocess check=True, a later PASS substring, or absence of a reported factor. An intentional ERROR followed by PASS exits zero on the locally inspected Singular 4.3.2.
lessons.boundary: The base guard has six small protocol tests and earlier tiny real interpreter controls. The RESULT adapter has four additional tests plus mocked many-channel/tagged integration; no GVC moment, elimination or census was replayed. The 19 many-channel substitutions preserve the AST of all mathematics, generated programs and timeouts. Historical outputs are not fresh guarded executions, and other CAS wrappers remain outside this audit.
lessons.reopen_when: A new interpreter version or output protocol changes diagnostic/completion behavior; cover that behavior with a tiny test before authorizing any research replay.

lessons.title: Calibrate local signatures against known quotient directions
lessons.when: A local Kummer signature rank is proposed as an exceptional-rank or Selmer predictor.
lessons.use: Use the rank-28 control: the generic seventeen and all twenty-eight points both have signature rank 15 in 53 coordinates, despite eleven globally independent quotient directions. At odd p compare known-image rank with v2(c_p*#E_ns(F_p)); equality certifies full local coverage. Keep the p=2 formal group separate.
lessons.avoid: Reading zero incremental local rank as zero global quotient gain, treating a smooth local point as everywhere-local solubility, or treating capped and timed-out lifts as obstructions.
lessons.boundary: Four odd places and infinity are covered; seven odd places and p=2 remain unresolved. The pilot has 60 witnesses and 24 inconclusive tests. Exact public point covers supply residual lower bound 11, but no ambient Selmer upper bound.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete ambient squareclass construction and all local conditions are available, or a different signature is tested against these positive controls.

lessons.title: Record whether visibility predicts or fits a known point
lessons.when: Comparing a multisection atlas against known high-rank fibres.
lessons.use: Freeze the atlas and cost order before targets; record genus, degree, family dimension and incidence codimension. The rigid rational-bisection span ranks are 5,3,2,1, but individually named degree-two generators number 4,0,0,0. All 38 displayed generators admit a genus-one degree-two member fitted after seeing the point, using the common norm-eight trace -P2-P5.
lessons.avoid: Calling a post-hoc moving-pencil interpolation predictive, equating span rank with the number of exposed named generators, or constructing millions of rational trisection equations just to fit already known points.
lessons.boundary: Only degree-two rational curves and the 320 deep norm-26 trisection classes are complete. The norm-20 and degree-four equation sets are samples, and degrees five/six were stopped, not excluded. The quotient is the displayed L_t/M_t, not a saturated full Mordell-Weil group.
lessons.reopen_when: A predeclared pencil gives a genuinely new target, or a target-directed rational multisection solves one of the remaining named-generator obligations.

lessons.title: Eliminate first and retain every good-reduction hypothesis
lessons.when: Seeking a two-node genus-two bisection with rational quadratic normalization.
lessons.use: Use the finite-pole chord M=M0+(l0+l1*u)h^2. In q=(u^2+a*u+b)^2*(c2*u^2+c1*u+c0), eliminate the three c coefficients from the top terms before solving the four essential variables. Intersect full quadratic squareclasses, including scalar characters, at distinct primes. Reconstruct coordinatewise only with compatible trace bases, then factor over QQ and check both section identities.
lessons.avoid: Dropping the scalar squareclass, trusting incompatible chart labels, promoting an empty affine multi-prime intersection to a global theorem, or treating standard CRT reconstruction as an unlimited rational-height search.
lessons.boundary: The recorded primes 17,23,29,31,37 and modulus 13005833 give no accepted candidates in the reconstructed boxes. Infinity, simultaneous bad reduction and larger heights remain open. The separate complete singular genus-one row gives first possible arithmetic genus at least two, not equality.

lessons.title: Reuse exact local lift failures and retain singular branches
lessons.when: Searching for a second anti-invariant section of a direct singleton twist.
lessons.use: For chi=3 and P.O=0, use the exact polynomial box deg X<=6, deg Y<=9. Fix the smooth infinity point, solve lower Y coefficients recursively, then classify tangent rank. Full-rank extra branches admit digit-by-digit exact lift tests. Reuse the 2423 recorded nonlifting certificates and the known-section depth-512 reconstruction control before another shell.

The retained-record auditor checks source/data integrity and coverage without rerunning arithmetic; its per-run digest cache invalidates on file changes.

lessons.title: Check the exact source image before tangent calculations

lessons.title: Separate carrier strata before number-field specialization
lessons.when: Specializing a coefficient system at classified carrier parameters.

Compute double-carrier operators over Q(rho), rho^2-3rho+1=0, using exact quotient-field arithmetic; the defect ratio adds the independent quadratic 27y^2-9y+1 and gives four embeddings of one quartic compositum.

lessons.title: Keep divisibility conditions when factoring an operator

In F2 the coupled obstruction is 294 divisibility jets plus 53 quotient coordinates; the final block is seven target and six Hermite coordinates after earlier endpoint controls.

All residual singleton radial e/f rows and special-direction lengths are now explicit. Original targetA2 node exclusions do not exclude the new radial/strict intersections after target blowup. lessons.when: Monomial compression or weighted channel matching is proposed as an all-order GVC transfer.
lessons.use: Prove both operator-versus-polynomial degree inequalities before replacing a contraction by matched channel counts. The cubic tagged lift forces equality and yields the explicit binomial/factorial channel sum. The weighted quartic plane instead admits unequal selections of equal weight; use its full moment equations. Keep the odd-only prime decomposition as a regression face when restoring even endpoints.

lessons.title: Choose elimination pivots by downstream expansion cost
lessons.when: A multi-channel moment system has several linear pivots or a fixed rational direction slice.
lessons.use: Reuse the recorded term counts before compiling another system. For the nested degree-ten boundary, the a3 pivot gives 648/7340/15300 terms versus 958/6173/34782 for a2, so the slightly larger middle equation buys a much smaller next one. On a fixed rational cross-ratio slice compile with the numeric Gram matrix before expansion.

lessons.title: Factor and rechart localization before retrying a large saturation
lessons.when: A product saturation times out on the coherent degree-ten boundary.
lessons.use: Reuse the cutoff-three factor-by-factor result: only a1 divides the original principal generator; after setting a1=1 every localization factor is coprime. At cutoff four use the recorded residual-intersection minors and solved linear D restriction to identify where growth and thickness occur.

lessons.title: Use the next moment to close a thick fibre before building its ambient colon
lessons.when: A moment ideal has a thick normal component and further equations are available.
lessons.use: On the degree-ten nested chart, solve D=C*a0+R with C invertible and use cleared restrictions. Cutoff-four normal lengths 12 and 18 are already classified. At moment five the second restriction is a unit times e^20 and the third is a unit modulo e, where e=lam-mu. A finite geometric-series inverse closes the entire D=0 fibre, including the exceptional branch.
lessons.avoid: Rebuilding a large ambient cutoff-four colon to reclose the D fibre, or replacing the finite inverse proof with a common-polynomial-gcd claim. The retained 600/900-second runs are diagnostics.
lessons.boundary: The closure holds on the declared localization. Residual D!=0, main A*B!=0 and omitted pivot/projective faces remain unresolved. Filenames ending modular3 can contain cutoff-four data; read max_order and field labels.

lessons.title: Compute all source-degree cutoffs with one incremental echelon
lessons.when: The same tangent space is tested at many degree cutoffs for its unique source trivializer.
lessons.use: Construct the tangent basis and coefficient rows of adj(DF)G once, group the rows by source degree, then insert them in descending degree order. Rank above each cutoff gives the whole filtered profile without solving a new tangent system. Reuse the retained p=32003 profiles and CSK1 exact rational seed degrees.
lessons.avoid: Reconstructing the tangent matrix for each cutoff or redoing the rational seed gauges as if they were only modular observations.
lessons.boundary: The full cutoffs 33/48/63 remain single-prime results. Source-only first-order degree is not the optimal two-sided filtration, and finite exhaustion does not erase stable moduli or prove algebraization.
lessons.reopen_when: A characteristic-zero full-profile certificate, a new coefficient box or a precisely defined two-sided filtration is in scope.

lessons.title: Keep lower-order kernel choices in higher deformation obstructions
lessons.when: A greedy formal lift fails, or quadratic and cubic homogeneous layers are passed to a component calculation.
lessons.use: Retain the lower-order free kernel parameters when formulating the next obstruction. Use the known seed family as a positive control. The quartic generic compiler already records 22 normal quadrics and 305 cubic equations; its 327-generator homogeneous-layer input is retained, together with the failed primary-decomposition attempt.
lessons.avoid: Calling a fourth-order failure of one chosen correction a universal obstruction, identifying the layer ideal with the completed local ideal, or interpreting transverse tangent excess as proof of embedded nilpotents.
lessons.boundary: A reduced family need not be a component; excess tangent dimension can come from thickness, other branches or both. The 12 GB failed standard-basis run produced no radical or primary decomposition.

lessons.title: Read terminal stopping reasons before treating unused adaptive capacity as work
lessons.when: A historical runbook calls a campaign active or quotes its maximum possible box count.
lessons.use: Use the existing terminal reporter on retained checkpoints. The record-scale cohort completed all48 curves at2352 certified boxes with zero gains; every initial no-gain wave stopped its curve. The32/8/8 score strata are fully reported. Bind roster, wave proofs, stopping reasons and completed exposure before interpreting a comparison.
lessons.avoid: Restarting a completed cohort to fill its11760-box adaptive maximum, treating a RUNNING snapshot as live state, or rebuilding the million-parameter intake to learn a retained outcome.
lessons.boundary: A completed no-gain detector result is a bounded miss. It establishes neither an upper rank bound nor score equivalence. Reporter hash checks reuse prior certificates; they are not a fresh independent arithmetic replay.
lessons.reopen_when: A different detector or population has a separately declared hypothesis, finite budget and proof plan.

lessons.title: Preserve frozen assignments while separating changed coordinate measurements
lessons.when: A historical protocol source hash differs after an explicit backend amendment.
lessons.use: Audit population, assignment, context and budgets unchanged; permit only declared source replacements whose historical bytes match the pinned revision. Keep raw and amended-runtime checkpoints separate. The rescue audit verifies the2239 assignments and historical66 clean zeros without Sage, while reporting current readiness as NOT_CERTIFIED. Preserve the exact301-class rescue set and its separate specialized reranking. The CRT half-lattice worker likewise writes a separate pointed-runtime ledger; its frozen v3 analyzer still requires the original v3 ledger.
lessons.avoid: Overwriting a frozen protocol to make its old builder --check pass, merging raw boxes into changed coordinate boxes, treating12 assigned historical zeros as12 compatible current inputs, or reconstructing absent base chunks during cleanup.
lessons.boundary: No rescue chart has run. The current worker recomputes the complete generic parity census rather than loading a persisted table. Assignment without outcome inputs does not erase that the protocol was frozen after the base checkpoint was known.

lessons.title: Normalize each local divisor before discarding a prime
lessons.when: An RR fake-Kummer panel rejects a place because one evaluation is nonunit or its basepoint has negative valuation.
lessons.use: Normalize the sextic and each divisor separately by rational prime powers. Omit only nonunit divisors; for negative basepoint valuation use the scalar-equivalent anchor1-T/T0. This recovered152 previously skipped pairs without new primes or points. At certified good reduction, compare the attained rank with the complete local dimension and independently check the fake kernel.
lessons.avoid: Requiring every inherited generator to be a unit, discarding a whole prime unnecessarily, or calling failure of this model reduction test intrinsic bad reduction.
lessons.boundary: The frozen panel closes553/640 pairs. The83 failed reduction tests and four anchor cases remain unresolved. Rational-scalar normalization is justified in the stated fake squareclass quotient; its true-image conclusion also uses the proved kernel statement.
lessons.reopen_when: An unresolved anchor or reduction case has a certified alternative local model, with the same class maps and completeness checks.

lessons.title: Reuse complete local images without collapsing the remaining global problem
lessons.when: A proposed RR incidence detector asks for classes outside the inherited image at an already certified place.
lessons.use: Reuse the553 complete good-prime images and all ten real and2-adic images: the inherited subgroup spans each. Preserve true/fake kernel data. A global comparison still needs simultaneous compatibility in a complete supported squareclass space, including unramified class contributions; the inherited combination can differ from place to place.
lessons.avoid: Searching for an outside-inherited class at a place already proved fully spanned, identifying local proxies with the original global fields, or replacing global completeness with trial-prime support or known rational classes. Do not identify this inherited-subgroup membership obstruction with a Sha obstruction, or treat failed feature transfer as proof that cohomology explains amplification.
lessons.boundary: The known rational Kummer dimension is18. A certified full Selmer dimension18 would give exact Jacobian rank18 and zero Sha[2]; a larger dimension is not automatically Sha. Prepared equation replay does not prove any local image or global Selmer group. Both frozen cases09/08 already have the simultaneous binary obstruction: individual blocks are soluble, but stacked inherited/augmented ranks are16/17. Both known true rational images have dimension18. Equal full Selmer dimensions alone would not establish differing realization; that inference also needs certified ranks. Subspace position requires specified arithmetic structure, and a full CT radical may contain divisible Sha.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete global algorithm or a new unresolved-place certificate supplies an obligation beyond the already closed local panels.

lessons.title: Test proposal recall and actual integral subgroup identity before tuning scores
lessons.when: A low-height or common-cover lattice candidate is proposed as a recovered generic family.
lessons.use: Check the full proposal ledger against the frozen masked control. The two generators peak at rank12 intersections8 and10; the second comparison covers all1928 rank12 proposals, so rescoring cannot recover an absent space. Keep the successful older graph-consensus primitive closure and its index2048 actual subgroup separate. Use Curve302's completed alternative MW17 parent for construction recovery.
lessons.avoid: Promoting a containing higher-rank space to exact recovery, recognizing Fermigier from index2^11 alone, or rerunning failed proposal generators to rediscover Curve302's already proved parent.
lessons.boundary: Any independent rank-r set in one nonzero parity class forces index divisible by2^(r-1) in its primitive closure. A projected Schur quotient is not an exact integral orthogonal complement. Neither rounded heights nor bounded proposal failure proves nonexistence.
lessons.reopen_when: A new generator passes a declared control at the exact requested rank and actual integral subgroup, with a separate geometric reconstruction proof.

lessons.title: Batch coset norms and sieve exact membership while preserving relation content
lessons.when: A fixed lattice proposal searches many shifted representatives or tests a large pool against candidate spaces.
lessons.use: Precompute shifts and their norms, then evaluate each coset with q(c+s)=q(s)+2s^T Hc+q(c) and stable ordering. Reuse an exact integer kernel: mod1009 matrix products reject nonmembers before exact integer products on survivors. Keep unit relations v_i plus or minus v_j equals v_k literal; dividing content would turn a+b=2c into a false unit edge.
lessons.avoid: Repeating full norm/rank calculations for every representative, treating the support-at-most-two shifted box as complete CVP, or using bounded qfminim's second field as the minimum.
lessons.boundary: The search explicitly minimizes returned norms. Agreement of80- and100-digit height balls is numerical evidence, not an interval-certified cutoff. verify_low_height_mw_sublattices --check rebuilds balls, minima and finite reductions; it is not a cheap metadata check.
lessons.reopen_when: The exact basis or proposal domain changes, or a new completeness claim requires certified numerical bounds and an appropriately scoped replay.

lessons.title: Keep section labels and ordinate branches fixed before stacking fibres
lessons.when: Finite reductions from several parameter values are stacked to prove generic independence.
lessons.use: Use one source-root permutation and exact rational-function ordinate branches. The Mestre adapter preserves both. The corrected13 probes have rank11; the old sorted-root and positive-square-root probes still have matrix rank13 but do not specialize one common coefficient relation.
lessons.avoid: Sorting section columns independently at each fibre, choosing square-root signs numerically, or treating tests that reproduce the old matrix as a valid generic proof.
lessons.boundary: A fixed coherent matrix of full column rank plus torsion exclusion proves the stated lower bound. Rank defects alone give neither dependence nor an upper bound. The rejected entry point now fails rather than emitting a false conclusion.
lessons.reopen_when: A fixed labelled section list has a new exact certificate for the stronger claimed rank.

lessons.title: Prove recursive section identities using explicit degree bounds
lessons.when: Expanded Mestre two-section residuals would create tens or hundreds of thousands of terms.
lessons.use: Keep the monic-square and triangular ordinate recursions. Bound the numerator degree after the declared denominator clearing, then check more distinct admissible exact values than that degree. The Fermigier component uses1141 values for bound1140; the diameter235 component uses1099 for bound1080. Retain excluded poles and the leading-square condition.
lessons.avoid: Treating a Hensel or Pade fit alone as a global identity, expanding residuals unnecessarily, or dropping D=w^2 after projecting to abscissa equations.
lessons.boundary: An identity proves an incidence component, not independence of its sections. Jacobian rank and finite jets do not settle the full component without the later exact argument.
lessons.reopen_when: A changed parameterization comes with a new denominator and degree proof.

lessons.title: Separate parameter aliases and nonminimal factors from source discrepancies
lessons.when: A Fermigier specialization or raw quartic discriminant appears to give a different family or bad-fibre pattern.
lessons.use: Reuse the exact adapter u=s/2 and retained coefficients. For Y^2=X^3-27IX-27J the raw discriminant scale is(607392u)^12, since c4_raw=1296I. The twelfth-power scalar and u factor are coordinate artifacts. The exact generic arithmetic rank12 is already proved separately.
lessons.avoid: Reusing the stale202464 scale, counting literal s and adapter u as unrelated candidates, or treating completed rank computations as a resolution of the paper convention.
lessons.boundary: Literal printed shift19754/39 and reconstruction shift39508/39 give different j-invariants; the source factor-two discrepancy remains unresolved. Benchmark GP conductor calls are not metadata checks.
lessons.reopen_when: Primary-source provenance explains the convention, or an explicit new coordinate map is proved.

lessons.title: Recover an unlabeled subgroup through exact relation components
lessons.when: Comparing high-rank specializations when the intended generic subgroup, section labels and source surface are not supplied.
