lessons.when: A known independent point basis will be removed from a 2-Selmer computation or relative-cover construction.
lessons.use: Pin the model, points and 2-division cubic; prove trivial rational 2-torsion; and certify the displayed basis rank in exact products of E(F_p)/2E(F_p). A bounded saturation routine may supply a shorter candidate basis, but admit it only after exact point membership and an independent full-rank finite-quotient certificate. Then subtract this certified Kummer dimension from a complete Selmer dimension before constructing residual covers.
lessons.avoid: Treating a mod-3-selected basis as full mod-2 input, promoting bounded ellsaturation to global saturation, interpreting a PARI output as a Selmer bound, or searching covers before removing the certified known subgroup.
lessons.boundary: For the four fixed near misses, the exact inputs have Kummer dimensions 20, 20, 19 and 19. They are descent inputs only: no complete Selmer group, residual cover, rank upper bound, or new rational point follows.
lessons.reopen_when: The curve, point basis, rational 2-torsion condition, finite-quotient certificate, or intended descent changes; rebuild and certify the Kummer image before reusing the relative quotient.

lessons.title: Replay a public baseline from retained arithmetic inputs, not its webpage
lessons.when: A published equation, family, or point list supplies a fixed elliptic-curve calibration or lower-bound replay.
lessons.use: Retain the exact formulas or model, every displayed coordinate, a compact certificate, and hashes binding the checker to those inputs. Make the replay read only repository files; keep citation URLs and retrieval dates as provenance. State separately which current-record, attribution, conditional-upper-bound, or unpublished-construction assertions the local packet cannot establish.
lessons.avoid: Downloading a replacement input during replay, treating a URL and old hash as sufficient evidence, silently updating a public point list, or promoting a fixed finite-reduction lower bound to an exact rank or current-record claim.
lessons.boundary: The retained Kihara formulas at t=2 and the retained 29-point public record each support their exact stated lower bound without upstream access. They do not certify current external rankings, conditional upper bounds, a further point, or a different specialization.
lessons.reopen_when: The formula/model/coordinate packet, certificate criterion, or intended claim changes; preserve a new complete projection and compare it to the old packet before replaying.

lessons.title: Bound a six-root parent search in primitive coordinates
lessons.when: A known elliptic curve is absent from a bounded six-root parent census.
lessons.use: Record the labelled rational roots, affine scale and translation, parameter scale, and the resulting primitive integral root tuple. Set the search bound on that primitive diameter, then verify the exact model change and transported generic section.
lessons.avoid: Treating a miss in a normalized coordinate box as absence of a parent family, or using a matching j-invariant without an exact Weierstrass change.
lessons.boundary: For ICARM curve 245, the earlier diameter-300 census could not see the recovered parent because its primitive integral diameter is 731. This recognition result recovers a parent; it does not transfer the specialized rank to nearby fibres.
lessons.reopen_when: The proposed family has a different equivalence relation, root labelling, or primitive-bound convention.

lessons.title: Keep a rebuilt replay in a named successor lineage
lessons.when: A historical checker cannot run because its immutable source artifact or toolchain is unavailable, but a compatible exact source chain can be rebuilt.
lessons.use: Keep the historical program and its expected digest unchanged. Write a separate successor wrapper that asserts replacement input digests and writes a distinct schema and output path. If a new independent global proof becomes available, register it separately rather than retagging the historical record.
lessons.avoid: Retagging a rebuilt output as the historical artifact, relaxing a frozen input assertion, overwriting the old output path, or treating a bounded successor sieve as the missing global proof.
lessons.boundary: The H3 source successor and bounded quotient sieve remain distinct current replay records. The later Sage quadratic-Chabauty certificate proves the rational base independently; it does not recreate the historic Magma output.
lessons.reopen_when: The original inputs and runtime become available for a byte-identical historical replay, or another frozen certificate needs a successor lineage.

lessons.title: Close an even genus-two curve with two rank-one elliptic quotients
lessons.when: An even sextic y^2=a6*x^6+a4*x^4+a2*x^2+a0 has two explicit elliptic quotients with unconditional rank one and trivial torsion, and a global rational-point proof is required.
lessons.use: Pin a bielliptic quadratic-Chabauty implementation, use two good ordinary primes with a compatible finite height-value ordering, normalize quotient coordinates at a rational base point, close p-adic roots under the curve automorphisms, CRT their coordinates modulo p^N, then eliminate the remaining classes by exact good-reduction images.
lessons.avoid: Treating one p-adic pass, a bounded multiple search, or a finite reduction sieve by itself as completeness; and claiming the direct quotient-coordinate lattice is a saturated Jacobian basis when only its necessary quotient condition is used.
lessons.boundary: The method certifies only the displayed curve and the pinned implementation, primes, precision and finite sieve. It requires exact quotient rank and torsion certificates and does not construct a downstream surface or fibration equation. An offline replay must supply the one SHA-checked upstream source through --upstream-source; a cache miss otherwise downloads only the pinned revision.
lessons.reopen_when: The model, quotient maps, rank certificates, implementation hash, p-adic precision or candidate-eliminating prime set changes.

lessons.title: Transfer a labeled finite-reduction certificate to generic rank
lessons.when: Explicit sections of an elliptic family are available and one smooth rational specialization may establish a generic rank lower bound.
lessons.use: Verify the section identities over the function field, preserve their labels through one good specialization, select only the needed points, and stack exact E(F_p)/lE(F_p) columns until they have full rank. Add a good-reduction exclusion of rational l-torsion, then invoke specialization to transfer that selected independent subgroup to the generic fibre.
lessons.avoid: Sorting or changing branches separately at each reduction, treating all displayed sections as independent, or replacing the torsion check with a bounded relation search.
lessons.boundary: This proves only the lower bound supplied by the selected labeled sections. It gives neither generic rank equality, saturation, independence of unused companions, nor an exact conductor statement.
lessons.reopen_when: The family formulas, labeled section roster, specialization, reduction prime set, or torsion exclusion changes.

lessons.title: Keep unresolved quotient transports as literal unknowns
lessons.when: A finite population of specialized elliptic fibres has a mixture of exact displayed-subgroup transports and uncompiled chart-specific quotient data.
lessons.use: Bind the population and each marked-U chart to a profile artifact. Retain only exact transports as exact, leave every other dimension null, and select a new tranche solely by a declared arithmetic criterion such as the maximum certified specialized rank lower bound. For each selected row, require a saturated generic transport, exact specialization and group-law relations, displayed-subgroup independence, and a Smith-form quotient proof.
lessons.avoid: Treating a null as a zero quotient, copying a transport across PGL2 or lattice-equivalent markings, reopening a completed tranche, or using public hit counts as a success-rate denominator or priority score.
lessons.boundary: A displayed-subgroup quotient is not the quotient of the full Mordell--Weil group and gives no rank upper bound. The selected initial tranche is a reproducible work priority, not evidence that it has positive quotient rank or that deferred rows are unpromising.
lessons.reopen_when: The marked-U transport, certified rank lower bounds, population membership, or exact quotient data changes.

lessons.title: Require quotient-invariant local data before using Kummer information as a selector
lessons.when: Comparing fixed high-rank specializations for a shared local Kummer signature that might justify congruence filtering or a parameter search.
lessons.use: Present the displayed directions as V/R before choosing any complement. Compare only local Kummer and component data that descend through R; for each componentwise Hilbert form B, check R*B=0 before treating it as a quotient tensor. If the retained quotient-invariant signatures disagree, preserve the exact obstruction primes and terminate that selector route.
lessons.avoid: Building a graph from RREF nonpivot coordinates, treating the identically trivial corestricted local Tate form as a coupling signal, turning a fixed-pair mismatch into a global nonexistence theorem, or launching a parameter search merely because a local diagnostic was computed.
lessons.boundary: The gate concerns the stated quotient presentation and selected fibres. It proves neither a full Mordell--Weil quotient nor a rank upper bound, and it leaves mechanisms based on different invariant data open.
lessons.reopen_when: A different quotient-compatible invariant, a changed visible relation space, or an independently justified family-wide mathematical gate is available.

lessons.title: Use certified local height bounds to compare complementary models of the same pointed chart
lessons.when: Comparing equivalent pointed quartic models for a fixed elliptic equation and anchor, before choosing search boxes.
lessons.use: Compose the exact x(2P-Q) map with each parameter matrix. Bound its real norm on the soluble compact projective charts, and refine the uniform Bezout cancellation divisor using complete finite residue trees with proved nonsquare exclusions. Keep unprocessed primes and branches conservatively. For multiple minimal models, retain joint local cells and take max over cells of min over complete models. Charge construction, bounds, failed attempts, point calls and verification in the next-direction benchmark.
lessons.avoid: Choosing a model by coefficient size alone, confusing a smaller sufficient height bound with containment of every old search box, summing model-wise minima independently across primes, or calling a rational-address work proxy a CPU or rank-gain prediction.
lessons.boundary: One actual Curve302 chart supplies independently replayed bounds and three certified minimal models. The base-plus7-neighbour pair has approximately1.48033 improvement in sufficient per-box height and0.91266 address-work ratio, but no new point search or speed advantage. The finite bounds need not be optimal. The old factor-free model is a comparator, not one of the three minimal models.
lessons.reopen_when: A frozen next-direction comparison pays for its new preparation and then transfers to independently sourced withheld directions on other curves.

lessons.title: Separate cold support, uniform coverage and actual target accessibility
lessons.when: Benchmarking a certified height-based model selector at the supplied equation, subgroup and anchor interface.
lessons.use: Freeze model vocabulary and exact pair-height allocation before search; charge required support discovery and verification. After all endpoints are sealed, transport each literal winning point into every model and verify its parameter height and exact slack decomposition log(C/g)/4 plus log(S/L)/4. Keep diagnostics separate from arm costs and target-informed selection.
lessons.avoid: Treating cached discriminant factors as free cold preparation, hiding a preparation timeout as a point-search miss, assuming the smallest uniform bound gives the smallest coordinate for each point, or using a distinct-prime product partition for two neighbours at one prime.
lessons.boundary: On three Curve302 controls the baseline recovers the next direction, while all six bounded arms hit a30-second support limit and make no point calls. Twelve individual-model coordinates replay; the best uniform bound selects a smallest actual coordinate only in the first row. Finite cancellation dominates the slack. This is a three-target conditional diagnostic, not a general performance or probability statement. The same-prime pair is UNKNOWN only for the frozen formula.
lessons.reopen_when: A specifically revised, bounded preparation or model-selection policy addresses the measured bottleneck and receives a new complete-cost comparison; no automatic rerun or budget enlargement.

lessons.title: Optimize complete coverage with unequal box heights and explicit model costs
lessons.when: A certified complete joint-state table for equivalent models of one marked chart is already available.
lessons.use: At a declared elliptic-height range X, compute exact ceil((X D_i(s))^(1/4)) thresholds. Minimize a supplied monotone cost over boxes meeting at least one model threshold for every joint state. Charge activation separately from all-bank preparation, including discarded models. Check the finite optimum by independent state assignments; keep the statewise choice coupled across all places.
lessons.avoid: Treating minimization of a shared coverage constant as the whole cost problem, dropping discarded-model preparation, calling an equal H-squared price a CPU calibration, or using uniform coverage as a probability model for the first independent point.
lessons.boundary: The earlier equal-box selector already charged model count through |T|^2 D_T. On its unchanged three-model/four-state first chart, unequal heights yield an exact 0.573942907264 address-proxy ratio to the best single, or 0.599197887808 with at most two models. This does not resolve cold support timeouts or the observed targetwise finite-cancellation slack. No search was run or selector deployed into the sealed benchmark.
lessons.reopen_when: A bounded preparation and independently calibrated pricing policy is frozen for a new complete-cost comparison. Transfer needs independently sourced cross-curve targets; proxy optimization alone does not authorize a campaign.

lessons.title: Verify integral orders and the backend input contract before global Selmer arithmetic
lessons.when: Completing global descent on one of the two frozen large nonmonic RR sextics.
lessons.use: Reuse the exact pair inputs and order checkpoints. A binary-sextic order removes an artificial monic index; certify ring closure and its trace discriminant before using it for generator reduction. Reconstructing a partial order after a generator change can lose integrality away from the trial primes. Keep complete supported squareclasses, class and unit contributions, local conditions and the true/fake comparison as separate obligations. Preserve both verified orders after a generator change by adjoining their pairwise basis products. In a commutative field their product lattice is already an order. The fixed RR join has independently checked containment, integral multiplication and Newton trace discriminants of22655/37378bits for cases09/08. The third retained order is contained in that join in both cases. Gcd-refining discriminant/index divisors and using the distinct coprime-list nfinit contract gives successor order discriminants22655/28881bits; exact support decomposition and containment replay independently.
lessons.avoid: Treating a nonempty nfcertify remainder as a field discriminant, treating known local or rational Kummer spans as a complete global space, or using nfcertify=[] on an arbitrary basis supplied to nfinit as an independent maximality proof. The supplied-basis example X^2-20 returns[] for the nonmaximal order of discriminant80.
lessons.boundary: Cases09 and08 have verified model and field maps and integral orders, but no certified maximal order or global Selmer dimension. Both certification passes returned unresolved composites. The measured order sizes and failure receipts do not prove intrinsic infeasibility or equal residual dimensions. Same-fibre matching tests the marked construction, not a population rank effect. The joined orders improve the retained checkpoints but have no new maximality certificate; their size is not a field-complexity comparison. Both coprime-list nfcertify calls still return unresolved cofactors22633/28878bits, so global completeness remains open.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact maximal-order/support certificate or a different certified global upper-envelope method addresses the unresolved pair; reusing already completed local images alone is insufficient.

lessons.title: Count normalization delta with infinity and keep the high-rank parent fixed
lessons.when: Forcing two polynomial trace-zero bisections of arithmetic genus5 to share a quadratic cover of genus0 or1.
lessons.use: Write F=x^3+A*x+B and its jet conditions. At a root of multiplicity m use delta=floor(m/2), and include the missing multiplicity at infinity in the degree12 binary form. Impose one literal D in both identities. Extract repeated factors D=e^2*d before deciding the genus: residual degree2 gives a possible genus0 boundary. Reuse the height8 independence criterion when the branch avoids the parent discriminant. For a fixed constant-abscissa line, the degree33 critical-point polynomial and critical-value norm can certify its entire singularity locus by exact interpolation and a good-prime squarefreeness witness. For the complete coefficient chart, factor the difference identity with g=gcd(D,h), u=gcd(h/g,r1-r2) and v=(h/g)/u after monic normalization. Keep all15 degree allocations and nine good coordinate patches; the squarefree height cross term is4-k-2*j. On Q80 use unramified Kummer descent to eliminate the complete k=4 genus-one case before any elimination. For genus0 pass to the full f(x_i)=q*s_i^2 chart with deg s_i<=5; repeated common-quartic models unnecessarily force a shared linear node factor. Keep all12 degree allocations. In the Q80 k2,j1 case use inherited unramified descent and the complete arithmetic-genus1 singular exclusion before coefficient elimination. After same-branch genus0 descent, the cross-height+/-2 cases have a smooth rational half-image. Reuse the complete branch atlas and exclude parent2-torsion over its residue fields with simple degree-one prime witnesses. Monic cubic integrality handles unbounded coordinates; specialization at ramification then forces anti-invariant height at least12. Before searching for a high-rank fibration on a new control surface, a complete good-prime surface count gives the cheap necessary bound rho_Q <= floor((22*p+#X(Fp)-1-p^2)/(2*p)). Subtract2 for any rational Jacobian fibration. Retain infinity and count a nodal cubic itself, not its normalization. Distinguish a cubic root from complete splitting and a square discriminant from a root. For a local full-splitting witness retain three distinct Hensel balls satisfying v(f)>2*v(f_prime) and pairwise disjoint error radii. Exact rational replay handles bad primes and weighted infinity without trusting approximate p-adic roots. Before coefficient elimination, pair the ramified norm-square class with inherited unramified alpha_T=X_T-theta by Weil reciprocity. Its odd divisor Z must satisfy Norm_Z(alpha_T) square for every T. For a single complementary fibre divisor this reduces to X_T(b)-e square. A complete good-prime root roster with one nonvanishing nonsquare character per point excludes that whole stratum. Recheck literal rational section identities and all infinity reductions; independence of the witness sections is unnecessary. For a degree2 branch divisor evaluate both selected-root norm-character vectors over the complete quadratic residue field. Use3*e^2+A when an inherited section meets the selected2-torsion root, and squareclass1 at a pole. Include roots with multiplicity at nodal quadratic residues. Distinguish rational branch pairs, unramified quadratic fields with rational or quadratic base residue, and ramified quadratic fields before deducing a coefficient congruence. After a genus0 branch collision is forced at a smooth fibre, first prove coefficient integrality using the flat divisor limit of the rational bisection and properness of genus0 stable maps. Treat the literal scalar valuation and constant nonsquare twist before enumerating reduced points. Recompute the finite basis Gram and use character rank and index-square divisibility to prove full saturation. Enumerate the complete norm4 lattice with exact rational LDL bounds, identify every polynomial point and test the full coefficient Jacobian, including homogeneous infinity. A simple ordinate zero has only its inherited split Hensel lift. Repeated contacts can support a nonsplit lift only if both required root labels survive at the same fibre. For genus1 k2, apply degree2 reciprocity to the unused root of P1-P2; this is only one norm condition. Use complete individual character codes and their pairwise XORs to classify both agreement and disagreement divisors. For a genus1 denominator limit, count positive-genus components and retain the actual zero-section multiplicity. A fourth-power smooth-fibre limit would require four unramified elliptic preimages and four separate nonconstant O tails, exceeding its O degree2. Keep the all-nodal case. With integral coefficients, compare complete reduced norm4 contact pairs and augment the full shared-quartic Jacobian by the first error from the literal coefficients modulo p^2. Use exact residue interpolation to cut a remaining polynomial search to p or p^3 tuples, including arbitrary scalar classes, and independently reconstruct square roots in the opposite coefficient direction. For a surviving nodal boundary, the anisotropic quadratic and quartic invariant give necessary local rational-point and j-valuation conditions. At an I1 denominator boundary, split off the analytic simple cubic root rho and prepare x-rho and r in the residue disc. Count their zeros with multiplicity before choosing a valuation scale. A double zero of x-rho uses one r zero; differentiating the remaining U^2-V contact determines the scale and its second derivative excludes higher contacts. Compare the abscissa difference quotient with the two analytic node-root labels on the common smaller branch disc. If each section must switch labels, partial branch agreement is impossible. Verify the implicit derivative of rho from the actual cubic coefficients, not from a polynomial representing only its residue value. Retain an exact local section control and distinguish split, unramified and ramified branch fields. A rational agreement branch at a good residue can force genus1 coefficient integrality. With one smooth and three nodal residues, a primitive simple abscissa zero produces three distinct simple zeros against the three analytic cubic-root functions, contradicting a single branch zero. Once integral, the agreement residue cannot collide with disagreement. Odd total multiplicity at a repeated cubic residue leaves a nonzero rational unused-root character. For squarefree degree3 disagreement, impose both its zero unused-root norm and its selected-root norm matching the rational agreement code. Reuse rational/quadratic tables and enumerate every nonrational cubic base orbit. A Frobenius splitting test avoids scanning all possible cubic roots; keep nodal root multiplicity and regularized zeros/poles. Replay using different extension-field and polynomial arithmetic, direct Q-power versus repeated p-Frobenius, and indexed joins instead of all composite tuples. lessons.avoid: Treating a rational coarse point alone as a marked K3; treating Galois-invariant Picard classes automatically as rational line bundles; treating one rootful frame as an exhaustive absence of MW17. In the retained rootless preflight, PARI qfminim with maxvec=0 returned no stored vectors despite a nonzero count; that false-hit packet is explicitly withdrawn. Always check the total against stored representatives and a known-root control.
lessons.boundary: This proves an abstract full rational marking, without an equation. The later global root-energy theorem excludes MW17 on this NS; it does not retract the descent result.
lessons.reopen_when: A new marking changes the local level, has residual automorphisms, or lacks a divisor-descent argument.

lessons.title: Exclude rootless2-neighbours with a complete parity cover and norm-eight witnesses
lessons.when: An even positive frame has displayed roots that every rootless2-neighbour must remove.
lessons.use: Enumerate v modulo2F with even quadratic value and odd pairing with every old root. For each class, an explicit same-parity norm-eight vector halves to a root in its even neighbour. Check mod2 radical lifts separately at determinant-dividing prime2. Replay needs only these finite witnesses, not a complete short-vector census.
lessons.avoid: Assuming2 is a good prime; ignoring radical-line neighbours; mistaking a bounded neighbour miss or one-frame obstruction for a genus-wide rootlessness exclusion.
lessons.boundary: The pinned388 index106 frame has a rootful entire even2-neighbour shell. The subsequent global root-energy theorem separately excludes all frames of this NS; the local method alone has only its one-frame scope.
lessons.reopen_when: The parent frame changes, the neighbour degree changes, or a global genus argument becomes available.

lessons.title: Seek low-degree points on the simultaneous branch-incidence curves
lessons.when: A24-I1 elliptic K3 with its full geometric MW group rational is being tested for two trace directions on one low-genus quadratic cover.
lessons.use: Two independent trace parities require residue-field lifts of every branch to the degree16 genus57 joint-half curve. A nonzero trace plus an actual nonzero branch2-torsion value requires a lift to the degree12 genus49 mixed incidence curve. Primitive forgetful maps and Castelnuovo-Severi exclude degree-at-most4 maps to genus0 or1; Kadets-Vogt then gives a finite low-degree-point locus. Use an actual low-degree incidence point as the next arithmetic gate before solving global trace torsors.
lessons.avoid: Assuming that high genus alone excludes low-degree points, applying Riemann-Hurwitz to a disconnected fibre product, confusing a local modular point with a residue-field point, or treating noneffective finiteness as an empty set or a construction.
lessons.boundary: Full geometric parity independence,24-I1 fibres and a fixed number field are essential. The two-trace locus gives finite branch divisors and constant characters. The mixed locus restricts only its marked branch. Q80 gain conclusions retain the good131 branch-image bounds; other branch-reduction scopes and the positive endpoint remain open.
lessons.reopen_when: A genuine degree-at-most4 incidence point is obtained, with an exact common trace-torsor lift and the required rational or infinite elliptic base; or a different parent changes the monodromy/fibre hypotheses.

lessons.title: Use a root-rich auxiliary and Weyl-support norm bounds before rank17 genus enumeration
lessons.when: An admitted NS has a positive rank7 opposite-discriminant auxiliary containing a rank5 root system.
lessons.use: Find a convenient explicit auxiliary in its much smaller genus, verify its discriminant anti-isometry, and compute the projected Gram of the two remaining generators. For each complete Niemeier anchor, bound simultaneous root avoidance by minimizing 1_S^t C^-1 1_S + 1_Z^t C_Z^-1 1_Z over Dynkin supports; add bounds across orthogonal components. If every required norm sum exceeds the available trace, all frame complements are rootful.
lessons.avoid: Replacing the actual finite discriminant form by determinant equality; the attractive rank6 auxiliaries tried for388 have the wrong form. Do not infer global nonexistence from local neighbour misses or from the auxiliary mass search alone.
lessons.boundary: For388 every case fails strictly. For852 energy bounds alone leave2A7+2D5; the subsequent exhaustive two-vector/glue calculation excludes that final case. The energy reduction alone is not the global exclusion, and auxiliary genus completeness is discovery only.
lessons.reopen_when: Another NS discriminant form, a new arithmetic marking, or an auxiliary whose projected norms pass the bound is supplied.

lessons.title: Certify elementary branch relations before searching for additional halves
lessons.when: Trying to populate the low-degree joint-halving or mixed incidence loci from a retained generic MW basis.
lessons.use: Form cancelled pole and signed abscissa-equality loci and the correct long-Weierstrass torsion ordinate2y+a1*x+a3. A pair of independent zero relations supplies explicit halves O; one relation with nonzero torsion supplies mixed incidence. Use monic polynomials integral at the chosen reduction prime, followed by exact rational gcd on every modular survivor. At known pole fields, bound the full specialization kernel with finite elliptic-group quotients and retain the visible generic parity as a lower bound.
lessons.avoid: Using a fixed prime without checking monic integrality or degree preservation, treating y=0 as the2-torsion condition on a long model, conflating an ordinary relation with two independent parity relations, or extending a basis-only miss to all MW combinations.
lessons.boundary: The four retained basis-derived lists have no simultaneous elementary incidence, including infinity. All12 Q80 basis pole fields have exactly one kernel direction and no nonzero residue-field2-torsion. The initial fixed131 prototype was unaccepted and is preserved; only the rerun with integral monic reduction supports the exclusions.
lessons.reopen_when: A distinct exact generic combination provides an additional residue-field half, or an actual low-degree incidence point outside these fixed elementary lists is constructed. A larger unmotivated coefficient box is not a new gate.

lessons.title: Check j-monodromy before trying to duplicate sections by a cover symmetry
lessons.when: A proposed correlated-gain mechanism uses an automorphism or isogeny to turn one known new direction into another.
lessons.use: For a degree24 K3 j-map, certify simple c4,c6,D divisors and18 distinct additional simple critical values. Compute critical images as multiplication by j in the degree18 critical algebra and verify its squarefree characteristic polynomial. The3^8,2^12 and18 transposition branch cycles force S24 by the normal-closure argument, so a distinct equal-j generic parameter costs degree23. This controls extra automorphisms even on covers where descent to the original parameter was not assumed.
lessons.avoid: Assuming no parent base symmetry automatically rules out cover symmetries, overlooking collisions among critical values, confusing generic equal-j rigidity with a ban on specialized j coincidences, or using an already independent new translation as its own construction.
lessons.boundary: All four retained actual MW17 parents pass the S24 gate. Every quadratic-cover j-symmetry is identity or deck, and origin-preserving symmetries act by signs on an anti-invariant direction. The24-I1 full mod-ell theorem also excludes nontrivial isogeny transport over a quadratic field. Neither statement bounds arbitrary twist rank or excludes fibration-changing surface automorphisms.
lessons.reopen_when: A different actual arithmetic MW17 parent has a certified suitable symmetry and an invariant low-genus cover with an independent section orbit. Critical-value collisions alone are insufficient, and a new parent still requires the rational marking and full arithmetic rank evidence.

lessons.title: Rationalize the full rank-one Inose Mordell-Weil group by its constant sign character
lessons.when: A rational Inose model comes from a non-CM isogenous pair and has two rational II* fibres with torsion-free geometric MW rank1.
lessons.use: Write the Inose equation using rational symmetric j invariants, without demanding rational cube or square roots. The two affineE8 graphs force every trivial-lattice divisor rational. The full geometric MW generator transforms by a continuous sign character; the matching constant quadratic twist fixes it and yields full saturated rational NS.
lessons.avoid: Calling the untwisted model fully marked before computing its character; treating rational roots of normalized invariants as necessary; using a coarse period point alone instead of surface/divisor descent. Unneeded large coefficient factorization in the preflight was stopped and is not a prerequisite.
lessons.boundary: The level311 source has NS determinant622 and a rationalizing twist exists; its squareclass and section remain uncomputed. The later global root obstruction excludes MW17 on this NS, so explicit twist calculation is not needed for this goal. Higher MW rank can have Galois action that a single twist cannot trivialize.
lessons.reopen_when: The character is computed, a different isogenous pair supplies a source, or the geometric MW rank or fibre Galois action differs.

lessons.title: Resolve borderline Niemeier energy cases with centered integer pairs and equality constraints
lessons.when: A two-vector auxiliary trace equals the sharp residual root-avoidance lower bound instead of violating it strictly.
lessons.use: For A_n encode two integral-pairing vectors as n+1 distinct integer pairs centered at their mean. Enumerate centroid residues modulo integers and nearest-point distances, certify equality sets and their separate coordinate norms. Equality in a total energy bound then constrains each projected norm. On the residual D5, short dual vectors leave D4 roots whose regular-vector norm requirement can contradict the remaining budget.
lessons.avoid: Declaring a rootless frame from a non-strict support bound, or treating the trace alone as the full Gram constraint. Retain the auxiliary discovery and all finite equality witnesses.
lessons.boundary: For622, A7 has sharp bound39/4 with each equality coordinate norm39/8. Two copies plus D5 meet trace51/2, but leave D5 norms<=1 and<=5, incompatible with the D4 regular-vector bound14. All16 Niemeier cases are thereby excluded in this NS genus.
lessons.reopen_when: Another admitted NS or auxiliary has different discriminant form, projected Gram or residual root systems; an equality-compatible case still requires actual primitive embedding and arithmetic fibration work.

lessons.title: An order-four lift makes one new direction an orthogonal pair
lessons.when: A prospective parent has an origin-preserving base involution and a symmetry-based two-gain construction is being considered.
lessons.use: Require a rational lift alpha with alpha^2 equal to the quadratic deck involution. The anti-invariant group then has Q(i)-module structure, even rank and an orthogonal orbit P,alpha(P). For a rational conic over Q the intermediate base involution must have fixed-point field Q(i); normalize it to -1/t and use w^2=t^2+1. Before equivariant lattice searches, test fields of known involution-fixed points: any fixed point over a field not containing i excludes this lift on every equivariant rational fibration. Before frame or involution searches on a fully rational Picard19 K3, test the actual T for rational isotropy. If it is anisotropic, real topology excludes every base-fixed-point-free pointed involution and hence the order-four conic mechanism. For a proposed rational Fricke source at composite level N, first forget to divisors d|N whose modular curves have a complete degree-at-most-two point classification. A non-CM rational Fricke point would induce a non-CM point of degree at most2 at each such lower level; an empty lower-level locus closes the source without building its fibre.
lessons.avoid: Assuming an order-two parent symmetry already forces two gains, overlooking the square of its lift, substituting a low-rank control for MW17, or treating a geometric9+8 eigenspace split as an arithmetic conic lift.
lessons.boundary: The explicit control realizes diag(8,8) on a rational conic but has parent rank at most10. The four retained MW17 parents fail the prior S24 symmetry gate. The canonical determinant622 Inose reversal and its Q-conjugates fail the fixed-point-field gate on every constant twist; the independent global determinant622 root obstruction now excludes every MW17 frame on that surface. The complete X1092 frame gate also excludes the required pointed base involutions on all nineteen rootless frames. A genus1 base over Q cannot have the required order-four lift because its differential eigenvalue would square to-1. The retained determinant1020 rootless frame also fails: its complete PARI isometry group is {I,-I}, so no trace1 involution exists. This is one frame, not a classification of that NS. Require a success marker when running PARI: stack changes discard remaining expressions on the same line, and default parallel worker stacks can exceed a fixed memory cap. Complete determinant948 rootless J2 coverage gives involution traces -17 and {-17,-3,3}; absence of1 excludes every MW17 fibration on that NS, independently of J1 orbit enumeration, and also excludes the rational-surface8+9 symmetric-parent setup there. This global real-place gate excludes the mechanism for948,1092 and1020 without a complete1020 frame census. Isotropic T is only necessary. Other Picard ranks, incomplete rational markings and nonsymmetry constructions are not excluded. A new star510 point is an explicit exploratory input for an isotropic Inose source, but its degree-eight Fricke lift is now excluded by the complete level51 quadratic-point classification. The existing determinant1020 rootless frame has the wrong discriminant form modulo5 for the isotropic NS. Author point logs and canonical HNF model files use different bases; bind coordinates to cached forms and verify the relation through its Sturm bound before using them.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual arithmetic MW17 parent has a verified suitable involution with the Q(i) fixed-base field, and one nontorsion anti-invariant section is constructed on the distinguished rational conic. All parent, cover and point evidence must be explicit.

lessons.title: Match published positive-rank Shimura quotients only after full stable-kernel verification
lessons.when: A content-one ternary lattice has a squarefree reduced Clifford discriminant and a candidate full-Fricke Shimura quotient in rational-point tables.
lessons.use: Match literal quaternion/order data first, then prove integral normalizers exhaust the discriminant actions and all local order units are stable. Verify the canonical arithmetic level. Separate published rational-point existence from Jacobian isomorphism; verify a non-torsion point directly on the model.
lessons.avoid: Using a coarse quotient or a positive-rank Jacobian as a rational marked source; labelling an infinite-order elliptic point non-CM without identifying its moduli interpretation.
lessons.boundary: The852 full curve, intrinsic rational non-CM point, primitive NS and actual divisor descent are proved. The subsequent complete final-anchor obstruction excludes MW17 in this NS. Its arithmetic marking survives;600 other rows remain unadmitted.
lessons.reopen_when: A non-CM point with moduli interpretation and full descent is certified, or another literal stable curve passes these tests.

lessons.title: A nine-plus-eight MW split must also satisfy discriminant gluing
lessons.when: Considering a pointed involution on a Picard19 rootless MW17 frame for correlated quadratic gains.
lessons.use: Inspect the complete frame automorphism group for trace-one involutions and require (g-I)H^(-1) integral. A symplectic involution fixes the transcendental lattice, so the NS discriminant action must be trivial. Apply this cheap exact test before equation reconstruction.
lessons.avoid: Treating a rational eigenspace split as sufficient for a K3 involution, or reconstructing another X1092 frame to revive the order-four mechanism.
lessons.boundary: All nineteen X1092 rootless J2 types are covered using inherited census completeness and group orders. Five trace-one candidates fail gluing. The theorem excludes pointed base involutions but not arbitrary correlated gains or fibration-changing automorphisms. The batched PARI timeout is preserved as an engineering failure; isolated generators and exact matrix closure supply accepted evidence.
lessons.reopen_when: A different NS with actual arithmetic marking has a compatible lattice involution, geometric realization, the Q(i) fixed-base condition and a new anti-invariant direction.

lessons.title: Halving points must have the same residue field as their branch value
lessons.when: Using low-degree points on a primitive halving curve to construct a quadratic rank-gain cover.
lessons.use: Require k(P)=k(t(P)). For the trace of a smooth rational bisection, use the F1 quotient and its adjoint fixed divisor to prove uniqueness of the original rational degree-four pencil. Points obtained by varying rational t lie over larger residue fields and are not usable branch halves.
lessons.avoid: Treating a quartic half above rational t as a half over the branch field, confusing field equality with a number field having no subfields, or claiming finiteness from uniqueness of a rational pencil.
lessons.boundary: Applies to the primitive trace of an embedded smooth rational bisection on a24-I1 K3, including Q80 parity65538. Its usable degree2..4 points are P1-isolated, but elliptic quotients and isolated arithmetic points remain uncomputed. The checker verifies embedding premises and intersection arithmetic; the quotient and complete-linear-system argument is written.

lessons.title: Finish an energy-surviving Niemeier anchor with exact dual-root labels and both D5 orientations
lessons.when: A primitive opposite-form auxiliary contains D5 and energy bounds leave a small number of Niemeier anchors.
lessons.use: Check both D5 outer diagram orientations unless an ambient extension is certified. Move the sixth vector into a residual Weyl chamber; enumerate nonnegative integral labels with its exact projected norm, regular seventh-vector lower bounds and actual Niemeier glue. Use its zero-node Weyl stabilizer to make the seventh labels positive there; exhaust dual-root vectors under exact component bounds and match both norm and pairing.
lessons.avoid: Treating one D5 diagram orientation as all embeddings, or substituting root-lattice coordinates for the Niemeier glue. Verify stored-vector counts equal full enumeration counts. A passed trace bound alone is neither a witness nor an obstruction.
lessons.boundary: For852,52 sixth label combinations per orientation reduce to13 integral vectors; all26 cases have zero seventh norm/pairing matches. This closes the last anchor and the actual NS genus, with no determinant-wide or lower maximum-rank claim.
lessons.reopen_when: A different admitted NS or auxiliary survives these exact constraints; a surviving vector pair still requires primitive embedding, rootless complement and arithmetic equation certificates.

lessons.title: Use rational tangent points for the first singular elliptic-bisection layer
lessons.when: Seeking genus-one quadratic covers beyond smooth bisection pencils on a24-I1 elliptic K3.
lessons.use: For arithmetic-genus2 images, normalize trace modulo twice the inherited MW group and pass to the quotient by T-P. Its F1 branch curve has genus9. A genuine genus-one normalization comes from a rational tangent point with exactly one contact of order2 or3; test its tangent line, integral pullback, residual quartic and rational base. For any smooth-branch cover, use h(anti-trace)=4*(p_a+3) to certify independence from a nonsquare genus ratio once the literal cover is identical. For an inherited rational contact in this layer, require h(T-2R)>=14 before interpolation. Recover a retained height-four word over Q by seven exact fibre evaluations, verify its polynomial equation, and use the intersection bound to attach it to the word; finite-field coordinates alone are insufficient. For arithmetic genus4, use a degree-three contact divisor on the F1 halving curve. Construct its Hermite lift modulo f^2 and test the three-by-two high-coefficient matrix before solving the full six jets. Rank1, homogeneous coprimality, actual incidence and a squarefree residual quartic are separate required checks. Infinite arithmetic supply would force a degree-three elliptic quotient; a contact-parameter elliptic curve is not the covering base. At equality in Castelnuovo-Severi, compare the same intrinsic adjoint line bundle on the forced smooth product model and on the ruled quotient. On F1, restriction of |2C0+F| retains C0.R as a fixed divisor; on a (3,4) curve in P1 times an elliptic curve, three explicit chart-glued adjoint sections have no common zero. Apply this obstruction before a cubic elliptic-map or Jacobian campaign.
lessons.avoid: Searching an unbounded two-parameter net as if rational one-node members formed a free rational family, mistaking rational singular points of the plane or dual curve for rational points of the normalization, or treating finiteness as an effective enumeration.
lessons.boundary: Finiteness is for arithmetic genus2 and normalization genus1 modulo inherited translations over a fixed number field. It does not exclude all such members or higher arithmetic genus. The height identity requires smooth parent branch fibres. A square height ratio proves neither dependence nor independence. Symbolic premises are checked but the geometric and Faltings arguments are written. For Q80 trace P3, the complete retained height-four shell at distance h(P3-2R)=14 has 230 oriented sections and no rational contact, including poles and infinity. Exact degree-five/degree-thirteen factors have modular no-root witnesses. This is a bounded experiment, not an all-height or all-trace exclusion. The cubic-contact constructor supplies no actual halving point. Although the genus9 Castelnuovo-Severi bound reaches equality for a degree-three elliptic quotient, its smooth product model makes |K_R-2L| basepoint-free, contradicting the fixed length-two divisor on F1. That quotient is now geometrically excluded and the arithmetic-genus4 layer is finite modulo translations. Exceptional contacts remain unenumerated; larger-degree elliptic maps and higher image genera are outside the result.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual eligible rational tangent point yields a literal quartic matching another independent bisection cover, with an infinite rational covering base, or a new construction addresses higher arithmetic-genus images.

lessons.title: Use a torsion CM orbit and one non-torsion CM orbit to specify a non-CM period intrinsically
lessons.when: A fully marked elliptic Shimura curve has rational torsionE[2], a four-point CM locus fixed by an inversion, and a second eight-point CM locus under residual translations and inversion.
lessons.use: Choose a point O in the first CM locus as origin. The first locus is exactlyE[2]; any point R in the second is non-torsion and that locus is +/-R+E[2]. Then2R is in neither locus, since2R=+/-R+T would make R or3R torsion. This gives a particular rational non-CM period without numerical CM coordinates.
lessons.avoid: Equating positive rank on a Jacobian with rational points on its torsor; applying the orbit argument before proving the complete CM locus and full marked group. Intrinsic coordinates are not a K3 equation certificate.
lessons.boundary: For1020 the full curve is510d2, CM discriminants are-3 and-163, and primitive embedding plus divisor descent prove full rational NS. A separate subsequent determinant1020 existence proof supplies the rootless frame and arithmetic MW17; this orbit method itself supplies neither equation nor frame. The source is outside the catalogue;600 historical rows remain separate.
lessons.reopen_when: Another full marked elliptic curve has the stated orbit and torsion data, or an explicit equation requires recovery of the intrinsic period coordinates.

lessons.title: Construct the second singular elliptic-bisection layer from actual quadratic contact jets
lessons.when: Seeking an arithmetic-genus3 bisection with genus1 normalization on a24-I1 K3.
lessons.use: Choose an actual degree-two contact divisor on the primitive halving curve. In F0 require the norm of its tangent slope to equal the squared secant coefficient; in F2 require slope trace twice that coefficient. Solve the four linear jet conditions, require a rank3 kernel giving an integral section, and verify the exact residual quartic and scalar. Fixed contact data determine at most one integral section by the intersection bound.
lessons.avoid: Replacing an actual halving-curve point by arbitrary quadratic coordinates, treating determinant zero as sufficient despite a reducible kernel, omitting diagonal contacts or infinity, or declaring an infinite rational base from a rational singular point.
lessons.boundary: The complete arithmetic-genus3 genus-one layer is finite over a fixed number field modulo inherited translations, not enumerated or empty. Higher image genus remains open. The exact interpolation controls are not K3 points. A matching cover of image genus1 or2 would give independent anti-traces by heights24 versus16 or20, but no match is supplied.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual halving-curve contact divisor passes the jet, irreducibility and residual quartic checks and matches a second verified cover with an infinite rational base.

lessons.title: A genuine inherited half can still force reducible contact interpolation
lessons.when: Using two conjugate quadratic halving points supplied by a fixed inherited section to construct an arithmetic-genus3 genus-one bisection.
lessons.use: Compute h(T-2R) first. The candidate quotient section intersects the inherited image in h(T-2R)/4-1; two common tangencies require at least4, hence height at least20. For exact equality fields, keep both ordinate signs. Factor a rational x-equality numerator only as needed and certify each higher-degree factor separately by a monic-integral finite-field gcd witness; verify the entire product.
lessons.avoid: Promoting a true halving point or a zero norm determinant to an integral carrier, dropping the sign T=+/-2R, claiming a whole-polynomial modular miss excludes factors, or applying the two-distinct-contact height bound to a diagonal point without its higher jet.
lessons.boundary: The fixed P1/P2 Q80 traces and O plus signed source basis supply exactly two nonpole quadratic half fields, both T=2P6 with height8 and reducible interpolation. Higher MW words, other traces, noninherited halves and diagonal contacts are not excluded. Initial26 unresolved whole-polynomial cases were resolved by factor-specific exact witnesses, not treated as positive points.
lessons.reopen_when: A new actual quadratic half outside the frozen bank has sufficient inherited distance height and passes integral jet interpolation, residual quartic, literal-character matching and rational-base checks.

lessons.title: Use root splitting for large-vector comparisons and stop genus work once a positive primitive witness suffices
lessons.when: A positive auxiliary has a large vector outside a high-rank root lattice and generic PARI automorphism or isometry enumeration overflows.
lessons.use: Split into the root lattice and its rational orthogonal complement, normalize the root Gram to Cartan, enumerate diagram actions and the small complementary automorphisms/isometries, then test integrality on the actual glued lattice. Weyl factors recover automorphism orders. For1020 a separate exact E6+<340> genus match led directly to a primitive4E6 rootless witness; finite-form comparison then identifies the admitted NS without completing the auxiliary genus.
lessons.avoid: Raising stack limits repeatedly or treating a bounded class list as a complete genus. Root rank and count need not uniquely specify the root type; require the exact Cartan isometry. A source-basis lattice transport or equation is not supplied by indefinite uniqueness.
lessons.boundary: Retained1020 exploration stopped at118 classes and100000 evaluations, with mass18329/7680 short of123721/51840. The structural helper supports only explicitly recognized Cartan cases and fails closed otherwise. The positive17-frame proof uses pinned primitive matrices, exact norm2 absence and discriminant isometry, not that partial list.
lessons.reopen_when: Another bounded calculation requires root-split comparisons, or an explicit source equation enables physical transport of the certified frame.

lessons.title: Distinguish a genuine branch divisibility defect from a vanishing generic relation
lessons.when: A low-degree branch half is available and its mechanism relative to the full inherited MW group is unclear.
lessons.use: Certify integral specialization injectivity with full-rank finite quotient matrices modulo an auxiliary prime ell and an independent no-ell-torsion reduction. A half of a primitive generic trace then lies outside every inherited integer combination. Combine with the modulo2 specialization kernel and absence of2-torsion to identify the first halving enlargement, without claiming a new rational vector-space rank.
lessons.avoid: Confusing a noninherited half with an extra number-field rank direction, inferring full2-saturation from its first step, or using a true F1 half as an F0/F2 contact input. For exact polynomial assertions use is_zero rather than coefficient-domain-sensitive equality of zero polynomials.
lessons.boundary: The known Q80 rank18 cover has an injective rank17 branch specialization and exactly one first-halving class, generated by its branch point. No second branch class, matching cover or new gain is constructed. The finite quotient and field calculations are replayed; the integral descent is written. A separate bounded height-six P3 contact attempt finds no nonpole or infinity rational half supplied by the signed source basis; its half-O contact is degenerate. For arithmetic genus2 an inherited tangent contact requires distance height at least14 by local intersection2. Higher inherited words and noninherited rational halves are not excluded.

lessons.title: Find a low-pole rank1 source presentation before solving large Humbert conditions
lessons.when: Arithmetic admission and a rootless frame are known but no explicit K3 equation is available.
lessons.use: Scan a bounded set of root-rank16 ADE lattices and generator component classes. Require the exact determinant and finite quadratic form, root saturation, and height-derived P.O. At1020 the primitive A2+2A3+A8 frame has height85/36 and P.O=0. This gives a polynomial-section chart; a nodal cubic parametrization eliminates the high I9 condition symbolically before solving the residual fiber equations. For additional multiplicative fibers, use a rational nodal root and local critical-value jets instead of expanding the full discriminant. Reduce the cubic jet modulo the quadratic jet only on the explicit nonzero-H chart.
lessons.avoid: Treating an ADE label as a physical nef marking, assuming A2 means I3 rather than IV, or accepting a modular/formal point as a rational source. A pairwise sum of dual basis vectors need not generate a cyclic discriminant group; use Smith transport and reduce the resulting dual vector modulo the lattice. The unsaturated nodal system includes additive and wrong-component degenerations. Two bounded eliminations, including one with an inverse-product open condition, returned no basis; a timeout gives no dimension or emptiness statement.
lessons.boundary: Discovery tested34517 component combinations in the declared <=4-factor, height(2,8], P.O<=2, torsion-free window. It is not a full fibration classification. The source frame is proved; the symbolic chart remains unsolved and elimination-denominator branches are retained. The F7 chart and fixed a1=0 F11 slice have no retained admissible finite-field point; this is not a Q-point obstruction. Both60-second Groebner pilots are terminal and unresolved.

Do not rerun the same time-bounded elimination merely with a larger limit.

lessons.title: Extend a branch-rank certificate to a congruence class of pencil parameters
lessons.when: A known one-gain genus-one pencil member could hide another direction at an unbounded height.
lessons.use: Compute the full generic basis modulo doubles at simple branch roots, exclude branch-field2-torsion independently, and apply the retained global trace theorem. Freeze enough coefficient congruences to preserve branch irreducibility, the residue places and the quotient matrix throughout a parameter progression.
lessons.avoid: Interpreting a small matrix kernel as a height-bounded point search, claiming a second gain from kernel deficiency, or treating an exact-rank genus-one function field as a proof of infinitely many rational base points.
lessons.boundary: The Q80 trace-P1 pencil has exact rank18 for lambda in 175361103335727332945*Z. Other parameters and two-gain constructions remain unresolved.

lessons.title: Compare component contact orders as well as section poles when choosing a source equation
lessons.when: A disjoint-section presentation requires a large cancellation system despite small P.O.
lessons.use: The central component5 of I10 permits t^5 divisibility of both B and C in a pointed cubic, making the large fiber automatic. For1020, account for P.O=1 with polynomial section degrees6 and9 in a minimal K3 model. High-degree cancellations at infinity and the nonidentity I3 conditions are all linear eliminations, yielding a rational six-parameter chart. Retain e=0 as the split-IV branch.

lessons.title: Use a fixed slice and polynomial degree to exclude a cotangent plane before graph searches

lessons.use: On the fixed slice, classify constant directions with vanishing second directional derivative. In this chart every x-invisible direction is forced onto the q axis. Prove the q degree is positive and even over the remaining function field, so q is never affine. Every two-plane meets the x-invisible hyperplane; the no-plane conclusion then feeds the reproduced structural alternative and closes all graph degrees at once. HC4MYGQ2 separately closes native q graphs by their square axis; HC4MYGP1 identifies and genuinely embeds the full remaining nonlinear p row orbit. HC4MYGL1/2 now close all nonlinear q-base and retained-dual automorphisms by the origin critical-coordinate first jet and the imported line-injectivity theorem. HC4MYGU0 closes zero boundary slices after arbitrary retained-dual substitutions. HC4MYGU1/2/3 reduce all origin-avoiding base-only graph reparameterizations exactly to the unit-ideal plane Keller problem, distinct from the p-chart singleton-zero problem. HC4MYGK0/1/2 add the relative critical-scheme determinant test and close every y=a(x)*p+b(x) with nonzero polynomial a after all retained-three-dual automorphisms. HC4MYGR0/1/2/3 add closed affine critical-component geometry and the generic-fibre Euler calculation, closing arbitrary nonlinear y boundary-root graphs and opposite x=a(y)*p+b(y) with a(0) nonzero. HC4MYGS0/1/2/3 add the preserved whole critical target-line map, an all-degree pole classification and the Chau/Orevkov plane-degree obstruction, excluding every nonzero-a opposite affine-p graph and reducing the full family to its base-only unit-ideal endpoint. HC4MYGN0/1/2/3 add empty-critical-scheme/Euler, initial Newton-face and finite smooth ramification gates, closing every separated y=a(x)*P(p)+b(x) in all degrees without Tang. HC4MYGM0/1/2/3 remove the whole finite polar and singular locus, require a full polynomial Bezout certificate and complete critical curve, impose an exact reciprocal conductor budget on escapes, and state the necessary entire abstract Keller-fibre realization. HC4MYGW0/1/2/3 add a genus-free whole-curve Euler/pole budget, algebraic differential descent, all quadratic p closure and a whole unbounded-degree family excluded despite passing local critical gates. HC4MYGY0/1/2/3 compare every Euler jump and one entire reciprocal-root product, closing the full positive-p y chart and leaving exactly its base-only nonautomorphic unit-ideal endpoint. HC4MYGX0/1/2/3 extend the global method to opposite nonlinear graphs, closing all simple-boundary and no-escape configurations and forcing at least six distinct critical roots in any remaining nonautomorphic mechanism. HC4MYGZ0/1/2/3 now compare the exceptional base-zero fibre and close both entire positive-p base charts, including every opposite escape; both whole p-only families retain only the base-only unit-ideal nonautomorphic endpoint. HC4MYHA0/1/2/3 extend the closure to every y=R(x,p,q) independent of old r: a general cylindrical-trace criterion combines with the all-degree plane polynomial G=P*(F^2-1)+Q*F and its square suspension, without a generic irreducibility or critical-projection assumption. HC4MYHB0/1/2/3 now use an isolated trace point and its Milnor intersection length to remove the generic-base Euler hypothesis for power-saddle traces. They close all r graphs under full (y,p,q) automorphisms fixing x and all hyperplane coordinate-triple pullbacks, including genuine old-r-dependent y graphs with unit-affine r boundary. HC4MYHC0/1/2/3 now retain the whole Hodge polynomial of one trace fibre. The positive t coefficient excludes rank zero, and genus/puncture coefficients force actual A1 Keller-fibre components in rank one. This closes arbitrary univariate-plus-saddle traces, nonlinear polynomial-coordinate r boundaries and branched trace triples, without isolated-point or generic-base data. HC4MYHD0/1/2/3 now count the whole value fibre by affine-dual row ranks, closing every one-affine-dual-direction y graph and every non-r opposite direction in arbitrary graph/coefficient degree. The pure-r opposite exception has no positive Hodge coefficient; its complete critical Hessian reduces remaining nonautomorphy to the two existing plane endpoints, without asserting a converse realization. HC4MYHE0/1/2 now compare two parallel whole trace Hodge profiles: one pure trace forces rank zero under nonautomorphy, whereas H(U)+V*a(U,W) of positive W degree and deg H>=2 cannot have a nonpositive pure signature. This closes arbitrary q-independent r boundaries with one constant nonzero-base slice. HC4MYHE3 also closes unibranch one-place boundary curves, including singular cusp powers, without that second slice. HC4MYHF0/1 now replace orientation-specific trial with the intrinsic plane: two distinct jointly affine planes force an inverse by an elementary proof, while the covectors admitting one pure trace form exactly the unique-plane annihilator under nonautomorphy. Three independent pure directions close every degree with no sign condition; two determine three concrete directional Hessian identities and otherwise retain the exact JC2 endpoint. HC4MYHF2 makes complete profiles count and reconstruct the reduced quotient fibre, preserving the two distinct unresolved ideals. HC4MYHG0/1 now use full critical schemes, critical Hessian values and entire value fibres to survive every polynomial source automorphism. No new graph-degree or source-word search is warranted inside those full orbits, and neither endpoint is solved. lessons.use: Retire every standard r graph after arbitrary base and relative dual automorphisms by HC4MYGC2. lessons.title: Split coefficient denominators before exact Macaulay replay; inspect incidence geometry separately

lessons.title: Use generic-fibre pole degrees and derivative residues after leading-symbol reduction
lessons.when: A finite surface map has a fixed volume divisor and one target coordinate has controlled pole order.
lessons.use: Derive support containment from a uniform principal-part identity. List every local Newton branch of a generic coordinate fibre. Divide the volume form by the normal derivative of the first coordinate to compute the second-coordinate differential on each branch; sum pole degrees and test simple-pole residues. Keep contact cancellation and all infinity points. At pole three divide the volume identity by F_z for F=z^3(P-c). lessons.title: Exclude low-degree constant Jacobian pairings before sparse algebra
lessons.when: A normalized low-degree three-variable Keller collision candidate is considered.
lessons.use: Reject completed supports with a nonlinear univariate coordinate or a nonconstant normal derivative on a coordinate hyperplane. In degree at most ten, a constant nonzero v^T*JF*w is excluded by a triangular source reduction to a plane map of degree at most D^2<=100 and Moh. For normalized maps search the finite bilinear direction incidence. The complete size-eight cover has 17435 univariate, 46 elementary-shear, and one hyperplane-normal-factor orbit. GLDC4 also forces a nonlinear own-variable term in each row and hence a strongly connected three-vertex dependence graph by block triangularity. Missing row or cut conditions require explicit possible repairs; lower-bound repair costs may be summed only when their atom sets are disjoint.
lessons.avoid: Discarding a repairable partial support because its current row is univariate or triangular; treating empty direction incidence as a counterexample; applying the D<=10 consequence at unbounded degree.
lessons.boundary: The univariate and hyperplane-normal-factor gates are arbitrary-degree necessities. The pairing gate imports Moh's degree-100 plane theorem. The special-form minimum four is for degree-at-most-ten counterexamples admitting a constant nonzero pairing, with a degree-seven stabilized witness; it is not an unrestricted dimension minimum.
lessons.reopen_when: The completed candidate passes all three gates, exceeds degree ten for the pairing reduction, or supplies a new plane theorem.

lessons.title: Use the complete affine-W generating-function classification before dense cubic search
lessons.when: A ternary Gaussian polynomial is W*h(Z)+v(Z)*T^2+u(Z)*T+r(Z), including either h(0) chart.
lessons.use: Apply GL1, then integrate the scalar Gaussian quadratic. On h(0)!=0 rational-exponential rigidity forces (h-Z*hprime)^2*(h-2Z*v)=h^3 and 2*(h-2Z*v)*r+Z*u^2=0; the root argument forces h constant or linear. On h(0)=0 evaluate the fixed point at zero and retain the separate one-sided branch. In total degree D>=2, use the sufficient 5D-3 pure-moment gate; the quartic failure locus is exactly the linear repair k0+k1*Z.
lessons.avoid: Restarting the closed twelve-coefficient cubic architecture, treating a finite prefix as an all-order survivor, or promoting a convenient W-linear frame to an exhaustive ternary normal form.
lessons.boundary: The original height-two twelve-moment gate covers its stated architecture. The additional cubic-height Riccati theorem now closes T^3 as well, with a sufficient 35-moment cubic gate. Neither theorem normalizes general W-dependent coupling into the completed family.
lessons.reopen_when: The candidate contains omitted cubic terms or a new exact normalization theorem expands coverage.

lessons.avoid: Inferring trace-coordinate status from a Keller determinant alone, assuming the limiting pencil member is a coordinate without its Jacobian mate, omitting planes tangent to x=0, or treating bounded derivative checks as all-degree nilpotence.
lessons.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. lessons.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. The universal f_M model has relative projection K and vertical Hessian -DK^T*DK, while the finite-free Fermat construction gives every K a proper relative projection with explicit monomial basis and ramification at zero. Its properness is not properness of K. Neither model automatically supplies a compatible closed ambient embedding. The two plane endpoints and unrestricted graph compatibility remain open. Uniform quadratic two-planes now have the same unique-plane rigidity under nonautomorphy as affine ones: any genuinely quadratic constant two-plane or two distinct quadratic planes closes the candidate. This classifies every fibre-affine two-affine embedding j=(s,t,b+A*w) in all base degrees. Global source generation requires a polynomial left inverse of A; generic rank is not enough. Alignment follows under nonautomorphy, a rank-three helper quadratic closes unconditionally, and lower ranks force a base-only helper and the two old endpoints. All unit-Hessian members have at most one full critical point. Arbitrary nonlinear free helpers and nonaligned potentials of free degree at least three remain open. Nonlinear isotropic-ideal image graphs now have explicit global quadratic isometries to hyperplanes, with arbitrary coefficients in unchanged variables and all source parameterizations. Compatible positive linear ambient weights give a constructive recognition gate: a smooth invariant image either has an isotropic tangent normal forbidding unit Hessian, or its lower-weight nonlinear terms admit a weighted Euler shear to the nonisotropic hyperplane. Only the singleton-zero endpoint survives for these positive images. Actual positive linear source weights would close gradient invertibility, but image invariance alone does not supply that hypothesis after nonlinear source changes. Other nonlinear images and both plane endpoints remain open. The output-base gate now admits arbitrary degrees for both ambient observables: a smooth scheme-theoretic codimension-two complete intersection of their highest forms at infinity forces any carried Keller pair invertible. The leading regular sequence supplies a common filtered basis and height-one graded domains, while the explicitly imported smooth complete-intersection Picard theorem supplies generic factoriality. Generic factoriality alone and smooth reduced support do not suffice; Pi=(x,xy+z^2) has an exact denominator failure. Arbitrary extensions need not have the required leading forms. Singular, nonreduced or excess-dimensional infinity intersections and both plane endpoints remain open. Generic factoriality is now relaxed by HC4MYHW0/1: torsion-free abelian divisor-class monodromy suffices, since Keller function fields contain no nontrivial abelian Galois intermediate field and all conjugate component classes then become zero. Geometric integrality of affine height-one fibres suffices for global primitive saturation even with nonconstant fibre units or reducible graded rings. The earlier r=1 exclusion for nondegenerate linear-quadratic output pairs is removed by HC4MYHW2, without calling the quadric surface factorial; degenerate restricted-rank-at-least-three quadratics close too. HC4MYHW3 closes cyclic Danielewski output pairs in every power m>=2, including nonreduced ordinary leading schemes and generic nonfactoriality outside every older smooth-infinity frame in the HC4-size first type. HC4MYGZ0/1/2/3 now compare the exceptional base-zero fibre and close both entire positive-p base charts, including every opposite escape; both whole p-only families retain only the base-only unit-ideal nonautomorphic endpoint. For boundary orbits retain both P and r exponents of the intrinsic normalization Fitting divisor. Its fixed endpoints exclude puncture reversal uniformly even when the projected support is symmetric. More generally a positive weight vector only needs gcd one: a unimodular complement can be shifted by positive multiples of the weight column to make a polynomial monomial section. Weights6,10,15 demonstrate why no coprime pair is necessary.
lessons.avoid: Demanding consecutive surviving weights, importing a clean-torus gap pattern after coefficients vanish, or using a construction-specific stable-class defect as a lower bound for all universal maps. A root-free target quotient section is not a whole affine-space source; use UACTARGET1 and the exact UAPROFILE1 Laurent landing test before suppressing its poles.
lessons.boundary: The sextic section and complete-fibre universality work in every infinite characteristic other than two; stable orbit classification and the N-5 trace-family non-descent theorem are proved in characteristic zero. lessons.title: Use a critical-coordinate first jet to obtain a line-injective Keller endpoint
lessons.when: The full dual trace at one base point is H(a) for a coordinate a, and one base derivative modulo H_prime(a) is a nonzero constant multiple of its coordinate mate plus a polynomial in a.
lessons.use: Project a hypothetical affine two-plane to the base. Rank zero contradicts the nonlinear trace. Rank one yields a residual Keller map with a component divisible by a transverse base coordinate, so its zero line is mapped injectively. Rank two uses a root of H_prime and normalizes only the two-variable coefficient pair to expose an injective straight line. Apply the explicitly imported Gwozdziewicz theorem, then reconstruct the full cotangent gradient inverse. For Meng--Yang q use old x direction and mate r0; for r use old y direction and mate q0. HC4MYGB0/1/2 now close both native base-eliminated charts and complete all five native coordinate graphs; retain nonlinear reparameterizations of the two new charts as a distinct remaining scope. lessons.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism.
