lessons.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. The universal f_M model has relative projection K and vertical Hessian -DK^T*DK, while the finite-free Fermat construction gives every K a proper relative projection with explicit monomial basis and ramification at zero. Its properness is not properness of K. Neither model automatically supplies a compatible closed ambient embedding. The two plane endpoints and unrestricted graph compatibility remain open. Uniform quadratic two-planes now have the same unique-plane rigidity under nonautomorphy as affine ones: any genuinely quadratic constant two-plane or two distinct quadratic planes closes the candidate. This classifies every fibre-affine two-affine embedding j=(s,t,b+A*w) in all base degrees. Global source generation requires a polynomial left inverse of A; generic rank is not enough. Alignment follows under nonautomorphy, a rank-three helper quadratic closes unconditionally, and lower ranks force a base-only helper and the two old endpoints. All unit-Hessian members have at most one full critical point. Arbitrary nonlinear free helpers and nonaligned potentials of free degree at least three remain open. Nonlinear isotropic-ideal image graphs now have explicit global quadratic isometries to hyperplanes, with arbitrary coefficients in unchanged variables and all source parameterizations. Compatible positive linear ambient weights give a constructive recognition gate: a smooth invariant image either has an isotropic tangent normal forbidding unit Hessian, or its lower-weight nonlinear terms admit a weighted Euler shear to the nonisotropic hyperplane. Only the singleton-zero endpoint survives for these positive images. Actual positive linear source weights would close gradient invertibility, but image invariance alone does not supply that hypothesis after nonlinear source changes. Other nonlinear images and both plane endpoints remain open. The output-base gate now admits arbitrary degrees for both ambient observables: a smooth scheme-theoretic codimension-two complete intersection of their highest forms at infinity forces any carried Keller pair invertible. The leading regular sequence supplies a common filtered basis and height-one graded domains, while the explicitly imported smooth complete-intersection Picard theorem supplies generic factoriality. Generic factoriality alone and smooth reduced support do not suffice; Pi=(x,xy+z^2) has an exact denominator failure. Arbitrary extensions need not have the required leading forms. Singular, nonreduced or excess-dimensional infinity intersections and both plane endpoints remain open. Generic factoriality is now relaxed by HC4MYHW0/1: torsion-free abelian divisor-class monodromy suffices, since Keller function fields contain no nontrivial abelian Galois intermediate field and all conjugate component classes then become zero. Geometric integrality of affine height-one fibres suffices for global primitive saturation even with nonconstant fibre units or reducible graded rings. The earlier r=1 exclusion for nondegenerate linear-quadratic output pairs is removed by HC4MYHW2, without calling the quadric surface factorial; degenerate restricted-rank-at-least-three quadratics close too. HC4MYHW3 closes cyclic Danielewski output pairs in every power m>=2, including nonreduced ordinary leading schemes and generic nonfactoriality outside every older smooth-infinity frame in the HC4-size first type. lessons.title: Check stable centralizer capacity before deleting a canonical correction
lessons.when: A high-degree Hamiltonian correction is removed from a polynomial canonical pair in order to seek a lower-degree full symplectic or Weyl map.
lessons.use: Determine the full polynomial joint centralizer or a Poisson quotient that bounds its symplectic rank. For quantum candidates, a nonzero finite-dimensional polynomial eigenspace yields a matrix representation of the centralizer and a stable PBW-growth obstruction. Distinguish ordinary polynomial fiber translations from actual canonical changes; for the cubic Long core their shifts are canonical exactly for H in K[R]. For a Hamiltonian linear in momenta, scalar polynomial invariants of its base vector field give a Poisson character on the whole centralizer by zero-momentum evaluation.
lessons.avoid: Treating an exact canonical pair as automatically completable to a full frame, dropping Long's H while retaining R, assuming adding spectator pairs removes the fixed-core obstruction, or extending the resonant normal-order quantum statement to every ordering.
lessons.boundary: QCC1 excludes D0 as any component, and hence the fixed cubic pair (R,D0), globally in all polynomial degrees and under stabilization. It rules out a canonical normalization from corrected Long D to D0 even when R changes. Its quantum result applies to D0+(3*m/2)*h*q for nonnegative integer m via a finite eigenspace; the symmetric shift -9*h*q/4 is outside that family. Other cubic pairs with a genuinely different D, the corrected Long map and spatially rational or formal completions remain outside this exclusion. A zero or infinite eigenspace alone gives no quantum obstruction.

lessons.title: Certify arbitrary target-degree obstructions by finite source coefficient functionals
lessons.when: A graph-restricted Keller map has a raw higher-degree component to be repaired by a polynomial in the other raw outputs.
lessons.use: Seek a rational coefficient functional supported above the allowed source degree, nonzero on the defect, and zero on the raw-output algebra. Close its monomial support downward to form a finite quotient. Origin-vanishing generators imply target words above the support order vanish, so exact finite coverage certifies every polynomial target degree. Check the dual equations, all commutative words, zero-prefix coverage and a known successful completion independently.
lessons.avoid: Calling finite-jet membership a full polynomial completion; confusing a capped target-degree miss with an arbitrary-degree theorem; accepting producer rank assertions instead of checking the explicit functional; redoing larger raw target-degree bounds after a full algebra obstruction is certified.
lessons.boundary: KCUB4 independently closes all nine fixed KCUB3 carrier graph slices for one raw-output elementary correction of arbitrary degree. Support orders<=7 suffice. Initial small quotients and the capped adaptive run were inconclusive; the final result uses explicit independently verified separators. Other target sequences, source graphs and global minima remain open. KCUB28 gives the independently checked512-subset finite frontier including degree4/5/6 witnesses, without a global optimum claim. Do not rerun unchanged parameter or subset screens.
lessons.reopen_when: Change the source graph or level, or mix the obstructed component into another output before correction. Transformations confined to the other raw-output algebra cannot escape the certificate. Higher intermediate degrees or a new carrier realization remain admissible.

lessons.title: Keep exceptional torsion and full admission when transporting a quantum fiber pair

lessons.use: Rewrite R/2=x*(1+x*y), b=B/3 and theta=x^2*d_x-(1+2*x*y)*d_y. Reduce F*(4*y^2*dx+(2*x*y-1)*dy) by the complete weight normal form. Vanishing of the whole normal form is equivalent to a global polynomial primitive for the vertical correction and to extension of b to b+F as a full polynomial canonical map fixing x,y. This applies exactly to the quantum Ore algebra as well. For an admitted full Long lift, the quantum fiber translation b to b+h^N*F preserves admission exactly when the whole class vanishes. Maintain the fourth image and all full relations during correction; F=1 leaves the admissible locus at any selected N while preserving exact partial relations.
lessons.avoid: Replacing global primitive membership by vanishing generic periods, checking fibers individually, assuming smoothness gives torsion-free relative cohomology, or using an arbitrary fiber automorphism as a global canonical transformation. Arbitrarily long matching jets and the same classical reduction do not certify admission of a prescribed all-orders pair.
lessons.boundary: The relative H is D_r/D_r*(r*partial_r), with an exceptional delta submodule and quotient K[r]. The explicit classes y^n*d(1+x*y) have exact r-torsion order n and are invisible on every fiber. The criterion fixes the base positions and a vertical correction class. QGR1 supplies the sharp primitive bound once the correction has a common degree bound.

lessons.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. The universal f_M model has relative projection K and vertical Hessian -DK^T*DK, while the finite-free Fermat construction gives every K a proper relative projection with explicit monomial basis and ramification at zero. Its properness is not properness of K. Neither model automatically supplies a compatible closed ambient embedding. The two plane endpoints and unrestricted graph compatibility remain open. Uniform quadratic two-planes now have the same unique-plane rigidity under nonautomorphy as affine ones: any genuinely quadratic constant two-plane or two distinct quadratic planes closes the candidate. This classifies every fibre-affine two-affine embedding j=(s,t,b+A*w) in all base degrees. Global source generation requires a polynomial left inverse of A; generic rank is not enough. Alignment follows under nonautomorphy, a rank-three helper quadratic closes unconditionally, and lower ranks force a base-only helper and the two old endpoints. All unit-Hessian members have at most one full critical point. Arbitrary nonlinear free helpers and nonaligned potentials of free degree at least three remain open. Nonlinear isotropic-ideal image graphs now have explicit global quadratic isometries to hyperplanes, with arbitrary coefficients in unchanged variables and all source parameterizations. Compatible positive linear ambient weights give a constructive recognition gate: a smooth invariant image either has an isotropic tangent normal forbidding unit Hessian, or its lower-weight nonlinear terms admit a weighted Euler shear to the nonisotropic hyperplane. Only the singleton-zero endpoint survives for these positive images. Actual positive linear source weights would close gradient invertibility, but image invariance alone does not supply that hypothesis after nonlinear source changes. Other nonlinear images and both plane endpoints remain open. The output-base gate now admits arbitrary degrees for both ambient observables: a smooth scheme-theoretic codimension-two complete intersection of their highest forms at infinity forces any carried Keller pair invertible. The leading regular sequence supplies a common filtered basis and height-one graded domains, while the explicitly imported smooth complete-intersection Picard theorem supplies generic factoriality. Generic factoriality alone and smooth reduced support do not suffice; Pi=(x,xy+z^2) has an exact denominator failure. Arbitrary extensions need not have the required leading forms. Singular, nonreduced or excess-dimensional infinity intersections and both plane endpoints remain open. Generic factoriality is now relaxed by HC4MYHW0/1: torsion-free abelian divisor-class monodromy suffices, since Keller function fields contain no nontrivial abelian Galois intermediate field and all conjugate component classes then become zero. Geometric integrality of affine height-one fibres suffices for global primitive saturation even with nonconstant fibre units or reducible graded rings. The earlier r=1 exclusion for nondegenerate linear-quadratic output pairs is removed by HC4MYHW2, without calling the quadric surface factorial; degenerate restricted-rank-at-least-three quadratics close too. HC4MYHW3 closes cyclic Danielewski output pairs in every power m>=2, including nonreduced ordinary leading schemes and generic nonfactoriality outside every older smooth-infinity frame in the HC4-size first type. Nonabelian class actions, torsion, nonintegral height-one fibres, uncovered ranks and infinity schemes and both plane endpoints remain open. The nonabelian boundary is now narrower: HC4MYHX0/1 prove that a nowhere-critical polynomial parameter is relatively algebraically closed in the source field, using an explicit classical closed-polynomial import. A class action descending from a finite cover of that one parameter retains its full possibly nonabelian group under Keller base change, so the component classes become principal. This does not make all special parameter fibres irreducible or the whole Keller extension trivial. HC4MYHX2 closes every constant-coefficient nonconstant Danielewski P(z), with arbitrary root group, and every suspended T*Y+xy-B(T,z) with arbitrary two-variable B and all degrees. The earlier nonabelian-P(z) and suspended-coefficient escape proposals are retired. Genuinely two-parameter unsuspended monodromy, torsion, nonintegral height-one fibres, other missing filtrations and both plane endpoints remain open. lessons.use: Fix a generic scalar base and complete the nonzero direction row over that field only. The ambient A/B rows are independent. No primitive/unimodular direction row or global row inverse is required. For pure-r opposite graphs the entire critical scheme lies at zero base with Hessian -4*L*N^3*(r*R0)second; constant nonzero critical values force R0 constant or linear by a derivative polynomial argument. Tang then yields the known unit-ideal or singleton-zero necessary endpoint. lessons.title: Classify nonflat factor schemes through parameter Smith torsion, torus faces and positive-weight primary truncations
lessons.when: A simple polynomial moment ideal is pulled back through a nonflat factorization map and generic coordinate components may hide parameter-dependent embedded primes.
lessons.use: Prove the all-order generating ideal in a small balanced invariant ring first. Reconstruct the factor coefficient map exactly. On a zero-factor chart, compute complete PID relation matrices in every potentially nonzero homogeneous degree and strip only actual inverted parameter factors. Torsion diagonal factors identify noncoordinate associated primes. Use torus transitivity only on faces with independent weights, enumerate every residual face orbit, and certify its socle by exact ideal quotients. Compute positive-graded local torsion support; pure powers above that support yield primary components. A minimal-height associated-prime contradiction proves the full intersection without requiring a large expanded decomposition.
lessons.avoid: Transferring a primary decomposition through a nonflat factorization, assuming torus-invariant primes are coordinate on weight-dependent four-faces, using a resultant alone as a flatness certificate, confusing root-fiber colength12 with intrinsic torsion4, or inferring any full decomposition from a timed-out general primdec call.
lessons.boundary: The homogeneous binary-cubic four-coefficient scheme has five primary components, degree2 and nilradical index6. Its actual N=2 three-factor pullback has45 components over C, including18 noncoordinate primes, degree36 and nilradical index9. Coordinate-origin torsion length13 differs from the auxiliary scheme length1 and from all chosen primary quotient lengths. The all-order tail and45-way intersection are written proofs with exact Smith/socle/Hilbert inputs; they are not finite extrapolations or an expanded45-way replay. N=3,4 schemes and affine factors are not closed.
lessons.reopen_when: The N=3,4 coefficient geometry, additional constraints, positive characteristic or more factors changes the support/weight assumptions; do not rerun the closed N=2 primary, nilpotence and local-torsion tests.

lessons.use: Find two divisors over the same base divisor on which a candidate coefficient t has a scalar residue on one and a nonconstant residue on the other. QSO2 then excludes every finite scalar canonical pair of order at most two throughout the completed fiber image. The full formal position-image theorem also applies to deformed first images that remain positional.

lessons.title: Use an elliptic differential class on a nonproperness component to obstruct canonical polarizations
lessons.when: A generically finite polynomial symplectic map has an explicit nonproperness component and a cotangent or positional normalization is proposed, possibly after stabilization.
lessons.use: An ambient locally nilpotent Hamiltonian in the image induces an equivariant additive action on the output and must fix each nonproperness component. Compute the component equation's full Poisson centralizer via its generic level curve. For Long, Delta_r=V(A)+8*Delta/(5r) obstructs every algebraic primitive by a nonzero holomorphic elliptic differential, eliminating all positive conjugate degrees at once. The remaining genus-one orbits force locally nilpotent Hamiltonians into the first-coordinate and spectator algebra. Its Poisson rank bounds independent commuting directions to one below the number needed for a full positional form, in every stabilization.
lessons.avoid: Assuming a mixed target canonical change or more identity pairs can restore a cotangent form, using ordinary polynomial equivalence to transport a Weyl realization, replacing the nonzero elliptic differential class by nonisotriviality, or extending intrinsic local nilpotence from an image to the ambient ring without proof.
lessons.boundary: QHR1 excludes one full positional/cotangent normal form after arbitrary polynomial canonical source and target changes, even wild ones and every identity stabilization. It does not exclude every composition of several noninvertible cotangent factors interleaved with canonical maps. The regular formal quantum corollary assumes both changes and inverses have invertible polynomial classical reductions; parameter-pole changes are separate. The elliptic curves are isotrivial j=0, but the displayed class is nonzero. No theorem says every bounded Weyl lift must have a positional form. QEI1 gives the exact quantum source normalizer and explicit three-isogeny, but no bounded target carrier. Its forced discriminant order jump excludes retaining a quadratic energy even with unboundedly high finite partner orders. QCI1 gives a different rational quantum obstruction: for the fixed Long position field and every identity stabilization, no ambient L-linear Weyl division automorphism can make all positions rational coordinate functions, with no regularity or pole bound on that target automorphism. It uses completed degree and centralizer saturation, not local nilpotence. Arbitrary mixed source changes are not covered by this rational extension. QCI1 exhibits a rational family whose source exchange redistributes centralizer degree and residual index. Its fixed-position qualification cannot be dropped. A separate bounded-powers test excludes finite lattices for that displayed rational family under polynomial source/target Weyl automorphisms and identity padding; it is not an exclusion of every mixed source position field for Long. QGD1 gives a full-image rational invariant independent of a position choice: no ambient finite division-automorphism group can have the Long image as its fixed ring, even with h poles or valuation movement. The obstruction transports through all L-linear rational source/target division changes and identity padding. It closes finite symmetry quotients, not every rational canonical form, larger Galois-closure/subgroup constructions or nonsymmetric bounded lifts.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual bounded full noncotangent carrier is constructed, a parameter-pole transformation is controlled, or a new invariant applies directly to higher-order nonpositional Weyl images rather than seeking a forbidden cotangent form.

lessons.title: Use independent pure-trace directions to recover or exclude the unique residual cotangent plane

lessons.use: First use elementary uniqueness: two distinct constant jointly affine two-planes force gradient invertibility. For hypothetical nonautomorphy Tang supplies one plane, and the pure whole-trace normals are exactly its two-dimensional annihilator. Three independent normals close the candidate regardless of signs. Two normals fix the plane and reduce the next action to its three directional second-derivative identities. Passing all three leaves the exact plane Keller cotangent problem; universal two-direction closure is equivalent to JC2. Complete parallel profiles count the reduced residual origin fibre; n+1 nonparallel quotient profiles recover its n points, and linear potential perturbations give other target-fibre profiles. HC4MYHG0/1 now use full critical schemes, critical Hessian values and entire value fibres to survive every polynomial source automorphism. Zero-boundary base graphs and split one-variable degrees at least three cannot acquire unit Hessian after any full source mixing. HC4MYHG2 identifies all full-source base-only graph orbits and the fixed degree-six p graph with the existing coordinate/unit-ideal and quadratic/singleton-zero endpoints. No new graph-degree or source-word search is warranted inside those full orbits, and neither endpoint is solved. HC4MYHH0/1 now normalize arbitrary finite reduced coefficient fibres by local orientation and three determinant-one base shears. Every nonautomorphic finite-critical cotangent candidate is right-equivalent to the explicit degree n+1 inverse-derivative template. HC4MYHH2 identifies full-source unitization for n>=2 with one relative SL2 row equation, without solving it or producing a graph embedding. All reference templates already meet the fixed-function critical/Hodge necessary conditions, so future work needs a global row/properness or embedding restriction rather than another such invariant or native-degree sweep. HC4MYHI0/1 now apply the classical global single-generator Keller criterion: one common extra reconstruction polynomial forces an inverse, while hypothetical nonautomorphic HC4 requires exactly two relative generators. HC4MYHI2 closes every embedded realization of the exact universal A=F, B=xF+yG encoding, regardless of the remaining dual function. HC4MYHI3 closes all target-dependent affine-dual output-base embeddings, including rank drops away from the image. These are genuine all-degree embedding obstructions, not a solution of the unrestricted row equation or a statement that every graph has the required global reconstruction. Disjoint constant-unit conjugate hypersurfaces form one polynomial pencil; primitive nonconstant coefficient content removes the target denominators, and smoothness makes the relation derivative a scalar unit and forces generic degree one. Thus (K(z),H(z,w)) cannot be a closed hypersurface embedding for nonautomorphic K, for arbitrary source-dependent nonlinear H. Changing only matrix descent, dual degree or embedded fibre shape is no longer a remaining direction. The exact stable additional-generator minimum is r+2, and the intrinsic cotangent pair cannot extend to ambient coordinates in A5. Arbitrary graph embeddings need not have that physical-base interpretation. HC4MYHK0/1 now make the mixed-projection boundary exact: for k linear outputs, ell their intersection dimension with the cotangent pair, the additional-generator minimum is N-k+ell under nonautomorphy. The pure-one-component lower bound uses the classical plane stable-coordinate implication; the full-pair lower bound is HC4MYHJ1. All other A5 completions are explicit source-recovery constructions, so embedding existence alone cannot close them. Keep the fixed potential identity and marked covector transfer separate. HC4MYHL0/1 now use the fixed-potential common-zero-base trace to close every rank-one mixed gradient realization, while preserving the correct abstract embedding classification. Check four affine-linear retained normal projections before further degree work. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. lessons.title: Demand global reconstruction and exclude exact cotangent or output-base encoding upgrades before increasing degrees
lessons.when: A universal plane Keller substitution is proposed as a genuine graph embedding, or an ambient hypersurface encoding is meant to carry the gradient outputs with one remaining coordinate.
lessons.use: Reproduce the classical single-generator theorem from the hypersurface relation: vanishing relative differentials make its T derivative a polynomial unit, hence a scalar, and characteristic zero makes the relation linear. Thus one global additional reconstruction polynomial over Keller outputs forces an inverse. In the exact A=F, B=xF+yG encoding, a single physical fibre gives (F,G-4F,h), closing every embedded nonautomorphic upgrade in arbitrary degree. For j=(K(z),M(K(z))*w+v(z)), the smooth closed image hypersurface has dual normal equal to a unit scalar times the target matrix cross product; the strict dual-degree comparison makes it linear and forces birational, hence invertible, K. The proof allows target rank drops away from the source image. HC4MYHJ0/1 remove every restriction on the dual map over a fixed plane Keller output base. Disjoint constant-unit conjugate hypersurfaces form one polynomial pencil; primitive nonconstant coefficient content removes the target denominators, and smoothness makes the relation derivative a scalar unit and forces generic degree one. Thus (K(z),H(z,w)) cannot be a closed hypersurface embedding for nonautomorphic K, for arbitrary source-dependent nonlinear H. Changing only matrix descent, dual degree or embedded fibre shape is no longer a remaining direction. The exact stable additional-generator minimum is r+2, and the intrinsic cotangent pair cannot extend to ambient coordinates in A5. Arbitrary graph embeddings need not have that physical-base interpretation. HC4MYHK0/1 now make the mixed-projection boundary exact: for k linear outputs, ell their intersection dimension with the cotangent pair, the additional-generator minimum is N-k+ell under nonautomorphy. The pure-one-component lower bound uses the classical plane stable-coordinate implication; the full-pair lower bound is HC4MYHJ1. All other A5 completions are explicit source-recovery constructions, so embedding existence alone cannot close them. Keep the fixed potential identity and marked covector transfer separate. Noncoordinate directional derivatives also identify exactly the unique cotangent plane. HC4MYHL0/1 now use the fixed-potential common-zero-base trace to close every rank-one mixed gradient realization, while preserving the correct abstract embedding classification. The free eta coefficient is (-Q_s*P+P_s*Q)/J, and nonlinear composite degree makes P divide P_s, forcing a triangular pair. Only the full-eta-rank centered gradient-base stratum survives. HC4MYHL2 adds the exact distinguished-critical-value transfer and a global necessary Euler square equation, neither of which is a properness proof or a completed embedding. HC4MYHM0/1/2 now straighten the entire ambient function to lambda_star+L*T^2+N*y*Z+2*N*x*W with an explicit polynomial inverse. Every literal graph in every constant affine direction is closed under unit Hessian by the quadratic-plus-one-square or ternary quadratic trace criterion. Check four affine-linear retained normal projections before further degree work. Preserve the actual source parameterization: full source orbits of two fixed normal graphs already contain exactly the two unresolved plane endpoints. The transverse square equation alone is not universally obstructive because constant noncritical D always passes it. HC4MYHN0/1 now lower the ambient affine projection gate from four to three, including all degenerate quadratic kernels and fully nonlinear remaining coordinates. Restricted source planes expose one-extra-generator Keller recovery, while the other cases give a triangular component or affine-line fibre. There is a genuine unit-Hessian example with exactly three affine retained projections, so this strengthens the graph theorem. Two-affine normal embeddings already realize both distinct conditional endpoints with actual polynomial inverses, and no full two-affine closure or JC2 equivalence is claimed. HC4MYHO0/1/2 now separate complete endpoint branches in the two-affine geometry: a unit two-directional-partial ideal forces a unique vertical cotangent plane and an explicit relative coordinate; aligned nondegenerate kernel rank three is exactly the unit-ideal endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal image types are classified under arbitrary source reparameterizations into the old singleton-zero/coordinate orbits or a forbidden critical-line case. New directions beyond those endpoints require nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces. No unaligned two-affine closure or singleton uniqueness from mere attainment is claimed. HC4MYHP0/1 now require checking the whole polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation, since explicit genuine nonlinear images can have zero affine pullbacks while their unchanged source potential is a closed quadratic. HC4MYHQ0/1 enlarge the output-base obstruction to linear-quadratic ambient observables through a global quadric filtration, without requiring ambient coordinate completion or fibre rectification. HC4MYHR0/1 now test relative critical sections and curve products and classify every base-only quadratic graph under unrestricted relative free-variable automorphisms, without alignment and with at most one full critical point under unit Hessian. HC4MYHS0/1/2 add a one-component proper-Morse closure and exact universal JC2 boundaries for the two separate conditions, with an explicit arbitrary-dimensional finite-free monomial-basis construction. HC4MYHT0/1 add uniform quadratic-plane rigidity and the entire fibre-affine two-affine embedding classification, with alignment forced and all base matrix degrees unrestricted. HC4MYHU0/1 now rectify isotropic-ideal image graphs explicitly and classify every compatible positive-weight invariant image into the singleton orbit or a degenerate critical-point obstruction, without assuming equivariance in actual source coordinates. HC4MYHV0/1 now test arbitrary-degree ambient output observables by a global filtered criterion and a smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection at infinity, with the Picard input explicit. HC4MYHW0/1 replace factoriality by torsion-free abelian divisor-class monodromy and replace height-one graded domains by geometrically integral affine fibres; HC4MYHW2/3 close r=1 quadric pairs, specified degenerate ranks and all cyclic Danielewski powers. HC4MYHX0/1 preserve arbitrary finite monodromy descending from a regular polynomial parameter; HC4MYHX2 closes all constant-coefficient Danielewski P(z) and every T*Y+xy-B(T,z) suspension in every degree, beyond the earlier abelian class-action gate. HC4MYHY0/1 now close normal finite monogenic root covers and every monic two-parameter Danielewski output by root transitivity; HC4MYHY2 imposes a global nonmonogenicity gate on every nontrivial finite Keller normalization. HC4MYHZ0/1/2 supply the finite leading-fibre gate and independent abelian-root gate for nonmonic outputs, with exact localized-unit defect. HC4MYIA0/1/2 upgrade the unconditional nonmonic gate to finite nilpotent root/class groups and arbitrary common-prime radical depth. HC4MYIB0/1/2 add arbitrary Galois-intermediate exclusion, the exact global normalization-boundary basis, and subnormal class-stabilizer closure beyond nilpotent actions. HC4MYIC0/1/2 add combined leading-order factor divisibility, rational-label critical-curve geometry and new unrestricted-parameter S3 cubic closures. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons.avoid: Replacing global algebra generation by field generation, generic-chart recovery or monogenic zero-fibre data; inferring relative generator count from five ambient versus four gradient coordinates; dropping closed embedding, characteristic zero or the source-unit condition; calling the classical Formanek criterion new; treating the exact two-generator minimum as an absolute embedding dimension; applying the target-descended matrix argument to a source-dependent or nonlinear dual map.
lessons.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. lessons.title: Test energy-constrained quantization by relative elliptic cohomology before enlarging supports
lessons.when: An elliptic-isogeny quantization is proposed to preserve a cubic energy, reparametrize it by a univariate rational series, or deform a curve differential module through a central reduction.
lessons.use: Separate the flat algebra deformation from the map deformation. The Hamiltonian Ore algebra has a flat two-parameter PBW family and a localized Weyl central reduction. For the actual normalized three-isogeny, linearize the commutator as a divergence equation and the energy relation as a prescribed Hamiltonian derivative. Rational logarithmic gauges fixing b remove first-order tangential changes. On the generic elliptic level, the second-order compatibility class is -5/(72*b^2)*[x dx/y], independent of every univariate energy correction. Therefore the natural-energy commutator must appear at h order2 or3, exactly3 for even lifts, in every rational spatial degree. Use the explicit unrestricted escape jet to check that energy motion, rather than formal lifting itself, is being obstructed.
lessons.avoid: Inferring a nonlifting theorem from a fixed-energy obstruction, keeping the energy in its old centralizer while only raising partner orders, treating a flat deformation of algebras as a deformation of their isogeny module, assuming a rational logarithmic gauge has bounded degree, or extending the arbitrary-first-order rational theorem to every algebraic coefficient cover without proof.
lessons.boundary: The theorem uses the normalized rational Moyal fiber and applies to exact-R full formal Long lifts after scalar parameter rescaling. It imposes no common spatial or scalar-order bound, but does not cover nonpositional R deformations or target changes moving the distinguished energy. The second-order class survives finite algebraic fiber covers; the full parity-free theorem is stated only for rational coefficients. Formal pairs exist by unrestricted homotopy and escape via genuinely transverse energy corrections. The flat diagonal central reduction does not construct a compatible module map, the fourth image, or global admission. QPL1 is an explicit full polynomial-coefficient formal Long lift with all six relations, fixed momentum orders0,2,3,5 and a scalar quadratic energy. Its PI coefficients have unbounded spatial support and lie outside the generic algebraic coefficient category. Thus full global admission and finite scalar orders do not remove that field hypothesis. Its S coefficient degrees8n-1 prove growth of this family, not of every formal representative. QGD1 adds an independent constraint on a noncentral-energy bridge: its full Long division image cannot be a finite ambient symmetry fixed ring, even when symmetries move the parameter valuation. Energy motion remains necessary by QEM1 but does not establish finite admission. An S3 Galois closure with an intermediate subgroup-fixed source is not excluded by this direct-quotient theorem. QGC1 requires no exact quantum energy relation and now no original saturation under graph or equivariant admission. Ordinary-parameter identified graph actions admit a finite full valuation-level residue lattice. At arbitrary parameter order, an equivariant quadratic closure with the correct torsion-free special rank is repaired by two central parameter shifts and is excluded by interior ramification. Energy motion still does not establish finite admission. Direct nonsymmetric carriers and matrix actions outside the natural division closure remain open. QRA1 makes b noncentral by adjoining an explicit surface Euler connection and gives a global logarithmic model, but x,y remain commuting coefficient positions. This is not the QEM1 physical isogeny pair with [y,x]=h. Energy noncentrality alone therefore does not provide the missing compatible map. An exact primitive Y=XW with the physical Weyl pair would force X to be a unit; the special norm -4b prevents it globally. Broken quantum primitive relations remain a distinct possible escape. QFR1 gives a punctual physical-plane obstruction distinct from QEM1 generic elliptic de Rham nonexactness. QUR1 excludes all ramified regular lifts of that single monic normalization via a rank-two connection, even with changed energy and primitive. Neither excludes the ordinary rank-one forward Long graph.
lessons.reopen_when: A candidate supplies transverse quantum energy motion and all admitted full images with a common spatial bound, or an all-order relative-cohomology argument excludes every such bounded energy deformation under stated global hypotheses.

lessons.title: Reduce the whole torus-curvette sector before tackling characteristic gcd chains
lessons.when: A smooth affine one-line K=R plane completion has regular-coordinate order r>=2 and complementary pole q coprime to r, or a quartic iterated-knot cover has irreducible atoroidal source and marked exterior with primitive odd cyclic homology. This also applies when r divides q and the largest support index j not divisible by r is coprime to r, including all prime r.
lessons.use: Take the actual Laurent charts, choose Bezout toric coordinates, and prove full omitted-line contact m=q-r+2 with the reference jet. Keep the puncture through R6 and the m free blowups: the end is (qr+m)-surgery on T(q,r), with primitive dual knot, atoroidal closed source and atoroidal exterior. Nonzero central-fiber homology, prime decomposition and Poincare give actual radial irreducibility; peripheral Waldhausen then identifies the filled pair. In the quartic proof replace the lens requirement by closed atoroidality. Repeated original cone factors obstruct a primitive regular fiber for every third filling. Use homology-preserving replacements without a distance-one requirement on the original nonlens filling. The last trefoil patterns have homology order at most three. Construct all coprime monomial geometric controls with the four-generator root ring and verify their explicit Euler volume primitive. For an integral leading power subtract the finite polynomial part of w=1/h(z); its first nonintegral exponent is beta=2q-j and its actual variation has k=j-r+2 free blowups. Track the original deleted boundary at its earlier internal attachment. The resulting (r*beta+k)-surgery has both atoroidality properties and excludes this whole sector. This closes every prime r and the entire free translation sector r=2.
lessons.avoid: Discarding lower Laurent terms when locating free centers; identifying a closed small-Seifert space from group or H1 alone; assuming nonzero Euler number is irrelevant to horizontal tori; retaining the old lens-only proof at a nonlens source; discarding a third cone without a replacement argument; inferring target equivariance from a source torus action; calling affine controls finite maps; or extending the new topological order threshold to three, where an actual (3,8)-cable countercontrol exists.

The end formula, marked torus-infinity/prime-boundary restrictions, entire monomial affine controls and regular primitive are all-degree structure. lessons.boundary: All earlier three-affine and ambient quadratic obstructions remain valid. Two directional partials generating the global unit ideal now force their unique plane to be the cotangent plane, give a globally affine free-variable form and an explicit relative coordinate inverse. The aligned rank-three quadratic kernel branch is exactly the unit-ideal plane endpoint. All affine-hyperplane normal images, under arbitrary source parameterizations, are exactly the singleton-zero orbit, the unit-ideal coordinate orbit, or the isotropic-through-center critical-line branch that forbids unit Hessian. Neither endpoint is resolved. Rank-one aligned fibre attainment is not singleton uniqueness; unaligned two-affine embeddings and nonlinear normal image hypersurfaces remain open with the unrestricted row equation. Polynomial quadratic-similitude saturation is now an additional global gate: if q composed with an ambient polynomial automorphism is a*q, undo it in the same source parameters before classifying retained projections or hyperplane images. The entire saturated three-affine class stays closed; the full-source hyperplane saturation retains exactly the old two endpoints or critical-line obstruction. Explicit unbounded words give zero affine pullbacks and nonlinear image equations while preserving a unit-Hessian quadratic source potential. Raw image nonlinearity is therefore insufficient. No universal rectification or generation of every quadratic symmetry is asserted. The output-base obstruction now includes a linear observable paired with any nondegenerate ambient quadratic, not only ambient coordinate pairs. In all stable dimensions r>=2, generic quadric factoriality and a height-one-compatible monomial filtration make the pencil and denominator arguments global, and smoothness forces the plane Keller base invertible. Thus an intrinsic nonautomorphic cotangent pair cannot have such an ambient extension, even after a certified ambient polynomial automorphism. Direct native A/B encodings of an independent Keller pair collapse to an invertible pair and a coordinate potential. Both plane endpoints and arbitrary other source-pair extensions remain open; no surface-quadric factoriality or embedding rectification is assumed. Relative critical schemes now give a separate global gate. A polynomial section over a constant two-variable base, or a base-compatible smooth curve times A1 with vertical Hessian rank one, forces gradient invertibility under unit Hessian. Consequently every base-only normal graph j=(s,t,h(s,t),H,G) under arbitrary relative free-variable polynomial automorphisms has at most one full critical point under unit Hessian, with no cotangent alignment. Its nonautomorphic members are exactly the two old endpoint source orbits. Native graph members with multiple full critical points have no relative unitization over that fixed base. Arbitrary four-variable source mixing and three genuinely free-dependent unretained coordinates remain open. One proper relative Morse component now suffices: no condition on other components is needed, and a globally proper everywhere-Morse relative projection can only have degree one. Each nonautomorphic component must therefore fail properness or contain vertical degeneracy. However each single condition separately retains exactly JC2. lessons.title: Use the affine Newton filtration of the Gaussian-subtracted phase and retain the rescaling Jacobian
lessons.when: A homogeneous cubic has a noncoercive singular direction, while subtracting its nondegenerate Gaussian quadratic gives a convenient Newton-nondegenerate affine polynomial.
lessons.use: Normalize the nodal binary cubic before checking its outer faces, retaining the full transformed metric. Use the affine Newton filtration theorem on f=P-Q and the actual volume-form membership in V_alpha. A rational constant seed functional extends to an analytic horizontal functional without a cyclicity or convergence assumption. Under x=z/t, lambda=t^-2, the volume scales by t^-3; a constant Gaussian series would force volume evaluation lambda^-3/2. A Newton volume degree strictly below3/2 excludes this through regular-singular growth. Review isotropic nodes separately with the existing nondegenerate W-conic theorem.
lessons.avoid: Using spectral-multiset equality without volume-form filtration membership, confusing affine convenience with Laurent-torus convenience, dropping the rescaling Jacobian, imposing only generic Newton nondegeneracy, applying a Gaussian covariance normalization as if it preserved the metric, leaving mixed binary cubic terms on the outer face, or assuming that a formally divergent Gaussian exponential defines the original real integral.

lessons.when: The cubic leading curve is irreducible nodal, its node is Gaussian-nonisotropic, and the quadratic part vanishes at that node.
lessons.use: Normalize P=T*(uv+h)+a*u^3+d*v^3+b*u^2+c*v^2+e*u+f*v+k while retaining the full affine Gaussian exponent. A simple projective gradient intersection at infinity gives affine length7. Count finite P-critical Milnor numbers, construct escaping branches by exact Puiseux rescaling and the implicit function theorem, and use the total length to prove exhaustiveness. For h=0, e!=0, the lowest nonconstant v degree j determines n=j+2 escapes, all with nonzero t^(2/n) action after subtracting k*t. Check the Hessian and local Gaussian scale. Complete the T square before assessing conic Gaussian width; the compact chart has limiting Phi_ss=1/m.
lessons.avoid: Inferring a complete sectorial period splitting from a critical-point count, applying fixed-phase convergence as a uniform parameter bound, discarding the full Gaussian metric or mean after affine changes, forgetting the common k*t before extracting a fractional action, equating Morse points with distinct critical values, or treating stable width on compact u as an endpoint bound. Preserve the initial determinant-sign and action-extraction failures.

lessons.title: Classify finite-momentum formal fixed-R gauges and keep the unbounded-momentum comparison open
lessons.when: Comparing a putative bounded exact-R Long lift with QPL1, extending a formal centralizer gauge to its fourth image, or testing whether the Euler connection forces the PI form.
lessons.use: Use multiplicative operator order in X*(1+X*Y)=r to force finite-order position images to remain positional. Factor them with f in h*K[x,y][[h]], compute the formal-unit Jacobian j, and write the centralizer image as j^-1*b+F. Full extension and fourth-image admission are equivalent to global coefficientwise exactness j*F=theta(G). All finite b orders are preserved in this category. The unique formal comparison with a bounded exact-R target must therefore have unbounded momentum in a position image. Use the global Hamiltonian H=I^2, I=(X^3*w+w*X^3)/2, as a control: its arbitrary-contact flow fixes R and K exactly but has unbounded momentum.
lessons.avoid: Extending QGR1 position-fixing rigidity from finite spatial support to all formal gauges, assuming exact R and K force finite momentum, or using one unbounded transported frame as all-representative nonlifting.
lessons.boundary: The full classification assumes both position images have uniformly finite momentum order, but allows unbounded position degree and puts no initial bound on b. The necessary momentum escape concerns bounded exact-R targets; nonpositional first images are outside it. The invariant flows themselves give unbounded frames, not bounded candidates or counterexamples to a bounded-target-specific theorem. Universal statements have written proofs and finite exact controls, without independent or external review. QPG1 compares unrestricted full formal lifts by a finite exact polynomial shear word followed by an inner formal unit; inner conjugacy alone is equivalent to agreement modulo t*a(t). Its intermediate shear words need not fix R, and its inner unit can have unbounded spatial and momentum support. It preserves existence of a good formal-module algebraization, not the raw momentum bounds of a representative or the fixed-R hypotheses here.
lessons.reopen_when: A property of an actual bounded target controls its unique comparison beyond the finite-momentum category, an invariant survives unbounded-momentum formal transport with the full boundary lattice, or a bounded full carrier is constructed.

lessons.title: Use finite-left full graph descent before requiring a scalar free frame
lessons.when: An algebraic full quantum graph carrier is sought but its rank-one free frame is unresolved, or a finite projective corner is proposed as a substitute for full right actions.
lessons.use: Require a finite-left R-flat h-Weyl bimodule with the identified classical graph, not just a coherent bimodule or formally free left completion. Generic projectivity follows from the cited finite-left bimodule lemma and the classical presentation forces rank one. Use a nonzero algebraic dual section to transport the rational right action: it has the same residue map and completed degree delta. Left and dual growth filtrations bound both finite generic indices below by delta. Stafford stabilization makes two copies free, so delta>1 forces a non-surjective Mat_2(A_n) endomorphism. A finite idempotent with admitted corner generators and scalar graph reduction is an explicit sufficient certificate. Test compression defects before claiming those generators satisfy Weyl relations. Use QPG1 central patching after proving generic finite projectivity and an admitted C-frame; if the generic module is rank-one free, its integral frame follows automatically. For generic rank-one full actions, QVA1 now supplies C-admission from Gauss-regularity and the intended shadow; it need not be assumed separately.
lessons.avoid: Treating a matrix result as a scalar A_n endomorphism, requiring a scalar frame before recognizing progress from an actual full algebraic carrier, assuming projectivity supplies a right action, substituting central curve energy for noncentral Weyl data, or applying prescribed arithmetic-support nonlifting from classical reduction alone.
lessons.boundary: This is a carrier criterion and a matrix realization theorem, not a constructed Long carrier. The scalar route retains its generic or parameter-compatible rank-one frame gate. Generic projectivity uses Kanel-Belov-Fedorov Lemma3.1 without its separate arithmetic-support hypothesis; generic two-copy freeness uses Stafford Theorem3.6. Neither external theorem is independently replayed. Finite-left carrier generation does not imply finite generation of the different valuation lattice governing equality of generic and completed division degree. The positive control is the identity graph; the QPF1 compression is a negative control. QPH1 constructs a full finite two-by-two phase representation but its left rank is two, not QMC1 rank one, and its second classical branch has an X=0 pole. Its phase form has no algebraic branch summand for any nonconstant finite polynomial g_h, by absolute irreducibility of a nonsingular polynomial connection; the original quadratic case also has a weighted order2/3 proof. Formal extraction gives a second global Long lift with exact S coefficient degree10n-1 and momentum order n. A linear-g example has a different finite scalar realization despite phase nonsplitting, so this excludes the chosen phase construction, not every algebraization or full quantum representative. QFT1 extends the phase exclusion to every minimal rational pre-Fourier line with h-regular coefficient and classical polynomial degree at least three, including logarithmic amplitudes and moving rational poles. Its one-puncture monodromy criterion is uniform over all finite covers in rank at least three. A true rank-two split and generic-rank-two/formal-rank-one degeneration mark the boundary: higher generic pre-Fourier rank and separately audited nonminimal constituents remain possible. No actual Long carrier follows. QKR1 supplies an all-rank cyclic-cover budget r>=(1-1/e)N+irr_0; N>2r excludes cyclic power splitting and, with one finite puncture, all finite covers. Boundary delta factors add inverse-Fourier rank. A genuinely splitting all-degree family S=g(a)+2v has inverse rank deg(g)+1, but its quadratic Long branch fails QSO2. QVM1 excludes every finite mate, on all finite coefficient covers, when S has v-leading term v*H(a), deg H>=2 and root-multiplicity gcd one, with arbitrary lower-growth terms. The candidate v*(2+h*a^3)+4a-3r*a^2 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction but fails this all-order mate test. Proper-power H, different leading faces and nonpositional first images remain outside it. No actual Long carrier follows. QVL1 transports repeated roots to nonlinear ordinary infinity limits and closes all proper-power v-linear repairs when lower coefficients are bounded. Together with QVM1, every leading H of degree>=2 is excluded in that entire Laurent class, with arbitrary finite partner order and algebraic coefficient covers. Euler limits and finite Newton support certificates give further tests. A remaining exact-R scalar Long model in the v-linear rational Laurent class has H degree<=1 and inverse-Fourier rank at least four, by QSO2 and a positive infinity Newton contribution. The family 2v*(1+h*a)^k+4a-3ra^2 is excluded for every k>=2, even though k3 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction. Nonlinear-limit commuting Darboux algebras cannot supply a scalar generator, but other operators in larger idealizers remain outside that assertion. Other leading faces, fractional positive lower growth for nonprimitive H, H degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. QZM1 gives a zero-mode cokernel test with finite-cover trace retraction and covariance under actual finite algebra automorphisms, provided the module is transported too. A new position localization can kill the vector and is not justified by trace. It excludes v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a) for every nonconstant polynomial G and every finite scalar mate order or algebraic coefficient cover. Combined with QVL1, the pure separable class v*H(a)+G(a) with both H and G nonconstant is closed; the leading-linear rank-four cubic and derivative-tuned cubic are excluded. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant nonlinear-G case by a universal p-power coefficient. The complete pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long form is therefore excluded, including every finite momentum degree and coefficient cover. Additional negative-v corrections, genuine mixed coefficients, other leading faces and deformed first images remain outside this classification. Conditional global pair transport clears c(R) and requires [R,T]=0; it neither admits every chart formula nor identifies QRF2 with this new class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. QGC1 now excludes the natural larger Long closure with the intended admission without assuming saturation. The ordinary-parameter classical graph gives finite full valuation-level lattices. For a finite group closure with special rank delta and no S-torsion, generic rank comparison forces group order delta and valuation invariance; split characters then give a finite saturated repair. QIR1 upgrades generic to integral projectivity for every parameter order and makes the finite normalized corner equations necessary and sufficient for a full graph carrier. One elementary stabilization normalizes the special idempotent without a formal inverse. In a fixed rational action there is only one generic full finite lattice; rank-one integral graph models differ by central powers. No Long corner or scalar free frame is supplied. QTC1 composes actual finite corners by entrywise block substitution, with product matrix size and degree bound. Generic indices and completed degrees multiply, so strict index excess cannot cancel. A carrier dual is finite on the target right side; composing over the source need not stay finite on the target left. Full generator relations in a larger matrix algebra alone are therefore not a QMC1 counterexample. The global monic elliptic A2 action is an explicit rank3 control. QVA1 gives an exact generic construction gate: finite projective rank-one full action plus Gauss-regular intrinsic Long shadow. Its valuation-ideal proof produces C-freeness and QPG1 supplies the integral finite carrier. Generic rank-one freeness gives the scalar lift; generic nonfreeness retains the matrix result. lessons.title: Keep Laurent coefficient powers outside polynomial-only source substitution

lessons.use: Make the coefficient-ring boundary explicit: keep every Laurent parameter exponent untouched and apply polynomial substitution only to source variables with nonnegative powers. Check equality to a complete independently known diagonal or source-normalization identity. lessons.avoid: Using a nonnegative-power loop as a Laurent substitution engine: negative powers may silently become one. A passing normalization after such a projection is weaker than the intended rational identity. Do not overwrite all older validation receipts merely to audit this domain boundary, or infer every repository checker is covered by a seven-module audit.
lessons.boundary: The new KCUB19 diagonal-conjugacy comparison caught the misuse before its pass and now specializes s=t0 by coefficient filtering. A seven-module read-only domain audit then found one additional misuse in KCUB18 core source normalization; selective u,v substitution now preserves beta denominators, the full checker passes, and all seven audited modules pass with zero domain failures. Original failures and the previous KCUB18 receipt are retained. KCUB18 mathematical scope and all construction bounds remain unchanged; the shared utility and other older theorem sources were not edited.
lessons.reopen_when: Another checker passes Laurent input to a polynomial-only helper, or the coefficient/source split or helper implementation changes. Extend the explicit audit scope before claiming further coverage.

lessons.title: Use uniform gradient carriers and integral-current limits to control a nonisolated Gaussian critical line
lessons.when: A polynomial Gaussian phase has a parameter-uniform complex gradient lower bound outside one fixed ball, while its leading phase has a nonisolated critical set.
lessons.use: Transport local vanishing cycles along independently chosen decaying phase cuts; the gradient bound gives radius squared<=A+B*s with no parameter factor. Apply compatible Hardt triviality to the compactified constrained cut-pair diagram to obtain one jointly semialgebraic flat basis. Coordinate-minor area bounds and uniform finite fibers control masses and boundary masses. On a fixed band the phase equation forces current limits into a proper complex level set, annihilating the holomorphic top form. Integral-current compactness and uniform tails prove normalized period decay. A supporting ray for all finite critical values then rules out a constant Gaussian period without formal block splitting.
lessons.avoid: Replacing uniform coercivity by bounded critical points, claiming the gradient flow is semialgebraic, selecting unrelated chains separately at each parameter, ignoring boundary-mass bounds needed for rectifiable current compactness, claiming real chain volume must tend to zero, assuming a generic t-angle is available when opposite actions require a boundary ray, or using a homogeneous theorem after affine changes have shifted the Gaussian mean.

lessons.title: Test linear-quadratic ambient output extensions using filtered quadric rings before attempting fibre rectification
lessons.when: A genuine stable hypersurface embedding carries a plane Keller output pair through an ambient linear and nondegenerate quadratic observable, or a direct native A/B encoding is proposed.
lessons.use: Normalize the two inverse-metric normal types. A monic hyperbolic relation gives a free normal-monomial basis and an additive degree filtration over the generic field and each height-one residue field. Generic factoriality follows from elimination in the isotropic type and a prime-coordinate Laurent localization with Nagata criterion in the nonisotropic type. Disjoint generic affine-space components then form a Galois-descended pencil. Primitive coefficient valuations clear denominators globally; smoothness and DK invertibility force the label-relation derivative constant and degree one. The plane Keller base is invertible. This extends the coordinate-pair obstruction without rectifying any quadric embedding. HC4MYHR0/1 now test relative critical sections and curve products and classify every base-only quadratic graph under unrestricted relative free-variable automorphisms, without alignment and with at most one full critical point under unit Hessian.
