lessons.use: Write the leading infinity term v*H(a). If deg H>=2 and its root multiplicities have gcd one, no finite mate exists over any finite algebraic coefficient curve, with arbitrary order and poles. Leading Puiseux exponents force finitely many integer-power subtractions of S; the remaining polynomial Wronskian equation cannot be constant. Arbitrary lower-v-degree corrections are covered. Apply the criterion before solving corrections.
lessons.avoid: Assuming that generic order three, minimum inverse-Fourier rank or an explicit branch projector supplies a full carrier. Do not extend a no-mate conclusion to proper-power H or different top infinity faces.
lessons.boundary: The theorem fixes v-leading degree one and requires primitive root multiplicities; the leading polynomial may have multiple roots if their gcd is one. It is a scalar finite-order theorem, not a theorem about all matrix or nonpositional carriers. The candidate v*(2+h*a^3)+4a-3r*a^2 passes rank and splitting tests at N6/r3 yet has no finite mate. Proper-power leading cancellation is a genuine boundary of this proof, without an accompanying positive Long construction. QVL1 transports repeated roots to nonlinear ordinary infinity limits and closes all proper-power v-linear repairs when lower coefficients are bounded. Together with QVM1, every leading H of degree>=2 is excluded in that entire Laurent class, with arbitrary finite partner order and algebraic coefficient covers. Euler limits and finite Newton support certificates give further tests. A remaining exact-R scalar Long model in the v-linear rational Laurent class has H degree<=1 and inverse-Fourier rank at least four, by QSO2 and a positive infinity Newton contribution. The family 2v*(1+h*a)^k+4a-3ra^2 is excluded for every k>=2, even though k3 passes N6/r3 and branch extraction. Nonlinear-limit commuting Darboux algebras cannot supply a scalar generator, but other operators in larger idealizers remain outside that assertion. Other leading faces, fractional positive lower growth for nonprimitive H, H degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. QZM1 gives a zero-mode cokernel test with finite-cover trace retraction and covariance under actual finite algebra automorphisms, provided the module is transported too. A new position localization can kill the vector and is not justified by trace. It excludes v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a) for every nonconstant polynomial G and every finite scalar mate order or algebraic coefficient cover. Combined with QVL1, the pure separable class v*H(a)+G(a) with both H and G nonconstant is closed; the leading-linear rank-four cubic and derivative-tuned cubic are excluded. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant nonlinear-G case by a universal p-power coefficient. The complete pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long form is therefore excluded, including every finite momentum degree and coefficient cover. Additional negative-v corrections, genuine mixed coefficients, other leading faces and deformed first images remain outside this classification. Conditional global pair transport clears c(R) and requires [R,T]=0; it neither admits every chart formula nor identifies QRF2 with this new class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. Scalar p-centrality requires central degree p and fails for general phase matrices; no arbitrary carrier exclusion follows. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified.
lessons.reopen_when: A candidate leaves the complete v-linear bounded-lower exclusion, passes the other transported infinity tests and has an actual full action, or a bounded-carrier-specific theorem controls every remaining face. A proper-power H alone no longer reopens the natural Laurent class after QVL1.

lessons.title: Preserve arbitrary root monodromy through a regular polynomial parameter before treating nonabelian class action as an escape
lessons.when: A stable hypersurface embedding carries a Keller base through observables whose generic divisor-class action descends from a finite cover of one polynomial target parameter, including general constant-coefficient Danielewski equations.
lessons.use: A nowhere-critical polynomial cannot be a nonlinear composition. The explicitly imported classical closed-polynomial theorem and the written denominator-clearing step make its one-variable function field relatively algebraically closed in the source field. Finite parameter covers remain linearly disjoint, preserving their full possibly nonabelian group. A source component class fixed by the source stabilizer is then fixed by the whole action, and its principal orbit sum in a torsion-free group makes it zero. Apply the retained global filtered denominator and smooth label arguments. All nonconstant P(z), including S3 examples, and arbitrary two-variable T*Y suspensions close. HC4MYHY0/1 now close normal finite monogenic root covers and every monic two-parameter Danielewski output by root transitivity; HC4MYHY2 imposes a global nonmonogenicity gate on every nontrivial finite Keller normalization. HC4MYHZ0/1/2 supply the finite leading-fibre gate and independent abelian-root gate for nonmonic outputs, with exact localized-unit defect. HC4MYIA0/1/2 upgrade the unconditional nonmonic gate to finite nilpotent root/class groups and arbitrary common-prime radical depth. HC4MYIB0/1/2 add arbitrary Galois-intermediate exclusion, the exact global normalization-boundary basis, and subnormal class-stabilizer closure beyond nilpotent actions. HC4MYIC0/1/2 add combined leading-order factor divisibility, rational-label critical-curve geometry and new unrestricted-parameter S3 cubic closures. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons.avoid: Turning generic parameter regularity into irreducibility of every special fibre, coordinate status, properness or Keller invertibility by itself; assuming arbitrary two-variable monodromy descends from one parameter; claiming the classical closed-polynomial theorem was reproved; omitting affine height-one geometric integrality or torsion-freeness; confusing suspended and unsuspended T-dependent coefficients.
lessons.boundary: The nonabelian boundary is now narrower: HC4MYHX0/1 prove that a nowhere-critical polynomial parameter is relatively algebraically closed in the source field, using an explicit classical closed-polynomial import. A class action descending from a finite cover of that one parameter retains its full possibly nonabelian group under Keller base change, so the component classes become principal. This does not make all special parameter fibres irreducible or the whole Keller extension trivial. HC4MYHX2 closes every constant-coefficient nonconstant Danielewski P(z), with arbitrary root group, and every suspended T*Y+xy-B(T,z) with arbitrary two-variable B and all degrees. The earlier nonabelian-P(z) and suspended-coefficient escape proposals are retired. Genuinely two-parameter unsuspended monodromy, torsion, nonintegral height-one fibres, other missing filtrations and both plane endpoints remain open. HC4MYHY0 now preserves irreducibility of every normal finite monogenic cover under Keller base change, in every dimension and degree. All conjugate constant cross-resultants and integral roots rule out inertia crossing; explicit purity and finite-cover comparison inputs make the quotient trivial. HC4MYHY1 closes every two-parameter P(T,z) with nonzero constant leading z coefficient: root transitivity, without full splitting-group preservation, makes the invariant root-divisor classes zero. HC4MYHY2 forbids a globally monogenic finite normalization for any nontrivial Keller intermediate field; a nonautomorphic plane normalization needs at least two additional global algebra generators. Generic primitive elements do not provide normal monogenic models. Nonconstant leading coefficients, nonnormal monic presentations, nonglobally-monogenic normal finite algebras, other embeddings and both plane endpoints remain open. HC4MYHZ0 computes the exact torsion-free localized-unit defect as the sum of the reduced full-fibre component lattices at the zeros of a(T). HC4MYHZ1 preserves normal monogenic root-cover irreducibility on that vertical open when just those finitely many full K1-fibres are irreducible. The remaining finite etale generic-affine-line quotient is a finite Galois parameter extension, eliminated using HC4MYHX0; the explicitly imported Riemann-Hurwitz formula proves the constant-field descent. HC4MYHZ2 consequently closes every nonmonic P(T,z) under that finite-fibre gate. Independently, abelian generic root monodromy closes all such P without the fibre hypothesis, including every z degree one or two and arbitrary translated powers a(T)*(z-b(T))^m+c(T). A remaining nonautomorphic realization in this family needs both nonabelian generic root monodromy and positive localized-unit defect at a leading-coefficient zero. Generic parameter regularity does not supply the finite-fibre hypothesis, and etale affine curve maps are not automatically finite. The audited Tian-Sun 2024 claims are excluded as proof inputs. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIA0 upgrades the cyclic obstruction to full preservation of every finite nilpotent Galois target group under Keller base change in every dimension: a proper source image lies below a normal cyclic prime quotient, which would give a forbidden intermediate field. HC4MYIA1 therefore permits finite nilpotent class monodromy in the filtered output criterion. HC4MYIA2 closes every nonmonic xy-P(T,z) with nilpotent generic root group without a special-fibre assumption, including arbitrary-depth common-prime radical compositions and every composition of arbitrary quadratics. The explicit nonmonic quartic T*(z^2-T)^2 has nonabelian D8 group and is newly closed even without K1=0 irreducible. The remaining branch in this full family needs both nonnilpotent generic root monodromy and positive localized-unit defect at a leading zero. Arbitrary solvable groups do not follow: an S3 order-two subgroup escapes all normal prime-index containers. General wreath embeddings are primary context, not an additional proof import; the restricted common-prime construction is proved directly. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIB0 now excludes every finite Galois intermediate target-field extension inside a complex Keller field, in every dimension and without a group restriction: a visible index-one place reaches all primes by Galois conjugacy, then explicit purity and finite-cover inputs force triviality. This does not assert arbitrary full splitting-group preservation. HC4MYIB1 identifies the finite plane normalization class group exactly as the free group on the omitted boundary divisors; a torsion or globally factorial normalization forces the inverse. Local factoriality alone is insufficient. HC4MYIB2 closes the filtered output criterion when divisor-class stabilizers are subnormal in an arbitrary finite class-action image; normal class stabilizers suffice even for nonnilpotent groups. The Hurwitz lattice gives an explicit nonnilpotent class-module certificate, without an asserted ambient realization. The S3 root-lattice order-two stabilizer is not subnormal and remains a genuine boundary. Within nonmonic xy-P(T,z), positive localized-unit defect and nonnilpotent monodromy remain necessary unless another retained gate closes the case. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC0 now constrains every source root-factor degree by m/gcd(m,q_1,...,q_k) when leading-drop coefficient orders lie above the single-slope chords; coprime combined orders give irreducibility and close the carried output in arbitrary z degree without a special-fibre or monodromy hypothesis. HC4MYIC1 clears a rational root to a polynomial label with an exact vertical-Jacobian identity. The constructed polynomial map omits its normalized critical curve, so the explicit qualitative Jelonek-Lason nonproperness input forces each critical component to have affine normalization A1. Independently a square-free leading coefficient dividing the next coefficient excludes rational roots. HC4MYIC2 consequently closes nonmonic cubics if a is square-free and divides b, or if the critical discriminant D=b^2-3ac has square-free part of degree at least two. This includes new S3 families with unbounded T degree and no special-fibre hypothesis. The remaining cubic branch requires a rational label, positive localized-unit defect, S3 group, D of square-free degree at most one, and failure of the independent no-pole gate; D=0 was already cyclic and closed. Critical and root discriminants are distinct, and no-rational-root is not irreducibility in arbitrary higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC1 also gives a quantitative critical-branch unit budget: if the normalized derivative Q_U has ell distinct rational roots over C(T), monicity puts them in C[T], and the corresponding polynomial labels u-beta_i(f) are localized source units with linearly independent classes modulo C(f)^*. Hence the exact localized-unit defect sum_(a(c)=0)(r_c-1) is at least ell. For a cubic with D=b^2-3ac a nonzero square, the two distinct rational critical roots force defect at least two. This counts rational critical roots, not every root after a parameter-field extension, and does not close the residual by itself. HC4MYID0 now gives precise allowed supports for all irreducible normalized critical factors over C(T), not only rational branches: H_i(f,u) can vanish only above leading levels with H_i(c,0)=0. Independence gives every subset rank inequality, so extra defect at an excluded level cannot help. An empty support, equivalently gcd(a,H_i(T,0))=1, excludes a rational root in every degree without a special-fibre hypothesis. HC4MYID1 closes cubic square-critical-discriminant outputs whenever gcd(a,b-H)=1 or gcd(a,b+H)=1, including arbitrary pure-power leading multiplicities with b nonzero at the sole leading zero and the explicit S3 family T^q*z^3+z^2-(2R+T^q*R^2)*z/3+d. No new external theorem is imported. A surviving square-discriminant cubic needs nonempty support for both branches and the subset defect budgets; when gcd(a,b)=1, two separate reducible full f-fibres are required. The two-level coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 passes this necessary support test and is not closed by it. No higher-degree irreducibility is inferred from no rational roots. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 adds a global singleton-support pencil obstruction: two reduced rational critical units, each supported at one leading level, force their polynomial critical branches to differ by a nonzero constant. Mutual divisibility modulo the reduced units and ordinary polynomial degrees prove this in arbitrary degrees. In the cubic case a square-free leading coefficient with at most two zeros and gcd(a,b)=1 makes the two populated critical units reduced by the valuation-two Jacobian identity. Thus a nonconstant square critical gap H closes the output even when the support gcd test passes. The old coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 is now closed. A new residual has a=T*(T-1), b=1-2T, c=4/3, H^2=1 and constant critical gap; it is not closed by this argument. Repeated leading multiplicities require a separate reducedness audit. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 further reduces the remaining two-simple-leading-level constant-critical-gap subclass, in all coefficient degrees, to the one fixed output model (T,xy-[T*(T-1)*z^3+(1-2T)*z^2+4*z/3]). The proof writes the affine parameter change, polynomial z shift, constant rescaling, target shear and their inverses, transporting closed embedding data and Keller invertibility in both directions. This is an output-data normal form; the fixed-model endpoint is closed by HC4MYID3, and any fixed quadratic potential must be transported literally rather than assuming Hessian invariance. Increasing coefficient degrees in this output subclass adds no new output-base geometry. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed constant-gap cubic output model. A rational root label gives reduced critical units and polynomial quotients p,q; their difference and the label give a dominant polynomial second chart (A,t). The cleared root equation forces that chart to omit the hyperbola A*(t+1)=3 except possibly one point. The explicit retained Jelonek-Lason nonproperness theorem forbids this, since a hyperbola has no nonconstant polynomial A1 parametrization. Therefore the fixed cubic stays irreducible under every plane Keller base change. Together with HC4MYID2 this closes all cubic outputs with square-free leading a having at most two zeros, gcd(a,b)=1 and nonzero square critical discriminant, in every coefficient and embedding degree. The constant-gap fixed model is retired; the output normal form still does not imply fixed-potential Hessian invariance. Nonsquare linear critical part, more leading levels, repeated-level reducedness and higher-degree factorization branches remain open, as do both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2. HC4MYIE0 now proves in every z degree m>=3 that any rational source root must have an actual intermediate pole 0<r<ord_c(a) at a multiple leading zero. Absence of such poles forces R=D^(m-2), polynomial quotients and a generically finite polynomial map from the original A2 to an integral cyclic derivative surface; the root equation makes it omit a Cstar boundary curve except finitely many points, forbidden by the retained Jelonek-Lason theorem. The integer coefficient pole spectrum excludes roots whenever only full poles are permitted; gcd(a,a_prime,b_(m-1))=1 suffices. HC4MYIE1 separately proves full arbitrary-degree irreducibility for balanced monic rescaling P=A^(m-1)z^m+sum A^(i-1)c_i z^i+d when its explicit finite monic surface is normal; every square-free A is allowed, and the triple gcd F,F_U,F_T at each repeated A zero gives the more general normality test. It explicitly imports Stacks 00SB,031S,07PF. HC4MYIE2 closes every cubic with square-free leading a of arbitrary degree, every cubic with gcd(a,b)=1, and every cubic with leading parameter degree at most two, without a critical-discriminant restriction or special-fibre assumption. This supersedes earlier residual wording concerning square-free-leading nonsquare-linear critical parts and additional square-free leading levels. Remaining cubic rational roots require actual intermediate poles at joint zeros of a,a_prime,b and failure of this normal monic rescaling and the other retained gates. No-rational-root is not full irreducibility in higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIF0 extends the obstruction to all factor patterns: for any Keller map in n>=2 dimensions, primitive source factors with pairwise coprime leading coefficients have constant cross-resultants. The target gcd(a,a_prime,b_(m-1))=1 guarantees that coprimality. At V=infinity all normalized-root differences have valuation -1/m, so every pair gives ell_i/d_i+ell_j/d_j=1/m with sum ell_i=0. This excludes three or more factors and two equal factors in arbitrary degree and dimension. HC4MYIF1 combines the plane rational-root gate to leave exactly two unequal factors 2<=d<e under that gcd. In particular all square-free-leading quartics of arbitrary parameter degree and all quartics with gcd(a,b_3)=1 close, without a critical-discriminant, root-group or special-fibre hypothesis. The full quartic conclusion uses the plane-only root gate. HC4MYIF2 proves for the surviving unequal pair R=lambda*a^(e(d-1))*D^(e-d), the exact degree divisor m(e-d)/gcd(de,m(e-d)) for [L:F], and an explicit integral zeta=a^ceil(e(d-1)/(e-d))*D generating a necessarily nonnormal finite monogenic order. Unequal-factor valuations remain consistent; generic primitive orders cannot be treated as normal. The remaining gcd-admitted high-degree cases have precisely two unequal factors of degrees at least two, subject to that field-degree and order obstruction; joint repeated-leading cases remain separate. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIG0 supplies an all-degree rational-parameter regularity test: every finite reduced pencil member must be nonconstant and square-free. At most one projective parameter point can have constant point form; Riemann-Hurwitz forces any nontrivial composition to give a forbidden constant finite member. A polynomial parameter also passes when all but one finite fibre are reduced and the exceptional multiplicity gcd is one. The proof explicitly imports Petravchuk-Iena Lemma 2(1) closedness/noncomposition equivalence and reuses projective Riemann-Hurwitz. HC4MYIG1 shows Keller pullback preserves these tests and the full group of every finite Galois cover of the resulting one-variable rational parameter field. It extends the filtered class-action criterion without deleting any affine pole fibres. Parameters include (V+B(U))/A(U) and Q(U)(V+B(U)) with arbitrary polynomial A,Q and arbitrary repeated zeros; critical points and critical lines are allowed. HC4MYIG2 closes every P=A(T)R(c(T)z+beta(T))+B(T) for arbitrary nonconstant constant-coefficient R and nonzero polynomial A,c, with beta,B polynomial, and every polynomial P=R(c(T)z+beta(T))/Q(T)+B(T) with nonzero polynomial Q,c. All parameter, source, z and embedding degrees and leading multiplicities are unrestricted, with no root-group restriction. This closes the S3 family T^(3k)(z^3+z)+B(T) despite its intermediate pole, and the full sparse family T^k z^m+z^(m-1)+B(T) despite previously allowed unequal higher factors. General coefficient variation, rational affine representations not meeting the stated polynomial or parameter tests, two unequal factors outside these new closures, other joint repeated-leading cases and other outputs remain open. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIG0 further admits a one-exception rational pencil with algebraically independent numerator and denominator and exceptional multiplicity gcd one; independence rules out every omitted point form. HC4MYIG1 therefore certifies q=Q(U)(V+B(U))/D(U) for arbitrary coprime nonzero polynomial Q,D and polynomial B. HC4MYIG2 upgrades the output closure to P=A(T)R(c(T)z+beta(T))+B(T) polynomial, with arbitrary nonzero rational A,c, rational beta and polynomial B. In particular every sparse a(T)z^m+b(T)z^(m-1)+d(T), a nonzero, closes fully in all degrees without any gcd or leading multiplicity restriction. This removes both unequal-factor and common-repeated-leading residuals for that sparse family. General coefficient variation and rational output translations lacking a parameter certificate remain open; both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIH0 now permits several exceptional projective pencil values: for independent coprime numerator and denominator, require a multiplicity-one factor in each exceptional member and a bound M_lambda for its largest multiplicity. If sigma=sum(1-1/M_lambda)<2, every composition degree is excluded by the per-fibre bound (d-1)(1-1/M_lambda) and Riemann-Hurwitz. Keller pullback preserves the exact multiplicities and hence full finite parameter-cover monodromy. Equality is not closed: an explicit independent-numerator cubic rational example has four double-plus-simple members and sigma=2. The four numerical equality lists and d=1 modulo each M are necessary only. HC4MYIH1 computes all exceptional values of (Q(T)V+C(T))/D(T) from content gcds when D is nonconstant square-free. Its finite members always have a primitive horizontal factor of multiplicity one. HC4MYIH2 closes P=D[R(beta+Hz)-R(beta)]/H^2+B whenever H,D are nonconstant square-free coprime, H divides R_prime(beta), and the zeros of H select at most three critical values of constant-coefficient R. All source, coefficient, embedding and z degrees are unrestricted, with leading D H^(m-2) and repeated H levels in m>=4. This includes an explicit family for every m>=3 and a mixed-three-critical-value quartic failing the older leading gcd. The proof adds no new external theorem or orbifold classification. Coefficient profiles at or above the bound, missing simple factors, uncertified denominator members and other output geometries remain open. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYII0 now identifies every ramified divisorial curve of any plane Keller intermediate field as a polynomially parametrizable nonproperness component; other unramified sheets may remain visible. HC4MYII1 consequently makes every rational affine-in-V parameter (Q V+C)/D regular under plane Keller pullback, with only Q,D nonzero and triple gcd one: primitive horizontal branch curves leave at most one finite composition branch value, and Riemann-Hurwitz plus valuation one exclude the remaining power map. No multiplicity or denominator restriction remains in this plane parameter class. HC4MYII2 closes every final-polynomial rational affine fixed-polynomial output A R(cz+beta)+B0, now with rational B0. HC4MYII3 places the normal subgroup of actual nonparametrizable-curve inertia inside every source group; transitivity gives irreducibility, while a separately preserved quotient, including any nilpotent quotient, gives the full group. This closes (T-c0)^r z^m+z^q+d(T) for every r>=1 and 1<=q<m, since its non-axis critical curves lie in a torus and the residual quotient is abelian. HC4MYII4 completes every cubic output with all coefficient and leading degrees unrestricted: square and zero critical discriminants use II2, while a linear critical double cover forces integral critical values, polynomial cube scaling and a monic Jacobian contradiction. Full splitting-group preservation is not asserted for all cubics. These are plane-only strengthenings; earlier all-dimensional strict multiplicity tests and their equality counterexample remain valid. General higher-degree coefficient variation outside the field/inertia certificates and other output geometries remain open. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIJ0 extends the full-group gate to a relative central series over any separately preserved quotient, using the absence of Galois intermediate fields to descend the series. HC4MYIJ1 preserves every finite cover etale on an actual product U times Y when the finite geometric fibre image is nilpotent: commuting product monodromy makes it relatively central, and an algebraic section plus newly used full faithfulness of Milne Theorem 3.4 identifies the residual field with a genuine parameter cover. Both statements work in all Keller dimensions; the parameter quotient may be nonnilpotent. Essential surjectivity is not used and old forward-only imports remain unchanged. HC4MYIJ2 combines this with plane bad inertia, replacing the former nilpotent residual-group restriction by a punctured-cylinder or certified product-cover quotient. HC4MYIJ3 closes a(T)z^m+b(T)z^q+d(T) whenever a,b are nonzero, 1<=q<m and b^m/a^q has a finite pole, equivalently a^q does not divide b^m. The reduced critical-value curve U V^(m-q)=W has a nonconstant unit U(T), so no component admits polynomial A1 parametrization; the residual branch support is vertical coefficient levels plus V=0. This proves full group preservation, irreducibility and every carried stable plane inverse, without any coefficient, leading-multiplicity or degree bound. In particular every a(T)z^m+z^q+d(T) closes for arbitrary nonzero a, and varying shared-zero coefficients a=T^(m+1),b=T close for every m>=2 and 1<=q<m. The binomial bad-inertia application is plane-only. No-finite-pole binomials require another certificate; their failure of this test is not a nonclosure or Keller-realization claim. Nonproduct residual arrangements and nonnilpotent geometric fibre images remain distinct. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 now close the entire plane polynomial output coefficient class. HC4MYIK0 extends normal monogenic irreducibility preservation over a finite algebraic parameter curve: the actual source is smooth and finite free over the original polynomial source, and its cross-resultant units have nonzero constant norms. Integrality of every conjugate monic model makes both the target resultant and its inverse integral; inertia, purity and algebraic section descent finish the proof without assuming constant units or an affine-plane parameter source. HC4MYIK1 admits every integral algebraic affine monic model in all dimensions, and combines the no-pole binomial side with IJ3 to complete all plane binomials. HC4MYIK2 directly proves that integral critical values force integral centered monic coefficients in every degree and every residue-characteristic-zero valuation; no dynamical reduction theorem is imported. HC4MYIK3 uses contained plane bad inertia and its normal-orbit block system. Ordinary one-variable Luroth plus a unique-pole argument gives a polynomial outer block quotient. Its surviving critical curves are polynomially parametrizable, so every outer critical value is integral. IK2/1 make the source outer action transitive, and the contained bad inertia then makes the whole root action transitive. lessons.title: Bound finite monodromy by a selected normalization tube and meridian centralizer before resolving finite contacts
lessons.when: A chosen target branch-image component has immersive normalization and cyclic zero-excess finite factors; its normal bundle on the simultaneous target infinity model has positive degree. Other branch images may have cusps or nonabelian local monodromy.
lessons.use: Construct the compact normalization neighborhood from Nori, retaining q:V->X locally holomorphic invertible. Its normal degree is eta=Cbar^2-2delta; WLT(C) bounds the complement subgroup index by Cbar^2/eta. Decompose the whole tube into its punctured oriented normal bundle and local pieces. In the actual finite cover each selected cyclic sheet cluster is separate from the others, so their local images centralize the selected meridian even if those other local groups are nonabelian. Thus the tube image lies in C_G(sigma), and(b-1)eta<=2delta for b the actual conjugacy size. Apply one component at a time; positivity and zero excess are not needed on every other image. In S_d use the exact cycle-profile formula and binomial(d,2) for a single fold. Before identifying G, a single fold already has exact conjugacy size d(m-1)/2, where m divides d and is the common orbit size of the normal transposition subgroup. This gives d<=2+4delta/eta, its least-prime-divisor refinement, and forces G=S_d in prime field degree.
lessons.avoid: Using the singular image neighborhood instead of the immersed normalization neighborhood; substituting Proposition3.26 despite a removed divisor meeting Cbar; discarding infinity loops; assuming tube monodromy abelian rather than merely centralizing the selected meridian; replacing the simultaneous target compactification by isolated-component data; resolving finite tangencies and paying unnecessary contact losses before using the finite monodromy; assuming every inertia is noncentral, or that noncyclic monodromy on unrelated sheets invalidates a selected cyclic-factor estimate.
lessons.boundary: PF2RULED47 is an all-degree, all-index selected-support inequality with eta>0 and actual conjugacy size; a single fold also gives the explicit unknown-monodromy field-degree bound d<=2+4delta/eta. It strengthens the quartic budget to a_n<=1+min(2T,floor(2(k+T)/5)), without closing that packet. In the retained degree-six gap21 problem, an immersive degree(3,5) second image in rows A,C,N has delta4 and conjugacy size15/40, so the exact infinity normal degree forces contact>=34 without finite tangency, singular-avoidance or nodality assumptions. Contacts34,38,40, a nonimmersive second image and arbitrary second-image degrees remain open. 120 exact controls support a written primary-imported proof; eta<=0, full exclusions, formal verification, independent full reproof, external review and priority remain unclaimed.
lessons.reopen_when: For positive normal degree use the finite conjugacy inequality before any new incidence or coefficient search. For eta<=0 compare several components on one actual target infinity model or seek genuinely new finite-algebra/peripheral information. Do not try to rescue the now-excluded immersive quintic contacts20..32 by finite tangencies. Retain arbitrary other image degrees and the three surviving quintic contacts.

lessons.title: Use normal monogenic covers and all conjugate cross-resultants before reopening two-parameter output monodromy
lessons.when: A proposed output realization has a monic normal finite root cover, or a finite Keller normalization is claimed to have one global integral generator.
lessons.use: Etale Keller base change preserves normality. A proper monic factorization has polynomial source coefficients and disjoint component sets, so its cross-resultant is a nonzero scalar. Every conjugate root cut has that constant resultant. Integral roots prevent inertia from crossing any cut, and the normal core quotient is finite etale by the explicit primary ramification/purity inputs, hence trivial over complex affine space. This preserves root irreducibility, enough to close all monic P(T,z) through the invariant root lattice. A normal monogenic Keller intermediate normalization would supply an irreducible equation with a source root, forcing degree one. lessons.title: Use intrinsic monodromy limits and free torsor bases before finite self-map searches
lessons.when: Extending universal finite etale maps to one fixed source geometry, promoting varying norm tori, or adding canonical volume preservation.
lessons.use: Use intrinsic translation lattices and holonomy for finite torus-quotient maps, free torsor bases and the cohomological isogeny criterion for specified-group realizations, and the semilinear class equation for the complete prime-power spectrum. UA1RIGIDCYL1 removes finite affine coupling; UACYLDICH1 forces every nonfinite self-atomic cylinder map to have base degree one, and UACYLCAN1 returns its marked data to an affine fibre. UACANFIB1 constructs a different nonfinite canonical receiver on genuine affine-space fibres, with explicit non-atomicity and all subgroup fixed restrictions. UAPARALLEL1 closes arbitrary polynomial profiles in all retained first outputs: every block subset has a polynomial factor even with cycles. UAWEILATOM1 gives exact ground-field stable length from the field-component count of A after the chosen base extension. The one-direction joint theorem remains complete. UAMULTIKER1 extends the exact common kernel C[Z] to every return rank. UABASICTIME1 factors selectors proved to lie in C[Z,t], even for nonlinear time Keller maps and cyclic nilpotent matrices. UAMARKEDDEF1 preserves the complete marked restrictions by vanishing ideals in a retained first output, giving atomic auxiliary maps of every generic degree d>=3 and preserving any prescribed finite-order thickening and canonical receiver deformations which still factor. UARETURNESC1 gives actual non-descended rank-two and full-rank escapes from the old cubic factor; full canonical atomicity still needs a separate proof. UAROOTDAG1 closes arbitrary polynomial corrections in all retained signals and source roots X_i=x_i*q_i: Keller forces the exact self equation and an effective DAG. UAROOTFACT1 gives polynomial order-ideal models and absolute stable atomic block stages even for some genuinely non-descended rank-two selectors. UAROOTSYM1 groups these into equivariant orbit factors; a transitive action on all blocks has complete fixed-target fibre T0^N and cannot give the natural N-label cover. UASELFCTRL1 closes one affine coefficient line with arbitrary own-source polynomial controls, and even rational controls if the WHOLE output map extends polynomially: only retained-signal effective profiles survive. UASELFLAUR1 supplies the exact nonlinear response and reciprocal-Riccati/pole proof. UASELFFORMAL1 provides all-order formal marked deformations and a genuine source denominator as the concrete next integration gate. UANATIVE2GEN1 replaces every finite native list by two unique effective source controls without changing the map. UAAFFINER1 closes all one-block affine-r controls and gives a fixed-size determinant equation for the nonlinear remainder. UASIGFIELD1 identifies stable signal-field normalizers as weighted compiler scalings plus vertical Keller maps. UAETALEGAUGE1 says the marked finite/formal examples are unique source coordinate changes, with necessarily unbounded source degrees in the explicit scalar family. UAQFSAT1 supplies polynomial descent for any dominant quasi-finite affine-space self-map. UANATIVEORBIT1 classifies the full native profile-coordinate orbit: affine Cout, generic affine-pair reducibility and signal-field-respecting stable profile equivalence all give the unique shear ideal (a^5*c^3). Its finite polynomial-r degree reduction closes the whole quadratic sector. UACUBICDESC1 tests an actual old cubic factor by reducing each output to its three fixed field-basis coefficients; no target-degree ansatz is needed. UAPROFFACT1 upgrades the native profile orbit to complete rational factor rigidity: recovery through ANY retained profile forces its unique target shear, by the already imported published HC4MYGL0 line theorem. UARPLANE1 converts the nonnegative-r generic leaf sector to an actual plane completion with Jacobian 1-SY. UAPLANEATOM1 makes every such completion plane-indecomposable and excludes signal-retaining whole factors whose intermediate coordinates also extend across its hyperbola. UARELPLANE1 cancels a plane Keller target whenever the final curve is a closed embedding, with no boundary-extension hypothesis. UASIGFACT1 closes EVERY native signal-retaining whole factorization, including negative Laurent-r sectors. UAINTERSURF1 replaces the former pole gate by the exact generic intermediate surface under arbitrary stabilization mixing: noninvertible target stages require a NON-PLANE fibre with the stated smooth complete-intersection, tangent, curve, unit, divisor and saturation constraints. UAPRIMUNIT1 closes the cofinite etale surface class with primitive source unit. UAUNITFACT1 uses published whole polynomial root closure to make every nonconstant geometric unit primitive and invert the source stage. A proper arbitrary stabilized native intermediate is therefore GEOMETRICALLY UNIT-FREE and non-plane, has arithmetic UFD ring and an all-irreducible-constant-fibre whole signal component. At every chain cut the unit lattice is either full Z or zero, dropping once at the first noninvertible prefix. UALOGVOL1 closes all nonnegative-logarithmic intermediates after a noninvertible source stage, by the actual r^2 whole-volume multiplier and log pullback on boundary resolutions. UAGEOPIC1 then forces NONZERO geometric Picard group for proper native factors, while its retained-field Galois invariant subgroup is ZERO by rational-point-normalized descent. UADANVOL1 excludes every ordinary smooth Danielewski exponent-one surface by a volume period; higher exponents have an explicit regular primitive. UAPLANECHART1 tests the ENTIRE carried line against EVERY open A2 chart: containment in any one inverts the whole target. Formal etaleness still makes all its finite/formal neighborhoods standard. UADANCHART1 exposes exact simultaneous Keller gluing on the classical Danielewski atlas, a JC(2)-level burden, nondividing ruling degrees and multi-root contact constraints. Its sharp beta-integral contact family fails geometric injectivity in every exponent. UAARITHRULING1 turns ANY actually descended affine-line ruling into a finite geometric plane atlas: arithmetic fibres are integral and geometric fibres reduced. A proper native factor would give JC(2) counterexamples and its whole curve must hit two components of one split fibre. UAPRODUCTTOPO1 uses source Euler characteristic1 and pi1=Z^N on actual product leaves to exclude finite proper stages and force a finite-index abelian intermediate subgroup with index dividing source degree. lessons.boundary: The finite geometric torus-quotient obstructions use characteristic zero; explicit tame integral models have their own good-characteristic range. All prime powers occur strongly in finite torus-quotient geometry. Nonfinite self-atomic degrees on Gm times A3 are all integers at least3, but this does not produce canonical symmetric actions. The canonical trace receiver supplies those actions in another geometry and pays with a nontrivial factorization. These classifications use characteristic-zero polynomial retained-signal profiles and the named compiler. Any number of controls with rank-one cubic return is closed; non-descended higher-rank return and other compilers are separate. For another auxiliary block rank-one output recovery is equivalent to geometric generic-line connectedness; no general closedness conjecture is silently assumed. Arithmetic atomicity of connected input algebras is not absolute atomicity. Common kernels are proved for all constant ranks; the full selector classification is only one-directional. Higher-rank membership in C[Z,t] is an explicit hypothesis, not a determinant consequence. The full C is not assumed finitely generated or polynomial. Marked divisor identities hold universally; effective degree and absolute atomicity use the stated characteristic-zero field hypotheses. Fixed-signal rank-two source leaves need not be affine planes. A slice does not imply local nilpotence, and stable polynomiality is not an atomicity converse. The root-feedback theorem requires characteristic-zero fields, unchanged first signals and corrections in k[u,sigma,X]. Independent r_i diagonal variables force every principal minor to vanish. Frobenius dependencies and nilpotent coefficient cycles show why positive characteristic and nonreduced bases are excluded. Transitive product-fibre conclusions require transitivity on ALL nonidentity blocks; the trace filter has an extra auxiliary orbit and changes its first signal. Scalar self-feedback rigidity is a one-block affine coefficient-line theorem with a nonzero effective direction in characteristic zero. It permits all own-source channels and rational controls with whole polynomial landing, but says only that EFFECTIVE profiles are retained-signal polynomials; common direction factors may cancel a rational signal control. Curved coefficient families and mutually changing blocks remain outside. Finite-order parameter bases are nonreduced; the formal ring k[P][[lambda]] permits unbounded source degrees and differs from k[[lambda]][P]. The two-control module identity is universal over bases with2 invertible and preserves arbitrary source dependence. Affine-r rigidity and the stable signal-field normalizer use characteristic-zero fields. Affine-r rigidity is a one-block theorem with actual identity parameters and native source jets, not a theorem about mutually changing blocks. Formal-etale source gauges are classical and work over arbitrary nilpotent base ideals; their compatible formal limit can have unbounded source degree. The source-field normalizer leaves a vertical JC(m) problem and does not classify merely retained-output maps or arbitrary coordinate changes moving that field. Formal marked source equivalence permits actual polynomial families with arbitrary generic-degree jumps; it is not a global degree or stable-class invariant. Native orbit rigidity requires characteristic zero, one retained block, polynomial module membership and coordinate operations fixing identity parameters. Its stable equivalence is restricted to source maps normalizing k(u,sigma); unrestricted source changes are outside. The profile-factor theorem is one block with retained identities and a literal profile first factor; arbitrary source changes remain outside. Plane completion is generic in the signal and covers only nonnegative r powers. Plane indecomposability requires an irreducible Jacobian and an embedded line; its extension to all fields requires GEOMETRIC irreducibility. It does not imply stable whole-map atomicity. A nontrivial signal-retaining factor must have a genuine intermediate boundary pole. Whole-source special-signal landing and signal-moving factors remain open. Intermediate surfaces satisfy BOTH saturation identities, geometrically have unit rank at most1 and their etale arrows miss at most finitely many points. Their abstract shape, smoothness and tangent triviality do not construct a proper factor. The affine-type descent subproblem is closed; extend by a new identification argument, not more necessary conditions.

lessons.title: Transport repeated momentum roots to infinity limits before accepting proper-power repairs
lessons.when: A proper-power leading polynomial is proposed to evade the primitive infinity criterion, a higher-order scalar mate is sought, or a rational Darboux/bispectral construction is proposed as a full carrier.
lessons.use: Apply an algebraic position change and momentum shift and compute the full operator coefficient limits. A nonlinear ordinary infinity limit has no finite scalar Weyl mate of any order or algebraic coefficient cover; an Euler infinity limit excludes every nonconstant limit. Repeated roots close all proper powers for v*H(a)+bounded-lower S0. Together with QVM1 this rejects every deg H>=2 in the natural v-linear Laurent class. A finite Newton support certificate can handle positive intermediate powers, with complete falling-factorial ordering at the Euler boundary. In the exact-R full scalar Long category a remaining H degree<=1 forces a growing Newton branch and inverse rank at least four. Rational commuting Darboux operators with nonlinear limits are excluded as generators as well.
lessons.avoid: Treating a repeated root as an automatic escape, omitting internal ordering at the Euler face, applying an ordinary infinity theorem when the new coordinate tends to a finite point, treating a rational momentum inverse as a finite operator, or inferring full carrier existence from bispectrality or commuting differential actions.
lessons.boundary: The complete v-linear conclusion requires every lower coefficient exponent<=0; QVM1 alone covers primitive H with fractional lower exponents<1. The tested generic root shift can have h poles and is not a regular formal comparison. Other infinity faces, H of degree<=1 and nonpositional first images remain open. The rank>=4 refinement uses exact-R scalar reduction and the rational Laurent class. The Darboux conclusion excludes one whole commuting algebra, not every member of a larger idealizer or every projective/matrix carrier. A formal mate of E+hE^2 exists with unbounded momentum, and an exact proper-power pair on another face is a positive control. QZM1 gives a zero-mode cokernel test with finite-cover trace retraction and covariance under actual finite algebra automorphisms, provided the module is transported too. A new position localization can kill the vector and is not justified by trace. It excludes v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a) for every nonconstant polynomial G and every finite scalar mate order or algebraic coefficient cover. Combined with QVL1, the pure separable class v*H(a)+G(a) with both H and G nonconstant is closed; the leading-linear rank-four cubic and derivative-tuned cubic are excluded. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant nonlinear-G case by a universal p-power coefficient. The complete pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long form is therefore excluded, including every finite momentum degree and coefficient cover. Additional negative-v corrections, genuine mixed coefficients, other leading faces and deformed first images remain outside this classification. Conditional global pair transport clears c(R) and requires [R,T]=0; it neither admits every chart formula nor identifies QRF2 with this new class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. Scalar p-centrality requires central degree p and fails for general phase matrices; no arbitrary carrier exclusion follows. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved.

lessons.title: Test finite leading fibres and abelian root monodromy before reopening nonmonic outputs
lessons.when: A nonmonic xy-P(T,z) output or a vertically localized normal monogenic Keller intermediate cover is proposed.
lessons.use: Compute the exact source localized-unit lattice. Irreducible full K1-fibres at leading zeros make every resultant unit descend to the target parameter. All conjugate cuts then force inertia into a normal core outside those zeros. A genuine finite generic-affine-line cover is a parameter extension by Riemann-Hurwitz, and regularity of the Keller component eliminates its quotient. Root transitivity closes the divisor lattice. Independently abelian root monodromy closes the same global filtered output without a special-fibre assumption. HC4MYIA0/1/2 upgrade the unconditional nonmonic gate to finite nilpotent root/class groups and arbitrary common-prime radical depth. HC4MYIB0/1/2 add arbitrary Galois-intermediate exclusion, the exact global normalization-boundary basis, and subnormal class-stabilizer closure beyond nilpotent actions. HC4MYIC0/1/2 add combined leading-order factor divisibility, rational-label critical-curve geometry and new unrestricted-parameter S3 cubic closures. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons.avoid: Assuming every fixed Keller-component fibre is irreducible; confusing generic regularity with localized-unit descent; silently changing the fixed target coordinate; inferring affine finiteness from etaleness; using the excluded Tian-Sun shortcut; upgrading root transitivity to full splitting-group preservation.
lessons.boundary: HC4MYHZ0 computes the exact torsion-free localized-unit defect as the sum of the reduced full-fibre component lattices at the zeros of a(T). HC4MYHZ1 preserves normal monogenic root-cover irreducibility on that vertical open when just those finitely many full K1-fibres are irreducible. The remaining finite etale generic-affine-line quotient is a finite Galois parameter extension, eliminated using HC4MYHX0; the explicitly imported Riemann-Hurwitz formula proves the constant-field descent. HC4MYHZ2 consequently closes every nonmonic P(T,z) under that finite-fibre gate. Independently, abelian generic root monodromy closes all such P without the fibre hypothesis, including every z degree one or two and arbitrary translated powers a(T)*(z-b(T))^m+c(T). A remaining nonautomorphic realization in this family needs both nonabelian generic root monodromy and positive localized-unit defect at a leading-coefficient zero. Generic parameter regularity does not supply the finite-fibre hypothesis, and etale affine curve maps are not automatically finite. The audited Tian-Sun 2024 claims are excluded as proof inputs. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIA0 upgrades the cyclic obstruction to full preservation of every finite nilpotent Galois target group under Keller base change in every dimension: a proper source image lies below a normal cyclic prime quotient, which would give a forbidden intermediate field. HC4MYIA1 therefore permits finite nilpotent class monodromy in the filtered output criterion. HC4MYIA2 closes every nonmonic xy-P(T,z) with nilpotent generic root group without a special-fibre assumption, including arbitrary-depth common-prime radical compositions and every composition of arbitrary quadratics. The explicit nonmonic quartic T*(z^2-T)^2 has nonabelian D8 group and is newly closed even without K1=0 irreducible. The remaining branch in this full family needs both nonnilpotent generic root monodromy and positive localized-unit defect at a leading zero. Arbitrary solvable groups do not follow: an S3 order-two subgroup escapes all normal prime-index containers. General wreath embeddings are primary context, not an additional proof import; the restricted common-prime construction is proved directly. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIB0 now excludes every finite Galois intermediate target-field extension inside a complex Keller field, in every dimension and without a group restriction: a visible index-one place reaches all primes by Galois conjugacy, then explicit purity and finite-cover inputs force triviality. This does not assert arbitrary full splitting-group preservation. HC4MYIB1 identifies the finite plane normalization class group exactly as the free group on the omitted boundary divisors; a torsion or globally factorial normalization forces the inverse. Local factoriality alone is insufficient. HC4MYIB2 closes the filtered output criterion when divisor-class stabilizers are subnormal in an arbitrary finite class-action image; normal class stabilizers suffice even for nonnilpotent groups. lessons.title: Use exact quadratic elimination and a zero-quartic frame branch for repeated leading lines
lessons.when: A ternary cubic has a repeated leading factor and its lower Gaussian terms are arbitrary.
lessons.use: Split the repeated linear form by isotropy. A nonisotropic factor leaves two purely quadratic transverse variables; eliminate them over C(t), retaining every determinant prefactor. Its identically zero quartic coefficient is an algebraic frame condition, so treat that branch by W-linear GMC safety. Otherwise split the symmetric2-by-2 matrix into invertible, semisimple rank1, nilpotent rank1 and zero. For an isotropic factor separate zero W^2 from generic-t W/T completion. Keep the full one-variable degree, all bounded and escaping dimensions, scalar actions and shrinking widths. This completes the leading-type cover and makes the sharp cubic mixed bound global.
lessons.avoid: Using null-coordinate quadratic elimination as a conditional t-adic Gaussian average at t=0; dropping a determinant prefactor; inferring the complete analytic period exclusion from a Hessian or a bounded Wick check; conflating the frame-plus888 certificate with888 alone; or promoting the normalized five-term quartic ansatz minimum to a global term minimum.

lessons.title: Transport the zero mode cokernel and use trace before enlarging coefficient covers
lessons.when: A candidate operator has an algebraic hyperexponential zero mode after an Ore shift, a missing Weyl action is sought, or an actual obstruction is being transported through canonical changes.
lessons.use: Compute the vector-space cokernel class [be] in V/LV with Le=0. A commutator [L,T]=b makes it exact. Normalized differential field trace retracts every finite algebraic coefficient extension, so a nonzero rational class survives all such covers. Carry the actual module under finite algebra automorphisms and identity stabilization. For S=v*(lambda*a+mu)+G(a), a root shift gives a zero mode and an all-degree rational pole/degree obstruction whenever G is nonconstant. QPC1 subsequently closes the H-constant case too, completing the pure separable polynomial Long exclusion. Clear c(R) denominators and retain [R,T]=0 for a conditional global pair certificate.
lessons.avoid: Holding the coefficient-function module fixed after Fourier transformation, discarding the supported zero mode by a new localization, treating the class as determined only by the classical symbol, identifying it with QRF2 without a comparison theorem, or applying linear trace descent to nonlinear correction equations or bounded support conditions.
lessons.boundary: The pure polynomial G theorem does not include arbitrary negative-v corrections. QPC1 closes the H-constant higher-degree polynomial family; genuinely mixed coefficients and deformed nonpositional first images remain open. Abstract covariance requires an actual algebra automorphism and an actual module; a classical Poisson change alone is insufficient. The global pair application assumes admission and a valid rational chart, and a root shift with h poles is not regular formal normalization. Self-Ext vanishing is necessary, not a complete finite-mate or full-carrier criterion. Matrix candidates need their own nonzero represented class. QPC1 also gives linear trace descent for a fixed operator mate and the necessary matrix-fiber condition chi_S derivative zero. Scalar p-centrality requires central degree p and fails for general phase matrices; no arbitrary carrier exclusion follows. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QSC1 proves Cent_classical(R,S)=K[R,S] and commutativity of the full formal joint centralizer for every commuting Long deformation, including nonpositional first images. Faithful finite/corner and QMC1 full-carrier endomorphism algebras inherit commutativity. Global spectral Koszul classes exactly test the two individual conjugates; if they vanish, one algebraic curvature class exactly tests flat completion. All spectral fibers can pass while the global class fails, and a formally exact curvature can have nonzero rational double residue. If both matrix positions are scalar, normalized matrix trace scalarizes a full completion without degree growth. This does not scalarize genuinely matrix-valued positions or free a projective carrier, identify QRF2, or construct a finite Long lift. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved.

lessons.use: Build a fixed finite target ideal, then test every target generator in each prefix radical using inverse-variable unit-ideal certificates. A proven equality of target and all-order zero sets plus finite support of ideal expressions supplies termination. Once a sufficient prefix is found, monotonicity gives the least one. Insufficient tests give algebraic points and eventual later nonzero moments. For ternary cubics, replace existential null directions by the8-by16 binary-quartic multiplication matrix and its degree8 maximal minors, retaining projective endpoints.
