lessons.reopen_when: A finite target description is unavailable or fails review, coefficient constraints are not effectively presented algebraically, positive characteristic is requested, or a numerical/complexity/scheme-theoretic bound is required.

lessons.title: Use normal quotients and the exact boundary class basis before reopening nonnilpotent output monodromy
lessons.when: A finite Keller intermediate field is Galois, a finite normalization is claimed factorial, or a nonnilpotent output class action has manageable class stabilizers.
lessons.use: Every target divisor has a visible source place of ramification index one. In a Galois intermediate normalization this reaches every prime over that divisor, including missing places; explicit purity and finite-cover rigidity force degree one. In the full plane normalization, source factoriality gives boundary generation and source constant units give independence, so the missing divisors are an exact free global class basis. A subnormal class stabilizer in the output action lies in a proper normal subgroup unless it is the whole group, yielding a forbidden Galois intermediate field. This closes some nonnilpotent class representations. HC4MYIC0/1/2 add combined leading-order factor divisibility, rational-label critical-curve geometry and new unrestricted-parameter S3 cubic closures. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons.avoid: Propagating one unramified place without Galois normality; inferring arbitrary full target-group preservation from the absence of Galois intermediate fields; confusing local factoriality with global class group zero; identifying normalization and ambient generic class groups; treating a nonabelian stabilizer as normal without evidence; claiming a Hurwitz-module ambient realization.
lessons.boundary: HC4MYIB0 now excludes every finite Galois intermediate target-field extension inside a complex Keller field, in every dimension and without a group restriction: a visible index-one place reaches all primes by Galois conjugacy, then explicit purity and finite-cover inputs force triviality. This does not assert arbitrary full splitting-group preservation. HC4MYIB1 identifies the finite plane normalization class group exactly as the free group on the omitted boundary divisors; a torsion or globally factorial normalization forces the inverse. Local factoriality alone is insufficient. HC4MYIB2 closes the filtered output criterion when divisor-class stabilizers are subnormal in an arbitrary finite class-action image; normal class stabilizers suffice even for nonnilpotent groups. The Hurwitz lattice gives an explicit nonnilpotent class-module certificate, without an asserted ambient realization. The S3 root-lattice order-two stabilizer is not subnormal and remains a genuine boundary. Within nonmonic xy-P(T,z), positive localized-unit defect and nonnilpotent monodromy remain necessary unless another retained gate closes the case. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC0 now constrains every source root-factor degree by m/gcd(m,q_1,...,q_k) when leading-drop coefficient orders lie above the single-slope chords; coprime combined orders give irreducibility and close the carried output in arbitrary z degree without a special-fibre or monodromy hypothesis. HC4MYIC1 clears a rational root to a polynomial label with an exact vertical-Jacobian identity. The constructed polynomial map omits its normalized critical curve, so the explicit qualitative Jelonek-Lason nonproperness input forces each critical component to have affine normalization A1. Independently a square-free leading coefficient dividing the next coefficient excludes rational roots. HC4MYIC2 consequently closes nonmonic cubics if a is square-free and divides b, or if the critical discriminant D=b^2-3ac has square-free part of degree at least two. This includes new S3 families with unbounded T degree and no special-fibre hypothesis. The remaining cubic branch requires a rational label, positive localized-unit defect, S3 group, D of square-free degree at most one, and failure of the independent no-pole gate; D=0 was already cyclic and closed. Critical and root discriminants are distinct, and no-rational-root is not irreducibility in arbitrary higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC1 also gives a quantitative critical-branch unit budget: if the normalized derivative Q_U has ell distinct rational roots over C(T), monicity puts them in C[T], and the corresponding polynomial labels u-beta_i(f) are localized source units with linearly independent classes modulo C(f)^*. Hence the exact localized-unit defect sum_(a(c)=0)(r_c-1) is at least ell. For a cubic with D=b^2-3ac a nonzero square, the two distinct rational critical roots force defect at least two. This counts rational critical roots, not every root after a parameter-field extension, and does not close the residual by itself. HC4MYID0 now gives precise allowed supports for all irreducible normalized critical factors over C(T), not only rational branches: H_i(f,u) can vanish only above leading levels with H_i(c,0)=0. Independence gives every subset rank inequality, so extra defect at an excluded level cannot help. An empty support, equivalently gcd(a,H_i(T,0))=1, excludes a rational root in every degree without a special-fibre hypothesis. HC4MYID1 closes cubic square-critical-discriminant outputs whenever gcd(a,b-H)=1 or gcd(a,b+H)=1, including arbitrary pure-power leading multiplicities with b nonzero at the sole leading zero and the explicit S3 family T^q*z^3+z^2-(2R+T^q*R^2)*z/3+d. No new external theorem is imported. A surviving square-discriminant cubic needs nonempty support for both branches and the subset defect budgets; when gcd(a,b)=1, two separate reducible full f-fibres are required. The two-level coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 passes this necessary support test and is not closed by it. No higher-degree irreducibility is inferred from no rational roots. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 adds a global singleton-support pencil obstruction: two reduced rational critical units, each supported at one leading level, force their polynomial critical branches to differ by a nonzero constant. Mutual divisibility modulo the reduced units and ordinary polynomial degrees prove this in arbitrary degrees. In the cubic case a square-free leading coefficient with at most two zeros and gcd(a,b)=1 makes the two populated critical units reduced by the valuation-two Jacobian identity. Thus a nonconstant square critical gap H closes the output even when the support gcd test passes. The old coefficient control T*(T-1)*z^3+z^2-4*z/3 is now closed. A new residual has a=T*(T-1), b=1-2T, c=4/3, H^2=1 and constant critical gap; it is not closed by this argument. Repeated leading multiplicities require a separate reducedness audit. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYID2 further reduces the remaining two-simple-leading-level constant-critical-gap subclass, in all coefficient degrees, to the one fixed output model (T,xy-[T*(T-1)*z^3+(1-2T)*z^2+4*z/3]). The proof writes the affine parameter change, polynomial z shift, constant rescaling, target shear and their inverses, transporting closed embedding data and Keller invertibility in both directions. This is an output-data normal form; the fixed-model endpoint is closed by HC4MYID3, and any fixed quadratic potential must be transported literally rather than assuming Hessian invariance. Increasing coefficient degrees in this output subclass adds no new output-base geometry. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed constant-gap cubic output model. A rational root label gives reduced critical units and polynomial quotients p,q; their difference and the label give a dominant polynomial second chart (A,t). The cleared root equation forces that chart to omit the hyperbola A*(t+1)=3 except possibly one point. The explicit retained Jelonek-Lason nonproperness theorem forbids this, since a hyperbola has no nonconstant polynomial A1 parametrization. Therefore the fixed cubic stays irreducible under every plane Keller base change. Together with HC4MYID2 this closes all cubic outputs with square-free leading a having at most two zeros, gcd(a,b)=1 and nonzero square critical discriminant, in every coefficient and embedding degree. The constant-gap fixed model is retired; the output normal form still does not imply fixed-potential Hessian invariance. Nonsquare linear critical part, more leading levels, repeated-level reducedness and higher-degree factorization branches remain open, as do both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2. HC4MYIE0 now proves in every z degree m>=3 that any rational source root must have an actual intermediate pole 0<r<ord_c(a) at a multiple leading zero. Absence of such poles forces R=D^(m-2), polynomial quotients and a generically finite polynomial map from the original A2 to an integral cyclic derivative surface; the root equation makes it omit a Cstar boundary curve except finitely many points, forbidden by the retained Jelonek-Lason theorem. The integer coefficient pole spectrum excludes roots whenever only full poles are permitted; gcd(a,a_prime,b_(m-1))=1 suffices. HC4MYIE1 separately proves full arbitrary-degree irreducibility for balanced monic rescaling P=A^(m-1)z^m+sum A^(i-1)c_i z^i+d when its explicit finite monic surface is normal; every square-free A is allowed, and the triple gcd F,F_U,F_T at each repeated A zero gives the more general normality test. It explicitly imports Stacks 00SB,031S,07PF. HC4MYIE2 closes every cubic with square-free leading a of arbitrary degree, every cubic with gcd(a,b)=1, and every cubic with leading parameter degree at most two, without a critical-discriminant restriction or special-fibre assumption. This supersedes earlier residual wording concerning square-free-leading nonsquare-linear critical parts and additional square-free leading levels. Remaining cubic rational roots require actual intermediate poles at joint zeros of a,a_prime,b and failure of this normal monic rescaling and the other retained gates. No-rational-root is not full irreducibility in higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIF0 extends the obstruction to all factor patterns: for any Keller map in n>=2 dimensions, primitive source factors with pairwise coprime leading coefficients have constant cross-resultants. The target gcd(a,a_prime,b_(m-1))=1 guarantees that coprimality. At V=infinity all normalized-root differences have valuation -1/m, so every pair gives ell_i/d_i+ell_j/d_j=1/m with sum ell_i=0. This excludes three or more factors and two equal factors in arbitrary degree and dimension. HC4MYIF1 combines the plane rational-root gate to leave exactly two unequal factors 2<=d<e under that gcd. In particular all square-free-leading quartics of arbitrary parameter degree and all quartics with gcd(a,b_3)=1 close, without a critical-discriminant, root-group or special-fibre hypothesis. The full quartic conclusion uses the plane-only root gate. HC4MYIF2 proves for the surviving unequal pair R=lambda*a^(e(d-1))*D^(e-d), the exact degree divisor m(e-d)/gcd(de,m(e-d)) for [L:F], and an explicit integral zeta=a^ceil(e(d-1)/(e-d))*D generating a necessarily nonnormal finite monogenic order. Unequal-factor valuations remain consistent; generic primitive orders cannot be treated as normal. The remaining gcd-admitted high-degree cases have precisely two unequal factors of degrees at least two, subject to that field-degree and order obstruction; joint repeated-leading cases remain separate. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIG0 supplies an all-degree rational-parameter regularity test: every finite reduced pencil member must be nonconstant and square-free. At most one projective parameter point can have constant point form; Riemann-Hurwitz forces any nontrivial composition to give a forbidden constant finite member. A polynomial parameter also passes when all but one finite fibre are reduced and the exceptional multiplicity gcd is one. The proof explicitly imports Petravchuk-Iena Lemma 2(1) closedness/noncomposition equivalence and reuses projective Riemann-Hurwitz. HC4MYIG1 shows Keller pullback preserves these tests and the full group of every finite Galois cover of the resulting one-variable rational parameter field. It extends the filtered class-action criterion without deleting any affine pole fibres. Parameters include (V+B(U))/A(U) and Q(U)(V+B(U)) with arbitrary polynomial A,Q and arbitrary repeated zeros; critical points and critical lines are allowed. HC4MYIG2 closes every P=A(T)R(c(T)z+beta(T))+B(T) for arbitrary nonconstant constant-coefficient R and nonzero polynomial A,c, with beta,B polynomial, and every polynomial P=R(c(T)z+beta(T))/Q(T)+B(T) with nonzero polynomial Q,c. All parameter, source, z and embedding degrees and leading multiplicities are unrestricted, with no root-group restriction. This closes the S3 family T^(3k)(z^3+z)+B(T) despite its intermediate pole, and the full sparse family T^k z^m+z^(m-1)+B(T) despite previously allowed unequal higher factors. General coefficient variation, rational affine representations not meeting the stated polynomial or parameter tests, two unequal factors outside these new closures, other joint repeated-leading cases and other outputs remain open. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIG0 further admits a one-exception rational pencil with algebraically independent numerator and denominator and exceptional multiplicity gcd one; independence rules out every omitted point form. lessons.title: Trace a fixed mate to the base field and test its p-power before constructing it
lessons.when: A fixed finite scalar operator is being tested for a Weyl mate, including partners on finite algebraic coefficient covers, or a relative finite matrix fiber is available.
lessons.use: For a fixed base operator S, normalized coefficient field trace retracts the linear commutator equation, eliminating finite algebraic covers. In a characteristic-p central algebra of degree p, a mate forces S^p central. Isolate a noncentral normal-order coefficient using word weights before computing the full power. For G(a)+mu*v on [a,v]=h/v, the two-v coefficient is universally (n^2-1)/(24n)*g_n^(p-2)*mu^2*h^(p+1) at v^-2p*a^((n-1)p-2n-1), for p>2n+1. Good reduction excludes every finite mate in characteristic zero. Combined with QVL1 and QZM1 this closes the entire pure polynomial v*H(a)+G(a) Long ansatz. For a general finite matrix fiber, use chi_S derivative zero as the necessary condition.
lessons.avoid: Bounding the unknown partner order, treating h-small leading coefficients as zero in the generic field, prescribing a Frobenius center map without proof, using normalized trace for idempotents or a nonlinear unknown tuple, or requiring scalar S^p in an arbitrary higher-dimensional matrix fiber.
lessons.boundary: The central-degree-p argument is relative rank one. Arbitrary m*p matrices require only chi_S(z)=f(z^p); QPH1 at p7 has nonscalar S^7 despite an exact Weyl mate. The complete classification concerns pure polynomial H,G and permits arbitrary partner poles and finite covers; it does not include arbitrary additional negative-v or genuinely mixed coefficients. The classification does not place every finite Long carrier in that form. New localization, nonpositional first images, global admission, a full right action and finite-left generation remain separate. QAD1 supplies an arbitrary-scalar mixed-coefficient admission test: nonzero Adler periods exclude even bounded-above PDO mates, whereas finite differential existence is exactly constant-linear membership in the full almost-commuting defect span. It identifies a characteristic-zero residue proportional to QPC1 gamma_n. Vanishing periods construct only a PDO mate, as the harmonic control demonstrates; neither an h-pole dressing nor a finite defect prefix supplies a finite full carrier. This does not compare arbitrary Fourier completions, identify QRF2 or cover nonscalar matrix actions. The finite leading-divisor gate is stronger than the first PDO period test: if gcd(operator order, all leading-coefficient zero/pole orders)=1, the entire base low-order commutator image is zero by finite power subtraction. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. A passing leading condition remains necessary, and nonscalar matrix carriers are not classified. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual surviving operator has genuinely different mixed coefficients or a different leading face, a new coefficient can be proved nonzero for an entire carrier class, or a complete full matrix/projective model passes the characteristic-polynomial and global finite-lattice tests.

lessons.title: Use combined leading orders and omitted critical-curve geometry before reopening nonmonic factors
lessons.when: A nonmonic root polynomial factors after Keller base change, or a cubic S3 output is proposed beyond the nilpotent and finite-fibre gates.
lessons.use: Single-slope leading drops constrain each factor degree by root valuations; combining all chosen levels can force transitivity without a monodromy hypothesis. A rational root clears to an integral polynomial label, whose exact Jacobian identity forces an auxiliary polynomial map to omit its normalized critical curve. The explicit qualitative nonproperness theorem makes that curve polynomially parametrizable. Cubic critical curves reduce to Y^2=b^2-3ac, giving a square-free-degree test; an independent square-free-leading no-pole criterion closes complementary cases. HC4MYID0/1 refine critical units to factor-specific supports and all subset rank budgets, closing a new square-discriminant S3 family with arbitrary leading multiplicity. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. HC4MYIM0/1/2/3 add parameter-extension irreducibility, moving-row invariant vanishing, an exact content-fibre criterion and uniform adapted global frames. The IM3 determinant-one parameter matrix covers moving B, multivariable monic-leading b and arbitrary affine root terms, with a separate primitive-content check. The IM3 frame admits every strict joint degree-gap remainder; its univariate leading-divisibility corollary allows all lower P coefficients. HC4MYIN0/1 replace the former global-frame requirement by rank-two reflexive pencil descent and close every primitive disjoint moving suspension. HC4MYIO0/1/2 extend to arbitrary independent coefficient fields and overlapping polynomial directions; monic and polynomial-Bezout leading overlap outputs have uniform generic filtrations. HC4MYIP0/1/2 use moved relative additive actions instead of positive generic filtrations, and force every surviving overlap image into the multiplier-variable invariant subring. HC4MYIQ0/1/2 descend any univariate generic helper, close every one-helper admitted overlap including nonprimitive content, and reduce HC4 survivors to two-helper invariant plane curves. HC4MYIR0/1/2 close multiplier-zero images in all helper counts and every admitted two-helper overlap in every stable dimension; the complete admitted HC4 overlap family is now closed. IS0/1/2 identify the full JC2 content of an unconditional residual-free extension, including an exact source-correlated class lattice and actual unit-Hessian embeddings with an always invertible constructed gradient. IT0/1/2 give intrinsic finite-energy and inverse-Hessian certificates and a mixed three-direction criterion before any ambient output construction. IU0/1/2 exploit actual free projections and the zero-section first jet, closing critical-value traces and testing the global immersion obligation in a universal noncritical construction. IV0/1/2 separate complete compensation identities from codimension-one source recovery and provide a canonical Legendre-hypersurface normality gate. IW0/1/2 close every constant trace through an infinite-order integral middle-cycle obstruction, with arbitrary helper degrees. IX0/1/2 separate arbitrary quadric plane classes from actual radical-curve recovery and close coordinate-composite or smooth/nonparametric descended nonconstant traces. IY0/1/2 close contractible full-preimage curves and descended cusps, and impose the exact generic-pencil boundary-defect certificate on the remaining multibranch cases. IZ0/1/2 match the intrinsic generic genus on all one-place zero curves and close every rank-one descended trace, including all internally multibranch cases and positive-power rational descent. JA0/1/2 force the actual disjoint extra-prime/unit/boundary configuration and bound its one-place part; scalar extra units close the selected one-place case.
lessons.avoid: Assuming source factors are integral at a leading zero; overlooking cooperation of several noncoprime leading orders; calling a rational root polynomial before checking denominators; using ordinary rationality rather than affine-line normalization; confusing critical and root discriminants; inferring higher-degree irreducibility from no rational roots; treating the imported nonproperness theorem as reproved.
lessons.boundary: HC4MYIC0 now constrains every source root-factor degree by m/gcd(m,q_1,...,q_k) when leading-drop coefficient orders lie above the single-slope chords; coprime combined orders give irreducibility and close the carried output in arbitrary z degree without a special-fibre or monodromy hypothesis. HC4MYIC1 clears a rational root to a polynomial label with an exact vertical-Jacobian identity. The constructed polynomial map omits its normalized critical curve, so the explicit qualitative Jelonek-Lason nonproperness input forces each critical component to have affine normalization A1. Independently a square-free leading coefficient dividing the next coefficient excludes rational roots. HC4MYIC2 consequently closes nonmonic cubics if a is square-free and divides b, or if the critical discriminant D=b^2-3ac has square-free part of degree at least two. This includes new S3 families with unbounded T degree and no special-fibre hypothesis. The remaining cubic branch requires a rational label, positive localized-unit defect, S3 group, D of square-free degree at most one, and failure of the independent no-pole gate; D=0 was already cyclic and closed. Critical and root discriminants are distinct, and no-rational-root is not irreducibility in arbitrary higher degree. Both plane endpoints and unrestricted HC4/JC2 remain open. HC4MYIC1 also gives a quantitative critical-branch unit budget: if the normalized derivative Q_U has ell distinct rational roots over C(T), monicity puts them in C[T], and the corresponding polynomial labels u-beta_i(f) are localized source units with linearly independent classes modulo C(f)^*. Hence the exact localized-unit defect sum_(a(c)=0)(r_c-1) is at least ell. For a cubic with D=b^2-3ac a nonzero square, the two distinct rational critical roots force defect at least two. This counts rational critical roots, not every root after a parameter-field extension, and does not close the residual by itself. HC4MYID0 now gives precise allowed supports for all irreducible normalized critical factors over C(T), not only rational branches: H_i(f,u) can vanish only above leading levels with H_i(c,0)=0. Independence gives every subset rank inequality, so extra defect at an excluded level cannot help. An empty support, equivalently gcd(a,H_i(T,0))=1, excludes a rational root in every degree without a special-fibre hypothesis. HC4MYID1 closes cubic square-critical-discriminant outputs whenever gcd(a,b-H)=1 or gcd(a,b+H)=1, including arbitrary pure-power leading multiplicities with b nonzero at the sole leading zero and the explicit S3 family T^q*z^3+z^2-(2R+T^q*R^2)*z/3+d. lessons.title: Localize each critical-factor unit at its permitted leading levels and enforce every subset rank budget
lessons.when: A rational source label survives the geometric critical-curve and global unit-rank tests, especially a cubic with square critical discriminant.
lessons.use: Normalize the label, factor Q_U over C(T) into distinct monic H_i, and compute the supports S_i={a=0,H_i(T,0)=0}. The root equation and derivative have only zero as a possible common root at a leading level. Therefore each critical-factor unit has precisely this allowed support. Their independence modulo C(f)^* gives every subset rank inequality. Empty support excludes a rational root. For cubics the factors are linear when D=H^2, giving the coefficient gcd test and new arbitrary-leading-multiplicity S3 closures. HC4MYID2 closes reduced singleton critical units with nonconstant separation, including the cubic two-simple-leading-level case. HC4MYID3 closes the fixed cubic by a polynomial second chart omitting a hyperbola and consequently the entire specified two-simple-level square-critical class. HC4MYIE0/1/2 supply the intermediate-pole necessity, cyclic derivative surface, normal monic rescaling and unrestricted square-free-leading cubic closure. HC4MYIF0/1/2 constrain every source factorization, close square-free-leading quartics and supply a field-degree and nonnormal-order obstruction for the remaining unequal pair. HC4MYIG0/1/2 add reduced-pencil rational monodromy, one-exception polynomial parameters and all-degree scaled and reciprocal-scaled one-variable output closures. The same mechanism now closes rational scalings and rational affine input with polynomial output translation, including all sparse two-positive-term outputs without a gcd condition. HC4MYIH0/1/2 add the strict projective multiplicity bound, exact affine-in-V exception certificate and all-degree mixed-critical-value expansion outputs. HC4MYII0/1/2/3/4 add plane intermediate-branch geometry, unrestricted rational affine parameters, actual-inertia quotient certificates, all nonadjacent pure-power binomials and every cubic output. HC4MYIJ0/1/2/3 add relative central-series descent, actual product-cover preservation with arbitrary parameter monodromy, and the all-degree finite-critical-pole binomial certificate. HC4MYIK0/1/2/3 add parameter-cover unit norms, integral algebraic monic models, a direct critical-value valuation lemma and unrestricted plane polynomial-output closure. HC4MYIL0/1/2 add generative factor transfer, exact fixed-multiplier class lattices and all-degree multivariable suspension closure with full global filtration. lessons.title: Check leading divisor multiplicities and Adler periods before finite admission
lessons.when: A finite scalar operator with arbitrary mixed coefficients is being tested for a missing Weyl action, or a pseudodifferential dressing is proposed as a finite carrier.
lessons.use: First test g=gcd(operator order, zero and pole orders of the leading coefficient). g=1 makes the whole low-order commutator image zero, regardless of lower mixed terms. Trace fixed mates to the base curve before this test. At prime order on K(v), require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. Then test the exact leading dual differential; in the quadratic chart it is the rational equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v. Trace fixed mates down from finite coefficient covers. Normalize the leading root algebraically, then test exactness of its dual differential and the Adler classes [res R^j*omega]. A nonzero class forbids even a bounded-above PDO mate. For finite differential existence, use the exact established criterion kappa in the finite constant-linear span of [S,(R^j)_+]. Seek a structural annihilator of the whole defect span, rather than an order prefix. The period of (G(a)+mu*v)^(2+1/n), after monic normalization, is -(2n+1)*(n^2-1)/(24*n^2)*(mu/g_n)^2*h^2, giving a characteristic-zero residue behind QPC1.
lessons.avoid: Inferring a finite differential mate from vanishing of every period, accepting an infinite negative PDO tail as a finite carrier, treating a finite defect prefix as all-order exclusion, replacing the constant-linear span by a function-field span, or calling the established Adler/almost-commuting basis machinery a new theorem of priority.
lessons.boundary: The harmonic oscillator passes the entire positive period hierarchy but has no finite differential mate. Period vanishing plus exact leading differential constructs only a PDO mate; its dressing can have h poles. Algebraic first-order generator changes and invertible PDO conjugations preserve the residue, but arbitrary Fourier changes require a completion comparison. The method is scalar and does not normalize all deformed first images or nonscalar matrix carriers. A full Long model still needs all relations, the correct graph, global admission and finite-left generation. This excludes every nonconstant squarefree polynomial leading coefficient, with arbitrary mixed lower terms and all finite coefficient covers. Prime operator orders over K(v) require a scalar times an nth power leading coefficient. The separate rational leading PDO equation Qprime-(Hprime/(n*H))*Q=v tests algebraic primitive exactness; its squarefree degree>=3 exclusion strengthens to PDO mates. lessons.title: Use prime leading classes and pole degrees, retaining partial fibre cancellations
lessons.when: A bounded-degree completion of r=x+x^2y reaches new prime z-degrees or leading common powers.
lessons.use: Reduce mate degrees overK(u)[z] to show a prime-z component has prime-power leading class. For monic53 use the unique smooth infinity point of its invariant cubic and potential pole7. For monic54 retain both first integrals and classify all rational coefficient poles; each gives a differential pole>=3. For quartic/quadratic common factors inspect h=0 andx=0 separately. Multiplying byx powers can clear thex component without clearing the full fibre, so first infer onlyh-divisibility and recover anyx-divisibility from the remaining normal-form equations.
lessons.avoid: Inferring r|t from polynomiality ofx^3*t/r; extending degree7 case bookkeeping without new prime/pole and common-power lemmas; treating a coefficient identity as formal verification of the universal proof.

lessons.title: Use the full grouped Schur budget, actual graded affine controls and the primitive monomial finite-map gate
lessons.when: A finite Keller normalization has several unramified pieces sharing a coordinate pencil complementary to an index-two prime, or affine exact-volume conditions are being mistaken for a finite-map obstruction.
lessons.use: Group the full primitive matrix by boundary values. Distinct-value unramified blocks have zero cross pairing. Normalize each block by pole orders and take its inverse energy E; the strict Schur budget n_R/q^2>sum E and E>=1 force one value except r2q1, which allows at most two. For simple pole2 primes use E=2m/(m+1), retaining every same-value cross term. Test any proposed affine-only obstruction against the explicit smooth B_n family with arbitrarily many D_i. If a primitive source monomial is globally regular and every boundary prime is vertical at finite values, use finite generic C* fibres and the fixed-origin Keller differential to prove primitive-element status before using the full norm family.
lessons.avoid: Dropping same-value matrix cross terms; conflating a bound on coordinate values with an unconditional bound on components; treating finite matrix tests as universal proofs; inferring a finite Keller map or target action from smooth affine exact-volume models; assuming the integral primitive element generates the normal algebra; declaring a curve complete after testing only two selected infinity charts.
lessons.boundary: PF2RULED51 gives all-degree value and conditional all-simple-D count bounds. The smooth graded affine family realizes every component count in the r2q1 one-value sector but supplies no Keller pair. The primitive monomial/norm gate requires the ACTUAL finite map, global regularity and all-boundary verticality. 180 controls support written proofs; full exclusion and independent review remain open.
lessons.reopen_when: Apply the full finite target algebra, the norm-family specializations and marked target topology to the actual common or minimal complementary models. Keep all source ends and all omitted primes. A universal affine-only component-count obstruction cannot survive the explicit B_n controls.

lessons.title: Use Reynolds projection and independent invariants to obstruct short pure-moment prefixes
lessons.when: A classified pure-null locus consists of positive-weight orthogonal orbits, and exact polynomial invariants have a nonzero Jacobian minor.
lessons.use: Prove every positive-degree invariant vanishes on the all-order pure-null locus. If r initial invariant moment equations forced that locus, Nullstellensatz followed by the invariant-linear Reynolds projection would make the invariant-ring quotient finite dimensional. Graded induction then makes the invariant ring finite over the algebra generated by those r moments, contradicting r+1 independent invariants. Exploit parity to convert nine/six even equations into19/13 initial zero moments. Use a retained finite upper and a nonvanishing inverse variable to obtain Qbar points.
lessons.avoid: Using ambient null-locus dimension as the quotient dimension; assuming the displayed invariants generate the ring; inferring a system of parameters or sufficiency from a truncated Hilbert numerator; asserting a specific next moment is nonzero; describing existence as displayed coefficients; importing standard-copy Reynolds algorithms for a symmetric-cubic representation.

lessons.title: Test global spectral translations and algebraic curvature before matrix padding
lessons.when: A commuting Long quantum pair in a finite operator algebra or a faithful projective carrier is to be completed, or a matrix repair keeps both position images scalar.
lessons.use: Use the all-deformation commutative joint centralizer proved from Cent(R,S)=K[R,S]. Work in the actual algebra E. The two global spectral Koszul classes (h,0),(0,h) test individual conjugates; if they vanish, the choice-independent curvature class lies in B/(delta1 B+delta2 B) and exactly tests the remaining mixed relation. Seek a nonzero global class or a finite primitive in that actual centralizer. For scalar matrix positions, normalized trace of a flat matrix pair is already a flat scalar pair, with no degree increase. For a projective carrier this scalarization is in its endomorphism algebra and does not supply a Weyl free frame.
lessons.avoid: Using pointwise or generic spectral vanishing to infer the global translation class, replacing the actual centralizer by its completed polynomial algebra, treating a completed curvature primitive as algebraic, tracing arbitrary nonlinear matrix tuples when the positions are nonscalar or the joint centralizer is noncommutative, or assuming a partial module has a faithful formal frame without separatedness/rank evidence.
lessons.boundary: The classical joint-centralizer theorem and formal induction cover every commuting Long deformation, including nonpositional first images. The finite carrier extension requires a faithful embedding, supplied by QMC1 rank-one torsion-freeness for full carriers or directly by finite projective corners. No finite Long pair with both individual conjugates is constructed. A twisted Ore boundary with double residue one proves completed curvature exactness is insufficient but is not a finite Weyl example. Actual algebra isomorphisms transport the classes; a classical Poisson change alone does not. The old QRF2 residue and the related Hochschild classes are not identified with these classes. QST1 separates rational and spectral admission. Any nonzero Adler period excludes the entire rational operator division ring and makes the universal spectral class nontorsion; the G(a)+mu*v first period is explicit in all degrees. This blocks every rational conjugate and the corresponding actual rank-one projective pair orbit without a scalar free frame. Fixed rational mate equations descend through finite algebraic coefficient covers by monic-denominator Galois averaging. Constant-coefficient G has instead a critical-value torsion annihilator and a rational mate. Zero Adler periods are insufficient for rational admission: a torus residue excludes harmonic/Euler functional classes even with arbitrary operator denominators and identity spectators. Finite primitive-divisor and ordinary infinity exclusions must not be silently promoted to rational ones. No arbitrary moving spectral coefficient localization, nonlinear Galois descent or universal Long rational normalization is proved. QFC1 closes algebraic curvature exactness under actual centralizer module finiteness, even if only the generic centralizer is module-finite. Integral individual mates and the polynomial classical centralizer yield an integral polynomial primitive in every rank, h-small for a flat classical tuple. Independent Bernstein leading symbols with a full module-finite Poisson centralizer supply a scalar filtered certificate. The required Long input has not been constructed. QET1 can decide the translation/completion route from the actual centralizer field. With finite generation, actual individual mates make it etale. Scalar Weyl units and a birational field force finite flat completion; a nontrivial Galois field makes simultaneous individual mates impossible. Non-Galois degree at least three and fixed sheets for all generic inertia generators remain possible. This does not compute a Long centralizer or its global translation classes. QET1 also removes actual parameter poles under the polynomial classical centralizer hypothesis, with no finite-generation or field-degree assumption: individual mates have unique finite polynomial polar parts. Subtraction preserves any integral curvature exactly, so an actual generic flat tuple with regular positions descends to a finite integral flat tuple and can match a prescribed classical flat frame. Only h is inverted; rational spatial/operator denominators and arbitrary completed series remain outside this descent. QTB1 provides all-partner tests without finite generation of the actual centralizer. A nontrivial finite Galois factor or actual new radical in its fraction field forbids simultaneous individual mates; birationality makes the centralizer polynomial and permits finite completion. The radical certificate uses two actual commutants, a cleared polynomial identity and a certified nonpower. No actual Long certificate is produced. QPD1 proves nonzero annihilator of each global translation class iff a rational individual mate exists, by clearing a finite adjoint orbit with a spectral polynomial. It applies to rank-one finite projective Weyl orders. Zero classes remain the actual-mate criterion; nonzero torsion can coexist with no actual mate. Full rational and actual curvature tests remain separate. QCI1 shows that even a polynomial actual joint centralizer and a flat completion retain a nontrivial residual division cover for Long. After adjoining the full rational position centralizer the residual indices are at least3. No ambient rational target automorphism, even with h poles, can make the fixed positions ordinary rational coordinate functions. Mixed source polarizations remain outside this statement. QCI1 adds a finite-carrier test before the actual spectral complex is available: a rational matrix Weyl generator with uniformly bounded Bernstein powers cannot preserve a finite full left lattice of any rank. Its exact rational degree-m Weyl pairs demonstrate why rational full relations alone do not supply an actual finite algebra in which the zero-class criterion can be applied.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual candidate lattice and commuting position pair admit computable global translation classes, a structural theorem proves algebraic curvature exactness for its centralizer, or a genuinely matrix-valued/projective model passes all classes and global admission with a finite frame where required.

lessons.title: Use invariant differentials to obstruct stable conjugacy identity factors
lessons.when: A tangent-to-identity map is to be reduced in active dimension by polynomial or formal conjugacy, possibly after adding identity variables.
lessons.use: WriteF=X+H2+H3+... . The first two invariant-function equations areell(H2)=0 andell(H3)+sumH2_i*d_i(h2)=0. Compute the kernel of the quadratic output coefficient matrix and a coefficient functional annihilating the homogeneous-quadratic Lie image. If it detects every remaining linear-jet cubic direction, all invariant differentials vanish. After identity stabilization, project the cubic equation onto added variables0; this bounds the number of independent invariant coordinate differentials by exactly the number of added identity variables.
lessons.avoid: Interpreting a finite jet certificate as a degree cap on the invariant function; claiming all invariants are constant; claiming a global cubic dimension minimum from one stable conjugacy class; confusing unequal inverse-derivative target normalization with conjugacy.
lessons.boundary: KCUB25 has quadratic rank11/minor-288 and a four-term functional that annihilates all78 quadratic Lie derivatives and detects H3_5. Exact455 pullback and27 stabilization cross controls pass. The written formal argument gives a sharp12 active-variable bound only in the stable polynomial/formal conjugacy class of KCUB3, with arbitrary conjugacy degree. Other constructions and unequal left/right equivalences remain open. The97-centre experiment is separately finite and has best145, not a universal translation lower bound. KCUB26 also excludes nonlinear target maps of degree<=5 producing another cubic from an affine frame of the savedK, and arbitrary-degree polynomial/rational single-coordinate target changes in its displayed axes. Coordinated nonlinear source/target changes and targetdegree>=6 involving all outputs remain outside this result; global bounds and62/12 counts do not change.
lessons.reopen_when: Use unequal source/target transformations, changed constructions, or pursue term improvements at unchanged dimension. To apply the criterion to another map, recompute its actual low homogeneous parts and the complete obstruction on its surviving linear-jet kernel.

lessons.title: Reject source-symmetry descent at field level and use explicit escaping weight primitives instead
lessons.when: A Keller-boundary affine model has a source translation or diagonal C* action, or a proposed finite-map reduction assumes its target field/algebra is invariant under that action.
lessons.use: Prove K intersect C[x,y]=C[P,Q] by quasi-finite divisor domination. Translation- or Euler-derivation stability of K then gives stability of the target algebra. A repeated derivative or exact weight projector produces an element affine-linear on a source-coordinate line, and the imported one-line injectivity theorem forces an automorphism. Thus a nontrivial target FIELD must break the source action. On B_n, after affine jet normalization, P_1=xF(h) and Q_-2=yG(h) are regular but outside K; at least one Euler coordinate derivative is outside too. Under retained S_d monodromy there are no intermediate fields, so these outside elements are full-degree primitive choices. Keep their coupling, rational source-coordinate norms and trace-dual constraint in the actual finite algebra.
lessons.avoid: Inferring rational or regular target descent from a source action, finite morphism or invariant ramification divisor; equating algebra invariance with homogeneous chosen generators; using generic finiteness in the intersection lemma; extending immersion to line injectivity; calling every outside element primitive without excluding intermediate fields; treating trace-dual membership as integrality or rational norms as polynomial ones.
lessons.boundary: PF2RULED52 excludes every translation or nonzero integral diagonal Euler descent to a noninvertible Keller target field, in all source coordinates and field degrees. The B_n consequences require the actual finite normalization; primitive status of the escaping components uses no intermediate fields, supplied by the retained zero-excess S_d case. The source action remains actual geometry and the non-equivariant finite-map problem remains open. 116 controls support written proofs with imported one-line theorem; no independent reproof or full exclusion is claimed.
lessons.reopen_when: Use finite target algebra and marked topology without imposing source symmetry. Any target-invariance ansatz is already closed. The escaping weight components, monomial primitive, exact norm coupling and trace-dual module give necessary algebraic tests; none constructs a Keller map or proves universal exclusion.

lessons.title: Turn a numerical moment root into a certified isolated algebraic cubic witness
lessons.when: A square rational polynomial moment system has a numerical candidate with an invertible Jacobian and a desired later nonzero moment.
lessons.use: Normalize a tractable coefficient slice, find approximate roots with bounded seeded Newton iteration, and retain all candidates separately from proofs. Refine one root and store rational center/preconditioner data. Bound B*F at the center and I-B*J on a full complex polydisc with outward-rounded intervals. Prove strict contraction and self-mapping, then certify the next moment excludes zero. A full-rank gradient multiplication matrix proves smoothness without a discriminant expansion.
lessons.avoid: Accepting small floating residuals as exact zeros; using a midpoint inverse as an exact inverse; claiming a rectangular enclosure is a circular ball; inferring smoothness generically; confusing a finite-prefix obstruction with sufficiency; or claiming minimal polynomials from an isolated-root representation. Flint fmpq does not parse decimal strings: pass exact Fraction numerator/denominator, preserving the original parser failure.
